sec06-R04-card.front: When can an eligible fifteen-day temporary license be extended after a DUI arrest?
sec06-R04-card.expected_back: An eligible temporary license may be extended when the administrative hearing is requested.

sec06-R05-card.front: What three questions are examined during an administrative DUI hearing?
sec06-R05-card.expected_back: An administrative DUI hearing examines the officer’s probable cause, the evidence of impaired driving or control, and refusal after warning about revocation.

sec06-R06-card.front: How long is the revocation after an unfavorable administrative probable-cause ruling on a first offense?
sec06-R06-card.expected_back: An unfavorable probable-cause hearing ruling brings a three-month revocation for a first offense.

sec06-R07-card.front: How long is the revocation after an unfavorable probable-cause hearing ruling for a second offense?
sec06-R07-card.expected_back: An unfavorable probable-cause hearing ruling brings a twelve-month revocation for a second offense.

sec06-R08-card.front: What revocation length applies when an unfavorable probable-cause hearing ruling is a third or later offense?
sec06-R08-card.expected_back: An unfavorable probable-cause hearing ruling brings an eighteen-month revocation for a third or later offense.

sec06-R09-card.front: How long is the administrative revocation for losing a chemical-refusal hearing on a first offense?
sec06-R09-card.expected_back: An unfavorable chemical-refusal hearing ruling brings a twelve-month revocation for a first offense.

sec06-R10-card.front: How long is the administrative revocation after an unfavorable chemical-refusal ruling on a second offense?
sec06-R10-card.expected_back: An unfavorable chemical-refusal hearing ruling brings an eighteen-month revocation for a second offense.

sec06-R11-card.front: What revocation length applies to an unfavorable chemical-refusal ruling on a third or later offense?
sec06-R11-card.expected_back: An unfavorable chemical-refusal hearing ruling brings a twenty-four-month revocation for a third or later offense.

sec06-R12-card.front: What four requirements must be met to reinstate after a probable-cause or chemical-refusal revocation?
sec06-R12-card.expected_back: Reinstatement after a probable-cause or chemical-refusal revocation requires the designated alcohol-evaluation course or rehabilitation, payment of related fees, service of the revocation period and a two hundred dollars reinstatement fee.

sec06-R13-card.front: Which three driver examinations may be required before reinstating after probable-cause or refusal action?
sec06-R13-card.expected_back: Vision, knowledge and road-skills testing may be required before reinstatement following probable-cause or chemical-refusal action.

sec06-R14-card.front: How many months of license loss apply on a first DUI conviction involving drugs or BAC below zero point one five?
sec06-R14-card.expected_back: The first-DUI-offense table assigns twelve months of license loss for drugs or BAC below zero point one five.

sec06-R15-card.front: On a first DUI conviction, what license loss applies for a zero-point-one-five to zero-point-one-nine BAC?
sec06-R15-card.expected_back: The first-DUI-offense table assigns eighteen months of license loss for the BAC bracket labeled zero point one five through zero point one nine.

sec06-R16-card.front: How long is license loss on a first DUI conviction with BAC at least zero point two zero or test refusal?
sec06-R16-card.expected_back: The first-DUI-offense table assigns twenty-four months of license loss for BAC at least zero point two zero or chemical-test refusal.

sec06-R17-card.front: What fine range and maximum jail term appear in the court table for a first DUI offense?
sec06-R17-card.expected_back: For a first DUI offense, the court-sanctions table lists a five hundred dollars to one thousand five hundred dollars fine, imprisonment up to twelve months, or both.

sec06-R18-card.front: What restricted license option may someone entering First Offender Election instead of trial seek before revocation ends?
sec06-R18-card.expected_back: A person entering First Offender Election instead of trial may seek an IID license before the revocation period ends.

sec06-R19-card.front: When does IID application eligibility begin for FOE offenses dated February two, twenty fifteen or later?
sec06-R19-card.expected_back: For FOE violations dated February two, two thousand fifteen or later, immediate IID application eligibility remains subject to the program’s listed requirements.

sec06-R20-card.front: What four items and record conditions are required on an FOE ignition-interlock license application?
sec06-R20-card.expected_back: The FOE IID application requires surrender of the Delaware license, a completed application, proof of insurance and Delaware vehicle registration, and no other withdrawal that prevents IID licensing.

sec06-R21-card.front: What happens once an FOE participant satisfies the IID application requirements?
sec06-R21-card.expected_back: After FOE IID requirements are met, the DMV authorizes device installation on the approved vehicles.

sec06-R22-card.front: How long must an FOE participant stay in the IID program, and what date starts that clock?
sec06-R22-card.expected_back: A FOE participant with an IID license must remain in the IID program for four months starting on the IID license issue date.

sec06-R23-card.front: What must reach the DMV for FOE reinstatement and IID removal, and what exams might also apply?
sec06-R23-card.expected_back: FOE reinstatement requires DMV receipt of satisfactory alcohol-program completion and a two hundred dollars fee; vision, law and road tests may also be required before DMV authorizes IID removal.

sec06-R24-card.front: What must an FOE participant without a vehicle in their name do if they choose not to get an IID license?
sec06-R24-card.expected_back: A FOE participant without a vehicle in their name who chooses no IID license must serve the full revocation, refrain from driving and meet the remaining reinstatement requirements.

sec06-R25-card.front: On a second DUI conviction, what license loss applies for drugs or BAC under zero-point-one-five?
sec06-R25-card.expected_back: The second-DUI-offense table assigns eighteen months of license loss for drugs or BAC below zero point one five.

sec06-R26-card.front: On a second DUI conviction, what license loss applies for a zero-point-one-five to zero-point-one-nine BAC?
sec06-R26-card.expected_back: The second-DUI-offense table assigns twenty-four months of license loss for the BAC bracket labeled zero point one five through zero point one nine.

sec06-R27-card.front: On a second DUI conviction, what license loss applies at zero-point-two-zero BAC or for refusal?
sec06-R27-card.expected_back: The second-DUI-offense table assigns thirty months of license loss for BAC at least zero point two zero or chemical-test refusal.

sec06-R28-card.front: What fine range and prison window apply in court for a second DUI offense?
sec06-R28-card.expected_back: The second-DUI-offense court table lists a seven hundred fifty dollars to two thousand five hundred dollars fine and imprisonment from sixty days to eighteen months.

sec06-R29-card.front: How can an eligible second-DUI offender have the minimum prison sentence suspended?
sec06-R29-card.expected_back: For an eligible second-DUI offender, the court may suspend the minimum prison term after successful participation in its Court of Common Pleas DUI Treatment Program.

sec06-R30-card.front: On a third DUI conviction, what license loss applies for drugs or BAC under zero-point-one-five?
sec06-R30-card.expected_back: The third-DUI-offense table assigns twenty-four months of license loss for drugs or BAC below zero point one five.

sec06-R31-card.front: On a third DUI conviction, what license loss applies for a zero-point-one-five to zero-point-one-nine BAC?
sec06-R31-card.expected_back: The third-DUI-offense table assigns thirty months of license loss for the BAC bracket labeled zero point one five through zero point one nine.

sec06-R32-card.front: On a third DUI conviction, what license loss applies at zero-point-two-zero BAC or for refusal?
sec06-R32-card.expected_back: The third-DUI-offense table assigns thirty-six months of license loss for BAC at least zero point two zero or chemical-test refusal.

sec06-R33-card.front: How is a third DUI committed at any time after two prior offenses classified in Delaware?
sec06-R33-card.expected_back: A third DUI offense committed at any time after two prior offenses is classified as a Class G felony.

sec06-R34-card.front: What maximum court fine is listed for a third DUI offense in Delaware?
sec06-R34-card.expected_back: The third-DUI-offense court table lists a fine up to five thousand dollars.

sec06-R35-card.front: What imprisonment range is listed in the court table for a third DUI offense?
sec06-R35-card.expected_back: The third-DUI-offense court table lists imprisonment from one to two years.

sec06-R36-card.front: What felony classification applies to a fourth DUI committed at any time after three prior offenses?
sec06-R36-card.expected_back: A fourth DUI offense committed at any time after three prior offenses is classified as a Class E felony.

sec06-R37-card.front: How many months of license loss carry across every BAC bracket on a fourth DUI conviction?
sec06-R37-card.expected_back: Every fourth-DUI-offense conviction carries sixty months of license loss in the DMV table.

sec06-R38-card.front: What maximum fine appears in the court table for a fourth DUI offense?
sec06-R38-card.expected_back: The fourth-DUI-offense court table lists a fine up to seven thousand dollars.

sec06-R39-card.front: What prison range applies in the court table for a fourth DUI offense?
sec06-R39-card.expected_back: The fourth-DUI-offense court table lists imprisonment from two to five years.

sec06-R40-card.front: How is a fifth DUI offense classified under Delaware law?
sec06-R40-card.expected_back: A fifth DUI offense is classified as a Class E felony.

sec06-R41-card.front: How many months of license loss apply to every fifth-DUI conviction?
sec06-R41-card.expected_back: Every fifth-DUI-offense conviction carries sixty months of license loss in the DMV table.

sec06-R42-card.front: What is the maximum court fine listed for a fifth DUI offense?
sec06-R42-card.expected_back: The fifth-DUI-offense court table lists a fine up to ten thousand dollars.

sec06-R43-card.front: What imprisonment range is assigned to a fifth DUI offense in the court table?
sec06-R43-card.expected_back: The fifth-DUI-offense court table lists imprisonment from three to five years.

sec06-R44-card.front: What felony classification applies to a sixth DUI offense in Delaware?
sec06-R44-card.expected_back: A sixth DUI offense is classified as a Class D felony.

sec06-R45-card.front: How many months of license loss does the DMV table assign to every sixth-DUI conviction?
sec06-R45-card.expected_back: Every sixth-DUI-offense conviction carries sixty months of license loss in the DMV table.

sec06-R46-card.front: What maximum fine does the court table list for a sixth DUI offense?
sec06-R46-card.expected_back: The sixth-DUI-offense court table lists a fine up to ten thousand dollars.

sec06-R47-card.front: What imprisonment range appears in the court table for a sixth DUI offense?
sec06-R47-card.expected_back: The sixth-DUI-offense court table lists imprisonment from four to eight years.

sec06-R48-card.front: How is a seventh or subsequent DUI offense classified in Delaware?
sec06-R48-card.expected_back: A seventh or later DUI offense is classified as a Class C felony.

sec06-R49-card.front: How many months of license loss apply to every seventh-or-later DUI conviction?
sec06-R49-card.expected_back: Every seventh-or-later DUI conviction carries sixty months of license loss in the DMV table.

sec06-R50-card.front: What maximum court fine applies to a seventh or later DUI offense?
sec06-R50-card.expected_back: The seventh-or-later DUI court table lists a fine up to fifteen thousand dollars.

sec06-R51-card.front: What imprisonment window does the court table list for a seventh or later DUI offense?
sec06-R51-card.expected_back: The seventh-or-later DUI court table lists imprisonment from five to fifteen years.

sec06-R52-card.front: When does an IID license permit driving an ignition-interlock-equipped vehicle?
sec06-R52-card.expected_back: An IID license permits operation of an IID-equipped vehicle only after the participant meets all minimum qualifications.

sec06-R53-card.front: How soon may First Offender Election participants apply for an IID license upon entering the program?
sec06-R53-card.expected_back: FOE participants are immediately eligible to apply for an IID license when entering the program, subject to its other qualifications.

sec06-R54-card.front: How many days of minimum revocation apply before IID application eligibility on a non-FOE first conviction?
sec06-R54-card.expected_back: For a non-FOE first conviction, the IID table gives a minimum revocation of thirty to forty-five days before application eligibility, depending on BAC.

sec06-R55-card.front: What minimum revocation period must pass before IID application eligibility on a second DUI conviction?
sec06-R55-card.expected_back: For a second conviction, the IID table gives a sixty-day minimum revocation before application eligibility, subject to other qualifications.

sec06-R56-card.front: What minimum revocation period precedes IID application eligibility on a third DUI conviction?
sec06-R56-card.expected_back: For a third conviction, the IID table gives a ninety-day minimum revocation before application eligibility, subject to other qualifications.

sec06-R57-card.front: How long is the minimum revocation before IID application eligibility on a fourth or later DUI conviction?
sec06-R57-card.expected_back: For a fourth or later conviction, the IID table gives a six-month minimum revocation before application eligibility, subject to other qualifications.

sec06-R58-card.front: Which license classes and crash outcomes are barred from using a Delaware IID license?
sec06-R58-card.expected_back: An IID license cannot be used for CDL-class vehicles or peripheral endorsements, and the qualifying offense must not involve death or serious injury.

sec06-R59-card.front: How do unrelated suspensions, revocations, disqualifications, or denials affect IID license issuance?
sec06-R59-card.expected_back: Other suspensions, revocations, disqualifications, denials or statutory disqualification criteria can prevent issuance of an IID license.

sec06-R60-card.front: What license status at offense time, enrollment step, and surrender action are required for a general IID application?
sec06-R60-card.expected_back: The general IID application process requires a valid Delaware license at the time of the offense, an application, the required treatment enrollment and fees, and surrender of the currently issued Delaware license.

sec06-R61-card.front: What insurance documentation must an IID applicant provide?
sec06-R61-card.expected_back: An IID applicant must provide insurance proof for the vehicles on which devices will be installed.

sec06-R62-card.front: Must an IID participant install devices and show Delaware registration on vehicles they drive even if owned by someone else?
sec06-R62-card.expected_back: The IID process requires proof of valid Delaware registration and installation on every vehicle the participant will operate during revocation, even a vehicle the participant does not own.

sec06-R63-card.front: Which three driver exams might the DMV require prior to issuing an IID license?
sec06-R63-card.expected_back: Vision, knowledge and road-skills testing may be required before an IID license is issued.

sec06-R64-card.front: What two steps happen with the vendor before the DMV issues limited driving privileges?
sec06-R64-card.expected_back: After all IID conditions are met, the DMV authorizes an approved vendor’s installation and verifies installation before issuing limited driving privileges for the approved vehicles.

sec06-R65-card.front: Who pays IID program costs, and from what date is required IID duration measured?
sec06-R65-card.expected_back: The IID participant pays all program costs and must keep devices installed for the required period, measured from IID license issuance rather than the original revocation end date.

sec06-R66-card.front: How many months does the IID duration table require for an FOE participant?
sec06-R66-card.expected_back: The IID duration table requires four months for a FOE participant.

sec06-R67-card.front: How many months of IID use are required for a non-FOE first DUI conviction?
sec06-R67-card.expected_back: For a non-FOE first conviction, the IID duration table requires twelve to twenty-three months, depending on BAC.

sec06-R68-card.front: What IID duration range applies to a second DUI conviction depending on BAC?
sec06-R68-card.expected_back: For a second conviction, the IID duration table requires sixteen to twenty-eight months, depending on BAC.

sec06-R69-card.front: What IID duration range applies to a third DUI conviction depending on BAC?
sec06-R69-card.expected_back: For a third conviction, the IID duration table requires twenty-one to thirty-three months, depending on BAC.

sec06-R70-card.front: At least how many months of IID use does the table require for a fourth or later conviction?
sec06-R70-card.expected_back: The IID duration table requires at least fifty-four months for a fourth or later conviction.

sec06-R71-card.front: What two actions can the DMV take if an IID participant fails to comply with program rules?
sec06-R71-card.expected_back: Noncompliance can cause the DMV to extend IID time or disqualify the participant.

sec06-R72-card.front: What rules govern a DUI offender who skips applying for the ignition-interlock program?
sec06-R72-card.expected_back: A DUI offender who does not apply for the IID program must serve the entire revocation and cannot drive during it.

sec14-F01-card.front: What two things should you communicate to surrounding road users so nobody gets caught off guard?
sec14-F01-card.expected_back: Let other road users know both your presence and your intended action so they are not surprised.

sec14-F02-card.front: In which three weather conditions do headlights help other motorists spot your vehicle?
sec14-F02-card.expected_back: Headlights help other drivers detect your vehicle in rain, snow and fog.

sec14-F03-card.front: What must you do with your headlights whenever your windshield wipers are running?
sec14-F03-card.expected_back: When the windshield wipers are turned on, the headlights must also be on.

sec14-F04-card.front: Why should you switch headlights on right as evening darkness begins?
sec14-F04-card.expected_back: Switch on headlights as darkness begins so others can see the vehicle.

sec14-F05-card.front: Why shouldn't you drive using only parking lamps when conditions call for lights?
sec14-F05-card.expected_back: Use headlights when driving requires lights; parking lamps serve parked vehicles.

sec14-F06-card.front: Why should you turn headlights on when driving away from a low rising or setting sun?
sec14-F06-card.expected_back: When traveling away from a low rising or setting sun, use headlights to help opposing drivers see you.

sec14-F07-card.front: What is the safety purpose of sounding your vehicle's horn?
sec14-F07-card.expected_back: A horn can attract another road user’s attention to help prevent a collision.

sec14-F08-card.front: When is a light tap on the horn appropriate?
sec14-F08-card.expected_back: A light horn tap can alert a driver beginning to move into your lane or failing to notice you.

sec14-F09-card.front: Which three immediate emergencies justify a sharp horn warning?
sec14-F09-card.expected_back: Use a sharp horn warning when a child or older person is about to enter the street, another vehicle may strike you, or your out-of-control vehicle is moving toward a person.

sec14-F10-card.front: Which three everyday temptations are improper reasons to sound your horn?
sec14-F10-card.expected_back: Do not use the horn to hurry another driver, criticize a mistake or greet a friend.

sec14-F11-card.front: How must you handle your horn around a blind pedestrian?
sec14-F11-card.expected_back: Do not sound the horn around a blind pedestrian.

sec14-F12-card.front: What is a key visibility priority if your vehicle breaks down along a highway?
sec14-F12-card.expected_back: If a vehicle breaks down on a highway, make it visible to other drivers.

sec14-F13-card.front: How should you summon help when communication gear or posted numbers are available during a breakdown?
sec14-F13-card.expected_back: When available, use a telephone or two-way radio to notify authorities of a breakdown and consult posted emergency contact information.

sec14-F14-card.front: Where should you stop and what lights should you activate when mechanical trouble strikes?
sec14-F14-card.expected_back: If vehicle trouble forces a stop, get off the roadway away from traffic if possible and activate hazard flashers.

sec14-F15-card.front: If you cannot get off the roadway during a breakdown, where should you avoid stopping?
sec14-F15-card.expected_back: If you cannot leave the roadway, stop where others can see the vehicle clearly, rather than immediately beyond a hill or curve.

sec14-F16-card.front: How do emergency warning devices placed behind a disabled vehicle help approaching traffic?
sec14-F16-card.expected_back: Emergency warning devices behind a disabled vehicle give approaching drivers notice and room to change lanes.

sec14-F17-card.front: How can you warn approaching drivers if your vehicle lacks emergency warning devices?
sec14-F17-card.expected_back: Without warning devices, the handbook describes warning traffic from a safe roadside position, using a white cloth if available.

sec14-F18-card.front: When must you refuse to stand near your vehicle or change a flat tire?
sec14-F18-card.expected_back: Never stand in a traffic lane or change a tire if that requires occupying the lane.

sec14-F19-card.front: Which simple visual cues on a parked vehicle signal a roadside emergency?
sec14-F19-card.expected_back: A raised hood or a white cloth tied to an antenna, mirror or door handle can signal an emergency.

sec14-F20-card.front: Why shouldn't you cruise beside and slightly behind another vehicle?
sec14-F20-card.expected_back: Avoid driving beside and slightly behind another vehicle, where its driver may not see you.

sec14-F21-card.front: How should you move through another driver's blind spot while passing?
sec14-F21-card.expected_back: When passing, clear the other driver’s blind spot promptly rather than lingering there.

sec14-F22-card.front: Why must you avoid pacing alongside a bus or large truck?
sec14-F22-card.expected_back: Do not remain alongside a bus or truck because large vehicles have extensive blind areas.

sec14-F23-card.front: Why must you warn drivers behind you before slowing down or changing direction?
sec14-F23-card.expected_back: Warn following drivers before changing direction or slowing so they have time to respond.

sec14-F24-card.front: Should you still signal turns, lane changes, merges, and parking when nobody looks nearby?
sec14-F24-card.expected_back: Signal before turning, changing lanes, merging or parking, even when no other road user is visible.

sec14-F25-card.front: What minimum time cue and legal turn-distance requirement does Delaware pair for signaling?
sec14-F25-card.expected_back: The handbook recommends signaling at least three seconds before a maneuver while separately stating the three hundred-foot legal requirement before a turn.

sec14-F26-card.front: How can signaling before an intervening driveway or waiting vehicle create a hazard?
sec14-F26-card.expected_back: Signaling before an intervening entrance or waiting vehicle can mislead another driver about where you intend to turn.

sec14-F27-card.front: What should you verify right after completing a lane change or gentle turn?
sec14-F27-card.expected_back: After a turn or lane change, check that the signal has canceled and switch it off manually if necessary.

sec14-F28-card.front: How should you use your brake pedal when slowing in an unexpected spot?
sec14-F28-card.expected_back: When slowing somewhere unexpected, the handbook recommends tapping the brake pedal three or four times to alert following drivers.

sec14-F29-card.front: Which three roadway situations call for extra warning before you slow down?
sec14-F29-card.memory_hook: No exit-lane, corner park, hidden block
sec14-F29-card.expected_back: Warn when slowing to turn from a road without an exit lane, to park near an intersection, or for an obstruction hidden from following traffic.

sec14-F30-card.front: What signal methods and minimum continuous distance apply before making a turn in Delaware?
sec14-F30-card.expected_back: Give a hand-and-arm signal, an electrical turn signal, or both continuously for at least three hundred feet before turning.

sec14-F31-card.front: How should you adjust signaling distance at high speeds such as expressway lane changes?
sec14-F31-card.expected_back: At higher speeds, the handbook recommends signaling over a longer distance, particularly for expressway lane changes.

sec14-R01-card.front: Which factors govern safe speed selection, and why do higher speeds demand bigger margins?
sec14-R01-card.expected_back: Set speed for road and traffic conditions, available visibility and the applicable limit because higher speeds require more room to maneuver or stop.

sec14-R02-card.front: At which three roadway features should you drop speed ahead of time?
sec14-R02-card.expected_back: Slow before a sharp curve, on a slippery surface and where water stands on the roadway.

sec14-R03-card.front: Which two paired elements determine how well your tires grip the road?
sec14-R03-card.expected_back: Tire grip depends on the type and condition of both the tire and road surface.

sec14-R04-card.front: Where should you look to find the right inflation pressure for maintaining your tires?
sec14-R04-card.expected_back: Keep tires in good condition and inflate them according to the vehicle owner’s manual.

sec14-R05-card.front: Why must you drop speed when moving onto gravel or dirt roads?
sec14-R05-card.expected_back: Reduce speed on gravel or dirt because traction is lower than on asphalt or concrete and stopping or turning can cause skids more readily.

sec14-R06-card.front: When should you finish slowing for a curve so you avoid skidding?
sec14-R06-card.expected_back: Slow before entering a curve so braking in the curve does not create a skid.

sec14-R07-card.front: When should you begin reducing speed as rain, sleet, or snow starts falling?
sec14-R07-card.expected_back: Reduce speed at the first rain, sleet or snow because wet or frozen surfaces reduce tire grip.

sec14-R08-card.front: By about how much does the Delaware handbook advise reducing speed on wet pavement?
sec14-R08-card.expected_back: For wet roads, the handbook’s speed-adjustment guidance is a reduction of about ten miles per hour

sec14-R09-card.front: How much should you reduce your speed when driving on packed snow?
sec14-R09-card.expected_back: For packed snow, the handbook advises cutting speed in half.

sec14-R10-card.front: What traction gear does the handbook recommend for snow-covered roads, and what pace for ice?
sec14-R10-card.expected_back: The handbook recommends snow tires or chains on snow-covered roads and a crawling speed on ice.

sec14-R11-card.front: What precaution applies to icy trips and using studded snow tires?
sec14-R11-card.expected_back: Avoid driving on icy roads when possible, and do not assume studded tires are permitted everywhere or in every season.

sec14-R12-card.front: How do shaded roadway sections behave on cold, wet days?
sec14-R12-card.expected_back: On cold wet days, shaded road areas can freeze first and remain icy longer.

sec14-R13-card.front: Why do bridges and overpasses freeze while approaching roadways remain wet?
sec14-R13-card.expected_back: Bridges and overpasses can freeze while nearby pavement remains unfrozen because their surfaces can be colder.

sec14-R14-card.front: Why is ice near thirty-two degrees more treacherous than deep-freeze ice?
sec14-R14-card.expected_back: Ice near the freezing point can become wet and more slippery than ice at much colder temperatures.

sec14-R15-card.front: What happens during hydroplaning, and what simple habit helps prevent it?
sec14-R15-card.expected_back: Hydroplaning occurs when tires begin riding on water instead of maintaining road contact; slowing in rain or on a wet road helps prevent it.

sec14-R16-card.front: How do bald or badly worn tires change wet-road hydroplaning risk?
sec14-R16-card.expected_back: Bald or badly worn tires can lose wet-road traction at lower speeds.

sec14-R17-card.front: What should your right foot do if your tires start losing grip on wet pavement?
sec14-R17-card.expected_back: If the tires seem to lose road grip, ease pressure off the accelerator.

sec14-R18-card.front: How should you handle steering and braking while road grip is lost?
sec14-R18-card.expected_back: When grip is lost, keep the wheel straight and avoid stopping or turning until traction returns; if an emergency demands a turn, make it slowly.

sec14-R19-card.front: What safety drawback comes from repeatedly speeding past surrounding traffic?
sec14-R19-card.expected_back: Repeatedly driving faster than traffic and passing creates additional collision opportunities.

sec14-R20-card.front: What should a driver moving much slower than normal traffic do when vehicles stack up behind?
sec14-R20-card.expected_back: If traffic collects behind a much slower vehicle, its driver should pull aside when safe and let others pass.

sec14-R21-card.front: How should you use a highway entrance ramp before merging into main lanes?
sec14-R21-card.expected_back: Use an entrance ramp to build toward traffic speed before merging.

sec14-R22-card.front: Why shouldn't you roll to the tip of an entrance ramp and stop, and what should you do instead?
sec14-R22-card.expected_back: Avoid reaching the end of an entrance ramp and stopping; if waiting for a gap, slow earlier so room remains to accelerate.

sec14-R23-card.front: When should you begin slowing down for a highway exit ramp?
sec14-R23-card.expected_back: For an exit ramp, remain with traffic speed on the main road and slow after moving onto the ramp.

sec14-R24-card.front: How should you turn off a fast two-lane highway when cars follow behind without a turn lane?
sec14-R24-card.expected_back: When turning from a high-speed two-lane road with traffic behind, signal and use brake lights before reducing speed quickly but safely.

sec14-R25-card.front: Why is spotting slow-moving vehicles far ahead important?
sec14-R25-card.expected_back: Identify slow vehicles early so a lane change or speed reduction can be made gradually.

sec01-F01-card.question_text: What is the main purpose of the Delaware Driver Manual?
sec01-F01-card.teaching_text: Every rule and habit inside the manual builds the foundation for operating everyday passenger vehicles safely.

sec01-F02-card.question_text: Which authority governs if a handbook statement ever conflicts with Delaware legislation?
sec01-F02-card.teaching_text: Handbook summaries simplify traffic law for learners, so enacted Delaware statutes prevail over any wording conflict.

sec01-F18-card.question_text: What does the word must signify when used in the Delaware handbook?
sec01-F18-card.teaching_text: Exam questions hinge on must versus should because ignoring a must statement breaks Delaware traffic law.

sec01-F19-card.question_text: What does the word should signify when used in the Delaware handbook?
sec01-F19-card.teaching_text: Best-practice advice marked with should boosts safety margins even though statutes do not mandate it.

sec01-F03-card.question_text: What step should an applicant with a disability take before visiting the DMV for special exam accommodations?
sec01-F03-card.teaching_text: Scheduling ahead lets staff line up assistive testing tools or interpreters instead of turning you away.

sec01-F04-card.question_text: How can an applicant take the knowledge exam by audio at the DMV?
sec01-F04-card.teaching_text: Listening through headphones helps applicants who process spoken test questions better than reading screens.

sec01-F08-card.question_text: What kind of document is a Delaware Blue Certificate?
sec01-F08-card.teaching_text: Knowing Delaware's color-coded paperwork prevents confusion when gathering your teen permit application packet.

sec01-F13-card.question_text: Which state department approves and sets criteria for a valid Delaware driver education certificate?
sec01-F13-card.teaching_text: Unapproved private driving lessons will not satisfy teen licensing rules without Department of Education approval.

sec01-R06-card.question_text: Whom does an Individualized Education Program serve under Delaware handbook definitions?
sec01-R06-card.teaching_text: Active specialized-education eligibility extends graduated learner-permit age windows under Delaware licensing rules.

sec01-F11-card.question_text: What does a Driving Privilege Card authorize, and what can it never serve as?
sec01-F11-card.teaching_text: Test questions contrast driving authority against identity proof because this card never counts as identification.

sec01-F17-card.question_text: What legal status does a driver license grant to its holder?
sec01-F17-card.teaching_text: Framing driving as an earned privilege explains why unsafe conduct allows the state to suspend it.

sec01-R07-card.question_text: What legal function does a Delaware identification card serve?
sec01-R07-card.teaching_text: Unlike a driver license, an identification card verifies who you are without granting driving authority.

sec01-R09-card.question_text: Which two categories of drivers are recorded in the National Driver Register?
sec01-R09-card.teaching_text: Crossing state lines never wipes away a suspended license or major traffic conviction tracked nationwide.

sec01-R10-card.question_text: Why do motor-vehicle agencies check the National Driver Register before issuing licenses?
sec01-R10-card.teaching_text: Checking national records stops dangerous drivers suspended elsewhere from grabbing a fresh Delaware card.

sec01-R19-card.question_text: What does the SAVE program verify during document screening?
sec01-R19-card.teaching_text: Electronic federal verification confirms immigration paperwork is genuine before DMV issues credentials.

sec01-F09-card.question_text: Which three outcomes count as a conviction under Delaware motor-vehicle law?
sec01-F09-card.teaching_text: Forfeiting a posted bail bond instead of appearing in court still lands on your record as a conviction.

sec01-F12-card.question_text: Who qualifies as a driver under Delaware motor-vehicle definitions?
sec01-F12-card.teaching_text: Sitting behind the wheel in physical control makes you legally responsible even if not cruising down a highway.

sec01-R01-card.question_text: Which agency is meant when the Delaware handbook refers to the Department?
sec01-R01-card.teaching_text: Spotting agency shorthand keeps you from confusing transportation officials with school or revenue offices.

sec01-R02-card.question_text: Which agency is meant when the Delaware handbook uses the capitalized term Division?
sec01-R02-card.teaching_text: Delaware organizes licensing and registration under its Division of Motor Vehicles rather than a separate department.

sec01-R13-card.question_text: Besides the legal titleholder, who else counts as a vehicle owner under the handbook?
sec01-R13-card.teaching_text: Financing a car over time still makes the buyer with immediate possession rights legally an owner.

sec01-R16-card.question_text: Which two items together make up vehicle registration in the handbook?
sec01-R16-card.teaching_text: Lawful road operation requires carrying the paper registration card inside and displaying the plate outside.

sec01-R20-card.question_text: Which state leader does the handbook refer to as the Secretary?
sec01-R20-card.teaching_text: Knowing who leads Transportation clarifies rules on special sponsor approvals and highway authority.

sec01-F10-card.question_text: What separates the roadways of a divided highway?
sec01-F10-card.teaching_text: School-bus stopping rules change on divided highways, so recognizing physical or impeding dividers matters.

sec01-F14-card.question_text: How wide is a highway under the handbook definition, and which roads are excluded?
sec01-F14-card.teaching_text: Public highway law spans boundary-to-boundary width while leaving out private or institutional roads.

sec01-F20-card.question_text: Which part of a highway counts as the roadway, and what edge area is excluded?
sec01-F20-card.teaching_text: Distinguishing the traveled roadway from the shoulder governs legal passing and emergency pull-offs.

sec01-R05-card.question_text: What defines an express highway in Delaware?
sec01-R05-card.teaching_text: Express routes prioritize continuous flow over local driveway access, demanding smooth high-speed merges.

sec01-R17-card.question_text: How does the handbook's meaning of road compare with its meaning of highway?
sec01-R17-card.teaching_text: Treating both words identically on test day prevents applicants from inventing nonexistent legal distinctions.

sec01-R18-card.question_text: What is a highway safety zone, and who is allowed to use it?
sec01-R18-card.teaching_text: Driving or parking across a marked pedestrian refuge strips walkers of their protected island in traffic.

sec01-R21-card.question_text: Where must a highway be located to fit the handbook's definition of a street?
sec01-R21-card.teaching_text: Urban and suburban districts bring tighter speed limits, crosswalks, and curb parking rules.

sec01-F07-card.question_text: Where is a bike box placed, and how does it help cyclists?
sec01-F07-card.teaching_text: Queueing cyclists ahead of stopped bumpers prevents right-hook and left-turn blind-spot collisions on green.

sec01-F15-card.question_text: What term names the shared zone where a public road meets or crosses train tracks?
sec01-F15-card.teaching_text: Recognizing rail crossings as intersections reminds drivers never to stop on tracks in backed-up traffic.

sec01-F16-card.question_text: Does an intersection require two highways to cross completely, or is meeting enough?
sec01-F16-card.teaching_text: A three-way T-junction where one road ends into another triggers full intersection parking and passing bans.

sec01-R15-card.question_text: Which everyday phrase does the handbook use interchangeably with highway-rail intersection?
sec01-R15-card.teaching_text: Connecting technical statutory terms with everyday wording keeps exam questions crystal clear.

sec01-R22-card.question_text: How many degrees does a three-point turn reverse your car, and in what three-move sequence?
sec01-R22-card.teaching_text: Nailing the exact left-forward, right-reverse, right-forward order prepares you for Delaware's road test.

sec01-R24-card.question_text: How is a two-way cycle track built, and how do cyclists move within it?
sec01-R24-card.teaching_text: Drivers turning across a cycle track must look both ways because riders approach from either direction.

sec01-F05-card.question_text: How are vehicles propelled under the standard bicycle definition?
sec01-F05-card.teaching_text: Human foot-pedal propulsion separates classic pedal bicycles from mopeds and motor-driven cycles under state law.

sec01-F06-card.question_text: What pedal, wheel, wattage, and motor-only speed caps define a Delaware electric bicycle?
sec01-F06-card.teaching_text: Exceeding seven hundred fifty watts or twenty miles per hour with a one-seventy rider reclassifies the machine.

sec01-R08-card.question_text: Which self-propelled machines are excluded from Delaware's motor vehicle definition?
sec01-R08-card.teaching_text: Carving out farm tractors and off-highway rigs keeps field machinery distinct from highway passenger cars.

sec01-R12-card.question_text: What capability defines an off-highway vehicle?
sec01-R12-card.teaching_text: Machines built for open woods, dunes, or fields lack standard highway safety equipment and licensing status.

sec01-R23-card.question_text: What two traits define a trailer in the Delaware handbook?
sec01-R23-card.teaching_text: Because trailers lack self-propulsion, towing rules govern their registration, lighting, and combined weight.

sec01-R25-card.question_text: Which five device types are excluded from the handbook's general vehicle definition?
sec01-R25-card.teaching_text: Memorizing all five excluded device groups prevents mixing general highway vehicles with special equipment.

sec01-R26-card.question_text: Which paint color and displayed lettering define a school bus in the handbook?
sec01-R26-card.teaching_text: Distinctive chrome-yellow paint and block lettering alert every lane to prepare for flashing student stops.

sec01-R27-card.question_text: Subject to its exclusions, what devices fall under the handbook's general vehicle definition?
sec01-R27-card.teaching_text: Any non-excluded rig moving people or cargo along a public road triggers general traffic responsibilities.

sec01-R03-card.question_text: Where does an electric vehicle get its propulsion and battery charge?
sec01-R03-card.teaching_text: Pure battery electrics run without a gas tank and rely entirely on plugging into external power.

sec01-R04-card.question_text: What energy source powers the electric motor inside a fuel-cell electric vehicle?
sec01-R04-card.teaching_text: Instead of charging a plug-in pack from the grid, fuel-cell cars generate electricity onboard from hydrogen.

sec01-R11-card.question_text: How does a non-plug-in hybrid combine power sources, and can it charge externally?
sec01-R11-card.teaching_text: Conventional hybrids recapture braking and engine energy internally without ever connecting to a wall charger.

sec01-R14-card.question_text: What distinguishes a plug-in hybrid from a non-plug-in hybrid?
sec01-R14-card.teaching_text: Adding an externally rechargeable battery lets plug-in hybrids cover short trips on electricity before burning fuel.

sec02-F01-card.question_text: Which five personal facts must your compliant-identification documents establish?
sec02-F01-card.teaching_text: Leaving even one of the five proofs at home stalls federally compliant issuance at the counter.

sec02-F02-card.question_text: What must the Delaware DMV do with the source documents an applicant presents?
sec02-F02-card.teaching_text: Staff validate every birth record, passport, and Social Security number directly against issuing databases.

sec02-F03-card.question_text: What visual symbol marks a federally compliant Delaware license or ID, and where does it sit?
sec02-F03-card.teaching_text: Spotting that upper-right gold star confirms your card meets federal boarding and facility standards.

sec02-F04-card.question_text: What wording is printed along the top margin of a noncompliant Delaware license or ID?
sec02-F04-card.teaching_text: Cards marked Not for Federal ID still prove state driving privileges without clearing federal checkpoints.
sec02-F04-card.must_match_memory_hook: Top reads Not for Federal ID

visual_sync.text_span: Top reads Not for Federal ID

sec02-F05-card.question_text: Unless exempted, what must anyone driving on Delaware public roads hold and keep with them?
sec02-F05-card.teaching_text: Having an active license record at home still violates the law if you drive without carrying it.

sec02-F06-card.question_text: How many days does a new bona fide Delaware resident have to get a Delaware driver license?
sec02-F06-card.teaching_text: Waiting past sixty days after establishing Delaware residency makes your old state license invalid here.

sec02-F07-card.question_text: Which three equipment types may operate temporarily on highways without a Delaware driver license?
sec02-F07-card.teaching_text: Moving farm tractors or paving rollers briefly along public roads falls under a narrow statutory exemption.

sec02-F08-card.question_text: When may a nonresident drive in Delaware using a home-state or home-country license?
sec02-F08-card.teaching_text: Visitors must be older than sixteen and keep their valid home license physically with them.

sec02-F09-card.question_text: Which driver license may active-duty military members and their dependents use in Delaware?
sec02-F09-card.teaching_text: Stationing orders in Delaware never force active service members or dependents to give up home-state licenses.

sec02-F10-card.question_text: Can an applicant ever obtain a Delaware license or endorsement before reaching its minimum age?
sec02-F10-card.teaching_text: Passing coursework early still requires hitting the statutory birthday before DMV can issue the credential.

sec02-F11-card.question_text: What coursework must any license applicant younger than eighteen finish?
sec02-F11-card.teaching_text: Every minor needs a Delaware Department of Education approved course before stepping into teen licensing.

sec02-F12-card.question_text: What signature requirement applies to a license applicant younger than eighteen?
sec02-F12-card.teaching_text: Minors cannot sign themselves into licensing liability without an eligible adult's witnessed consent signature.

sec02-F13-card.question_text: How does an active license suspension or revocation in another jurisdiction affect a Delaware application?
sec02-F13-card.teaching_text: Delaware screens national records and refuses licenses until out-of-state suspensions or revocations clear.

sec02-F14-card.question_text: What residency status must a Delaware driver-license applicant hold?
sec02-F14-card.teaching_text: Only genuine Delaware residents qualify for state licensing rather than short-term travelers.

sec02-F15-card.question_text: What road-sign skill is required to qualify for a Delaware license?
sec02-F15-card.teaching_text: Reading English warning and regulatory signs in traffic is essential even if written tests offer translations.

sec02-F16-card.question_text: What two broad capacities must an applicant possess to qualify for a license?
sec02-F16-card.teaching_text: Safe vehicle control requires both physical coordination at the controls and sound judgment in traffic.

sec02-F17-card.question_text: What proof must an applicant supply for a central-nervous-system condition that causes blackouts?
sec02-F17-card.teaching_text: Written medical confirmation ensures seizure or fainting conditions are controlled before driving.

sec02-F18-card.question_text: Which requirements apply when an applicant cannot establish lawful U.S. presence?
sec02-F18-card.teaching_text: Delaware routes residents lacking lawful-presence paperwork through dedicated Driving Privilege Card screening.

sec02-F19-card.question_text: What happens if personal records held by other agencies conflict with your application?
sec02-F19-card.teaching_text: Mismatched birthdates or names across Social Security or immigration databases halt credential printing.

sec02-F41-card.question_text: Which two substance-related conditions bar issuance of a Delaware driver license?
sec02-F41-card.teaching_text: Chronic alcohol dependence or narcotic addiction poses an unacceptable ongoing hazard on public roads.

sec02-F21-card.question_text: When must noncitizens present original immigration documents, and what two facts does DMV check?
sec02-F21-card.teaching_text: Both first-time visits and renewals require original immigration papers to confirm lawful status and stay.

sec02-F22-card.question_text: What options remain if an applicant's passport or immigration documents are invalid or expired?
sec02-F22-card.teaching_text: Expired status documents bar regular licenses or IDs while leaving Driving Privilege Card eligibility open.

sec02-F23-card.question_text: How far out can a noncitizen's Delaware license or ID expiration date extend?
sec02-F23-card.teaching_text: State credentials track your federal departure date so the card expires alongside authorized presence.

sec02-F24-card.question_text: Which electronic system does the DMV use to verify noncitizen status and authorized stay?
sec02-F24-card.teaching_text: Running SAVE checks electronically confirms current federal immigration records before issuing cards.

sec02-F25-card.question_text: What license expiration length applies when temporary immigration records list duration of status or indefinite stay?
sec02-F25-card.teaching_text: Without a fixed departure calendar date on file, Delaware sets a one-year credential cycle.

sec02-F26-card.question_text: Where must a temporary nonimmigrant resolve an unverified SAVE mismatch before DMV issues a card?
sec02-F26-card.teaching_text: DMV clerks cannot override federal immigration records, so USCIS must clear mismatches first.

sec02-F35-card.question_text: What core status proof must noncitizens provide for a regular Delaware license or ID?
sec02-F35-card.teaching_text: Every regular credential path requires valid proof of lawful presence in the United States.

sec02-F20-card.question_text: How and where must a Delaware driver-license application be submitted?
sec02-F20-card.teaching_text: First-time licensing requires live document verification, vision testing, and photos inside a DMV office.

sec02-F27-card.question_text: What forms must an applicant sign and complete when applying for a license?
sec02-F27-card.teaching_text: Answering every eligibility question and signing the surrender agreement prevents holding multiple state licenses.

sec02-F28-card.question_text: What must an applicant do with an existing license or ID card from another state?
sec02-F28-card.teaching_text: Drivers may hold only one jurisdiction's credential, so prior state cards get turned in.

sec02-F30-card.question_text: Which screening must every Delaware driver pass?
sec02-F30-card.teaching_text: Even out-of-state transfers and renewals must prove safe eyesight at the screening machine.

sec02-F31-card.question_text: Which two tests is every driver-license applicant subject to?
sec02-F31-card.teaching_text: Unless waived for a valid transfer or GDL completion, written and road tests apply.

sec02-F36-card.question_text: What can happen if you put false information on a signed license application?
sec02-F36-card.teaching_text: Lying about prior suspensions, health, or identity lets DMV suspend the card issued from it.

sec02-F32-card.question_text: Which two categories of identity documents do Delaware's identification rules call for?
sec02-F32-card.teaching_text: Pairing a foundational birth or passport record with supporting proof locks down applicant identity.

sec02-F33-card.question_text: What two personal facts must the primary identity document show, plus what verification feature?
sec02-F33-card.teaching_text: DMV accepts primary identity records only when the issuing authority can verify your name and birthdate.

sec02-F37-card.question_text: Which three document flaws disqualify identity and lawful-presence paperwork?
sec02-F37-card.teaching_text: Showing up with a photocopy, expired passport, or scratched-out text gets rejected immediately.

sec02-F38-card.question_text: How must your name appear across all documents presented at the DMV?
sec02-F38-card.teaching_text: Unexplained name differences between your birth certificate and Social Security record halt processing without linkage proof.

sec02-F39-card.question_text: What issuer and seal requirements apply to a U.S. birth certificate used for identity?
sec02-F39-card.teaching_text: Only state health or vital-statistics records bearing an embossed seal prove legal birth registration.

sec02-F40-card.question_text: Which two common birth items are rejected as substitutes for a certified birth certificate?
sec02-F40-card.teaching_text: Decorative hospital footprint sheets and wallet cards lack state vital-statistics registration authority at the counter.

sec02-R01-card.question_text: What extra detail must appear on a birth certificate presented for an applicant under eighteen?
sec02-R01-card.teaching_text: Listing birth parents lets DMV verify that the adult signing GDL sponsorship has parental authority.

sec02-R02-card.question_text: What extra proof must an applicant under eighteen or in the IEP graduated program present?
sec02-R02-card.teaching_text: Verifying legal parentage or guardianship ensures the right responsible adult signs teen paperwork.

sec02-R03-card.question_text: What companion document is required when offering a valid foreign passport as identity proof?
sec02-R03-card.teaching_text: For regular licensing, a foreign passport proves identity only alongside matching federal immigration status paperwork.

sec02-R04-card.question_text: How does Delaware treat a consular report of birth abroad during document screening?
sec02-R04-card.teaching_text: U.S. citizens born overseas use a consular report of birth abroad in place of state birth records.

sec02-R05-card.question_text: What two licensing requirements does a certificate of naturalization satisfy?
sec02-R05-card.teaching_text: Presenting an original naturalization certificate establishes both personal identity and U.S. citizenship in one step.

sec02-R06-card.question_text: How is a certificate of citizenship classified on Delaware's document list?
sec02-R06-card.teaching_text: Derived or acquired citizens use their certificate of citizenship to clear identity and lawful-presence checks.

sec02-R07-card.question_text: What does a valid U.S. passport establish on the Delaware document checklist?
sec02-R07-card.teaching_text: An unexpired U.S. passport covers both primary identity and citizenship without hunting down a birth certificate.

sec02-R08-card.question_text: How does Delaware treat a permanent-resident re-entry permit at the counter?
sec02-R08-card.teaching_text: Lawful permanent residents carrying a valid re-entry permit satisfy both identity and status verification.

sec02-R09-card.question_text: What does a refugee travel document qualify as under Delaware's document list?
sec02-R09-card.teaching_text: Federal refugee travel documents carry verifiable identity and lawful-presence status for state licensing.

sec02-R10-card.question_text: How is an employment authorization card listed among Delaware's identity documents?
sec02-R10-card.teaching_text: A current federal work-authorization card verifies identity and authorized U.S. presence through SAVE.

sec02-R11-card.question_text: What must an alternate-list court order show, what accompanies it, and what card can it never earn?
sec02-R11-card.teaching_text: Even with citizenship proof attached, an alternate-list court order never qualifies for gold-star federal compliance.

sec02-R12-card.question_text: Does a criminal or civil conviction abstract count as an alternate-list court order?
sec02-R12-card.teaching_text: Court dockets summarizing civil or criminal judgments lack the identity verification of a formal court order.

sec02-R13-card.question_text: What two limits apply when offering a state photo license under the alternate identity list?
sec02-R13-card.teaching_text: Using an alternate-list state photo license still demands separate lawful-presence proof and bars federal compliance.

sec02-R14-card.question_text: What must a certified school record from the alternate list verify, and what limits apply?
sec02-R14-card.teaching_text: School transcripts help establish identity for noncompliant cards only when paired with citizenship or presence proof.

sec02-F29-card.question_text: When must a Delaware applicant provide proof of a Social Security number?
sec02-F29-card.teaching_text: Anyone eligible for a Social Security number must document it before receiving a regular credential.

sec02-R15-card.question_text: Does an original Social Security card satisfy Delaware's Social Security-number proof rule?
sec02-R15-card.teaching_text: Bringing your unlaminated original Social Security card is the most direct way to verify your number.

sec02-R16-card.question_text: Is a W-two tax form accepted to prove your Social Security number?
sec02-R16-card.teaching_text: Employer W-two wage statements work as backup proof whenever your Social Security card is misplaced, provided all nine digits appear.

sec02-R17-card.question_text: What condition must a pay stub meet to count as Social Security-number proof?
sec02-R17-card.teaching_text: Modern payroll stubs that mask the first five digits with asterisks get turned away at DMV.

sec02-R18-card.question_text: Can a Medicare or Medicaid card be used to prove your Social Security number?
sec02-R18-card.teaching_text: Health-benefit cards no longer serve as verifiable Social Security proof at Delaware licensing counters.

sec02-R19-card.question_text: How does presenting a Social Security ineligibility letter affect federal compliance on your Delaware card?
sec02-R19-card.teaching_text: Applicants ineligible for a Social Security number cannot receive a gold-star card, though noncompliant options remain.

sec02-F34-card.question_text: How many proofs of Delaware residence does the general identification checklist require?
sec02-F34-card.teaching_text: Showing up with only one utility bill stalls issuance unless a teen sponsor waiver applies.

sec02-F42-card.question_text: Which three document defects cause residence-proof papers to be rejected?
sec02-F42-card.teaching_text: Tampered dates, expired leases, or photocopied envelopes fail Delaware's strict residency verification.

sec02-R20-card.question_text: What issuer and address rules apply to your two Delaware residence proofs?
sec02-R20-card.teaching_text: Two statements from the same bank or a post-office box cannot establish physical Delaware residency.

sec02-R21-card.question_text: Which carrier and age limit govern mail used as Delaware residence proof?
sec02-R21-card.teaching_text: Only Postal Service mail postmarked or received inside the past sixty days proves current residency.

sec02-R22-card.question_text: Does the DMV accept address-proof packages delivered through UPS, FedEx, or DHL?
sec02-R22-card.teaching_text: Private shipping labels fail postal address verification, so stick strictly to United States Postal Service mail.

sec02-R23-card.question_text: May personal letters or greeting cards from friends or family prove Delaware residence?
sec02-R23-card.teaching_text: Handwritten envelopes from relatives lack institutional verification, so bring business or government statements.

sec02-R24-card.question_text: Which six business or contract document types are listed as valid Delaware residence proofs?
sec02-R24-card.teaching_text: Utility bills, credit or bank statements, work records, insurance policies, and rental agreements satisfy address proof.

sec02-R25-card.question_text: What documentation is required if you have changed your legal name more than once?
sec02-R25-card.teaching_text: DMV must trace an unbroken paper chain from your birth record through each marriage, divorce, or order.

sec02-R26-card.question_text: What Social Security step and timing gap are required before visiting the DMV for a name change?
sec02-R26-card.teaching_text: Visiting DMV the same afternoon fails because federal Social Security databases take forty-eight hours to sync.

sec02-R27-card.question_text: What two features make a marriage license or civil-union certificate valid for a DMV name change?
sec02-R27-card.teaching_text: Only county or state civil records carrying an embossed seal establish a legal name change.

sec02-R28-card.question_text: Does a ceremonial marriage certificate signed by clergy satisfy DMV name-change rules?
sec02-R28-card.teaching_text: Ceremonial keepsake certificates signed at a wedding lack government vital-records filing proof.

sec02-R29-card.question_text: When does a finalized divorce decree authorize returning to a previous name at the DMV?
sec02-R29-card.teaching_text: A divorce decree missing explicit name-restoration language requires a separate court name-change order.

sec02-R30-card.question_text: Must a foreign-born adopted minor prove citizenship or lawful presence when an adoptive parent is a U.S. citizen?
sec02-R30-card.teaching_text: An adoptive parent's U.S. passport alone does not establish the child's own federal citizenship or status.

sec02-R31-card.question_text: What is required if a foreign-born adopted minor's foreign birth certificate and status proof show different names?
sec02-R31-card.teaching_text: Linking the birth name to the adopted name requires formal legal name-change or adoption documentation.

sec02-R32-card.question_text: When must adoption paperwork be presented for a foreign-born adopted minor?
sec02-R32-card.teaching_text: When a foreign birth record still lists biological parents, adoption decrees prove the adoptive parents' authority.

sec02-R33-card.question_text: What copy standard and language requirement apply to foreign-adoption documents?
sec02-R33-card.teaching_text: Uncertified scans get rejected, and non-English adoption decrees may require certified English translations.

sec02-R34-card.question_text: Where does a Delaware Driving Privilege Card authorize driving, and does it count as valid ID?
sec02-R34-card.teaching_text: Treat a Driving Privilege Card strictly as in-state driving authority rather than government photo identification.

sec02-R35-card.question_text: Which group of residents is eligible to apply for a Delaware Driving Privilege Card?
sec02-R35-card.teaching_text: Delaware created this credential specifically for eligible foreign residents unable to document lawful U.S. presence.

sec02-R36-card.question_text: Can U.S. citizens or people holding valid lawful-presence documents get a Driving Privilege Card?
sec02-R36-card.teaching_text: Anyone holding citizenship or valid lawful-presence paperwork must use the regular license path instead.

sec02-R37-card.question_text: How much does a Delaware Driving Privilege Card cost, and how long does it stay valid?
sec02-R37-card.teaching_text: Contrast the twenty-dollar, four-year Privilege Card against the fifty-dollar, eight-year regular Class D license.

sec02-R38-card.question_text: How do Delaware's traffic laws and driving rules apply to Driving Privilege Card holders?
sec02-R38-card.teaching_text: Every speed limit, insurance mandate, point rule, and traffic penalty applies identically on the road.

sec02-R42-card.question_text: What must accompany any foreign-language document presented for a Driving Privilege Card?
sec02-R42-card.teaching_text: Bringing untranslated foreign birth or identity papers stalls your Driving Privilege Card review.

sec02-R43-card.question_text: Which five items make up the complete Driving Privilege Card document package?
sec02-R43-card.teaching_text: Missing your fingerprint receipt, two-year tax proof, identity, name link, or two address proofs halts processing.

sec02-R44-card.question_text: What extra birth documents must a Driving Privilege Card applicant under eighteen supply?
sec02-R44-card.teaching_text: Minor Privilege Card applicants need both their foreign birth record and its professional translation to confirm parentage.

sec02-R48-card.question_text: When can a valid unexpired foreign passport establish identity for a Driving Privilege Card?
sec02-R48-card.teaching_text: Unlike regular cards, no U.S. visa is needed once DMV electronically verifies the unexpired passport.

sec02-R49-card.question_text: When may a home-country consular identity card establish identity for a Driving Privilege Card?
sec02-R49-card.teaching_text: Consular IDs qualify only while unexpired and capable of electronic verification approved by DMV.

sec02-R50-card.question_text: Which alternate identity card does the handbook list specifically for Mexican Driving Privilege Card applicants?
sec02-R50-card.teaching_text: Delaware recognizes Mexico's federal voter credential as an approved alternate identity document for DPC applicants.

sec02-R51-card.question_text: What document-condition standards apply to Driving Privilege Card applications?
sec02-R51-card.teaching_text: Just like regular licensing, photocopied, altered, or expired records are rejected at the counter.

sec02-R39-card.question_text: Which agency appointment starts the Driving Privilege Card application process?
sec02-R39-card.teaching_text: Heading to the DMV first wastes a trip because State Bureau of Identification screening comes first.

sec02-R40-card.question_text: What three steps does the State Bureau of Identification complete for a Driving Privilege Card applicant?
sec02-R40-card.teaching_text: Hold onto your SBI receipt carefully because DMV requires it later to confirm completed fingerprinting.

sec02-R41-card.question_text: What tax certification must a Driving Privilege Card applicant get from the Division of Revenue?
sec02-R41-card.teaching_text: Documenting two prior years of Delaware state tax filings confirms established in-state compliance.

sec02-R45-card.question_text: What signature and DMV testing requirements apply to Driving Privilege Card applicants?
sec02-R45-card.teaching_text: Privilege Card drivers pass the exact same vision, written, and road tests as regular drivers.

sec02-R46-card.question_text: How does the DMV confirm a Driving Privilege Card applicant's fingerprint clearance?
sec02-R46-card.teaching_text: Staff cross-check your paper receipt directly against State Bureau of Identification records during application.

sec02-R47-card.question_text: Which state agency does the DMV check with to verify a Driving Privilege Card applicant's tax document?
sec02-R47-card.teaching_text: Direct verification with the Division of Revenue confirms authentic two-year Delaware tax compliance.

sec02-R52-card.question_text: What fee does the State Bureau of Identification collect when fingerprinting a Driving Privilege Card applicant?
sec02-R52-card.teaching_text: Budget seventy-two dollars for State Bureau of Identification fingerprinting separately from DMV's twenty-dollar card fee.

sec03-F01-card.question_text: What two goals does Delaware's graduated-license program balance for new drivers?
sec03-F01-card.teaching_text: Building road hours beside an experienced adult while curbing night and crowd hazards cuts teen crash rates.

sec03-F02-card.question_text: How does a signing parent or sponsor guide a graduated-license applicant's progress?
sec03-F02-card.teaching_text: Delaware empowers the signing adult at home to pace privileges based on demonstrated maturity behind the wheel.

sec03-F03-card.question_text: At what age may an applicant skip the graduated-license program, and what replaces a sponsor?
sec03-F03-card.teaching_text: Turning eighteen removes the sponsor mandate while requiring full DMV vision, written, and road testing instead.

sec03-R01-card.question_text: What must accompany a foreign-language name-change record used for a Driving Privilege Card?
sec03-R01-card.teaching_text: Staff cannot verify foreign legal name changes without a formal English translation alongside the record.

sec03-R02-card.question_text: Which three document types fail as residence proof under the Driving Privilege Card table?
sec03-R02-card.teaching_text: Bringing home-printed bills or greeting cards instead of original business mail triggers an immediate counter rejection.

sec03-R03-card.question_text: Which carrier and date window apply to residence-proof mail for a Driving Privilege Card?
sec03-R03-card.teaching_text: Stale envelopes older than two months or private courier packages fail Delaware's recency and carrier rules.

sec03-R04-card.question_text: What source and address rules govern the two Driving Privilege Card residence proofs?
sec03-R04-card.teaching_text: Two bills from the same company or a post-office box cannot verify where you physically live.

sec03-F04-card.question_text: What are the standard and active-IEP age windows for Delaware's initial graduated learner permit?
sec03-F04-card.teaching_text: Students on an active Individualized Education Program keep graduated-permit access four years past eighteen.

sec03-F05-card.question_text: Which certificate colors prove completion of a Delaware driver education course for a graduated permit?
sec03-F05-card.teaching_text: Handing DMV your school's Blue or White Driver Education Certificate unlocks the teen permit application.

sec03-F06-card.question_text: How can an out-of-state driver education certificate qualify a graduated-permit applicant in Delaware?
sec03-F06-card.teaching_text: Taking a transfer certificate straight to DMV fails unless Delaware's Department of Education approves it first.

sec03-F07-card.question_text: Which core proofs must a regular GDL applicant bring, and when are residence proofs skipped?
sec03-F07-card.teaching_text: Living with a Delaware-licensed sponsor saves teens from hunting down two utility bills in their own name.

sec03-F08-card.question_text: What two sponsor conditions waive the two-document Delaware residence requirement?
sec03-F08-card.teaching_text: Both conditions must hold together because an out-of-state or separate-household parent cannot waive residence proof.

sec03-F09-card.question_text: Whose signature is required on every graduated-license application?
sec03-F09-card.teaching_text: No teen can enter Delaware's graduated program solo without an eligible adult co-signing responsibility.

sec03-F10-card.question_text: Who bears financial responsibility if a graduated-license holder causes damage through negligence?
sec03-F10-card.teaching_text: Co-signing a teen's application puts the sponsor's wallet on the hook alongside the young driver.

sec03-F11-card.question_text: Who decides whether a GDL teen is ready to drive and approves who may supervise?
sec03-F11-card.teaching_text: Even if an adult meets age and license minimums, only sponsor-approved supervisors may oversee practice.

sec03-F12-card.question_text: When is a stepparent legally eligible to sponsor a graduated-license applicant?
sec03-F12-card.teaching_text: Marriage to a biological parent alone never grants sponsorship authority without formal adoption or guardianship.

sec03-F13-card.question_text: Which document verifies a parent listed as a graduated-license sponsor?
sec03-F13-card.teaching_text: DMV checks the raised-seal birth record to confirm the signing adult is named as parent.

sec03-R05-card.question_text: Who is the preferred sponsor when a minor lives with both parents together in Delaware?
sec03-R05-card.teaching_text: When both parents share the Delaware home with the teen, either mother or father tops preference.

sec03-R06-card.question_text: Who may sponsor a minor living with only one parent in Delaware?
sec03-R06-card.teaching_text: Living under one Delaware parent's roof makes that custodial resident parent the natural signing sponsor.

sec03-R07-card.question_text: When a teen lives apart from both parents without a Delaware guardian, which parent may sponsor?
sec03-R07-card.teaching_text: Without a custodial parent or guardian, Delaware looks next to a noncustodial parent living in state.

sec03-R23-card.question_text: How are graduated-license sponsor choices structured in the handbook?
sec03-R23-card.teaching_text: Applicants cannot jump down to alternate adults when a higher-priority eligible parent arrangement exists.

sec03-F14-card.question_text: Which court-recognized adults under Delaware law may act as an applicant's sponsor?
sec03-F14-card.teaching_text: Formal Delaware guardianship or custody orders establish legal authority to sign when parents are unavailable.

sec03-F15-card.question_text: Which two state leaders can approve another suitable person to act as GDL sponsor?
sec03-F15-card.teaching_text: Teens lacking eligible parents or guardians still have a path through high-ranking state approval.

sec03-F16-card.question_text: In whose presence must the sponsor sign the graduated-license application?
sec03-F16-card.teaching_text: Bringing a pre-signed form from home fails unless witnessed directly at the counter by DMV staff.

sec03-F17-card.question_text: What authority does the signing sponsor hold throughout the twelve-month graduated-license period?
sec03-F17-card.teaching_text: Reckless choices or broken house rules let your sponsor cancel your permit at any point.

sec03-F18-card.question_text: Until what birthday can a sponsor still revoke endorsement after a teen finishes GDL?
sec03-F18-card.teaching_text: Earning a Class D card at seventeen does not end parental revocation power before adulthood.

sec03-F19-card.question_text: What license fee, term, and screening apply when submitting a graduated-license application?
sec03-F19-card.teaching_text: Your upfront fifty-dollar fee covers the full eight-year Class D cycle once vision screening clears.

sec03-F20-card.question_text: Who identifies graduated-license students needing disability-related evaluation, training, or equipment for DMV testing?
sec03-F20-card.teaching_text: Classroom and behind-the-wheel instructors spot adaptive equipment needs early and coordinate specialized DMV testing.

sec03-F21-card.question_text: What document must a graduated learner-permit holder carry every time they drive?
sec03-F21-card.teaching_text: Leaving your physical permit in a backpack at home violates permit conditions during any roadside stop.

sec03-F22-card.question_text: What restraint rule applies whenever a graduated learner-permit holder's vehicle is moving?
sec03-F22-card.teaching_text: One unbuckled friend or unrestrained toddler puts a permit holder in instant violation of GDL law.

sec03-F23-card.question_text: May a graduated learner-permit driver use a cell phone, texter, or similar electronic device?
sec03-F23-card.teaching_text: Delaware bans mobile electronics completely for permit holders so novice eyes and minds stay locked on traffic.

sec03-F24-card.question_text: Who may ride with a graduated permit holder during all twelve months, including the family carveout?
sec03-F24-card.teaching_text: Immediate family can fill extra back seats only while the adult supervisor is riding along.

sec03-F25-card.question_text: What minimum age and Class D experience must a mandatory GDL supervisor hold?
sec03-F25-card.teaching_text: Test questions trap teens who confuse adult-permit twenty-one supervisors with GDL's twenty-five and five-year rule.

sec03-F26-card.question_text: Where must the supervising driver sit while a supervised permit holder's car is moving?
sec03-F26-card.teaching_text: Sitting right next to the learner lets the supervisor spot hazards early and coach immediately.

sec03-F27-card.question_text: Who else may sit in the front seat beside the supervisor during mandatory supervision?
sec03-F27-card.teaching_text: Even in a three-across pickup bench, only the learner and supervisor may occupy the front row.

sec03-F28-card.question_text: For how many months after permit issuance must a graduated learner remain supervised on every drive?
sec03-F28-card.teaching_text: Every single mile during months one through six requires your qualified twenty-five-plus supervisor beside you.

sec03-F29-card.question_text: How many total and nighttime practice hours must the sponsor certify during initial supervision?
sec03-F29-card.teaching_text: Ten logged after-dark hours ensure new drivers experience headlight glare and reduced sightlines with coaching.

sec03-F30-card.question_text: Which agency receives the supervised-driving certification, and when is it turned in?
sec03-F30-card.teaching_text: Exam questions catch students who guess DMV instead of filing the fifty-hour certificate with Education.

sec03-R24-card.question_text: Between a Delaware guardian or custodian and an agency-approved suitable adult, who ranks higher as sponsor?
sec03-R24-card.teaching_text: Court-appointed Delaware guardians and custodians stand ahead of Secretary- or Chief-approved sponsors.

sec03-R08-card.question_text: During which daily hours may a graduated permit holder drive unsupervised after the first six months?
sec03-R08-card.teaching_text: Completing six clean supervised months unlocks daytime and evening solo driving before the ten-o'clock curfew.

sec03-R09-card.question_text: After six months, when may a graduated permit holder drive solo between ten at night and six in the morning?
sec03-R09-card.teaching_text: Late-night solo trips stay illegal outside direct routes for worship, jobs, or on-campus school activities.

sec03-R10-card.question_text: How many passengers may ride with an unsupervised graduated permit driver during months seven through twelve?
sec03-R10-card.teaching_text: Each extra teen voice spikes crash risk, so solo driving allows at most one friend.

sec03-R11-card.question_text: During the second six months, when does the immediate-family passenger exception apply?
sec03-R11-card.teaching_text: Driving two siblings to school solo violates your permit because extra family requires an adult supervisor.

sec03-R12-card.question_text: How does Delaware treat a first graduated-permit restriction violation, and how long is the suspension?
sec03-R12-card.teaching_text: Breaking curfew or passenger limits counts legally as driving without a license and suspends you two months.

sec03-R13-card.question_text: How long is the suspension for a subsequent violation of graduated-permit restrictions?
sec03-R13-card.teaching_text: A second permit-rule infraction doubles the penalty from two months off the road to four.

sec03-R14-card.question_text: What conditions let a graduated permit driver under eighteen earn a Class D license after twelve months?
sec03-R14-card.teaching_text: Finishing twelve months converts your permit only while sponsor endorsement holds and privileges stay unblemished.

sec03-R15-card.question_text: What two paths let a graduated permit holder aged eighteen or older earn a Class D license?
sec03-R15-card.teaching_text: Eighteen-year-olds can either finish the twelve-month sponsored track or test out through DMV vision, written, and road exams.

sec03-R16-card.question_text: What happens to a graduated learner permit after twelve full months of valid driving authority?
sec03-R16-card.teaching_text: Keeping valid driving status for a full year upgrades your permit to Class D automatically.

sec03-R17-card.question_text: Does time spent suspended, revoked, canceled, denied, or surrendered count toward the required twelve months?
sec03-R17-card.teaching_text: Any period without active driving authority freezes your twelve-month graduation clock until privileges resume.

sec03-R18-card.question_text: What two requirements apply if a graduated permit holder's privileges were suspended, revoked, canceled, denied, or surrendered?
sec03-R18-card.teaching_text: Losing privileges forces you to add equal valid driving months and pass full testing.

sec03-R19-card.question_text: Which two screenings must a first-time adult applicant pass to receive a learner permit?
sec03-R19-card.teaching_text: Clearing the eye chart and written rules test unlocks supervised behind-the-wheel practice for adults.
