sec07-R93-card.teaching_text: Ninety-day advance renewal reminders line up cleanly with Delaware's ninety-day early-inspection window.
sec07-R93-card.must_match_memory_hook: Ninety days via mail, email, phone

visual_sync.text_span: Ninety days via mail, email, phone

sec07-R94-card.question_text: Within how many days and to which DMV sections must you report a Delaware address change?
sec07-R94-card.teaching_text: Updating only your driver license leaves registration renewal and insurance-audit mail going to your old address.

sec07-R95-card.question_text: How can you update a registration address, and what fee applies to the replacement card in the written process?
sec07-R95-card.teaching_text: Writing to Vehicle Services updates your registration address and mails a replacement card at zero cost.

sec07-R96-card.question_text: After a legal name change, which card must be updated first and how many days do you have for title and registration?
sec07-R96-card.teaching_text: Change your driver license first so your ID matches when applying for replacement title and registration within thirty days.

sec07-R97-card.question_text: Which four documents are required to update your name on a Delaware vehicle record?
sec07-R97-card.teaching_text: Bring your marriage certificate or court order alongside existing title, prior registration, and active insurance proof.

sec07-R98-card.question_text: How much do replacement title and registration cost for a name change without a lien versus with a lien?
sec07-R98-card.teaching_text: Name-change title replacements match standard Delaware title fees at thirty-five dollars clear or fifty-five with a lien.

sec07-R99-card.question_text: How far outside Delaware must a resident be temporarily living to qualify for mail registration renewal?
sec07-R99-card.teaching_text: College students or temporary assignees stationed over two hundred miles outside Delaware can renew tags by mail.

sec07-R100-card.question_text: Which two vehicle documents must stay with the car every time it is driven?
sec07-R100-card.teaching_text: Never carry your paper vehicle title in the glovebox—keep only the registration card and liability insurance proof.

sec07-R101-card.question_text: Where must the license plate and its expiration sticker be mounted on the vehicle?
sec07-R101-card.teaching_text: Sticking your renewal decal in the wrong corner makes the tag look expired at a glance.

sec07-R102-card.question_text: At what exact time does Delaware vehicle registration expire, and is there any grace period?
sec07-R102-card.teaching_text: Driving past midnight on your sticker date risks immediate citations because Delaware grants zero registration grace days.

sec09-F01-card.question_text: What does Delaware law require if you want to hold a phone conversation while driving?
sec09-F01-card.teaching_text: Holding a phone or typing steals both your vision and steering grip, making hands-free audio the only legal option for licensed adult drivers.

sec09-F02-card.question_text: What must a driver immediately do after dialing, activating, or turning off wireless equipment?
sec09-F02-card.teaching_text: Delaware allows a brief touch to initiate or end wireless service, yet keeping the phone in your hand afterward turns into an illegal handheld violation.

sec09-F03-card.question_text: Besides cell phones, which other handheld electronic communication devices are restricted while driving?
sec09-F03-card.teaching_text: Test questions often swap a cell phone for a laptop or pager, hoping you forget that every handheld electronic messaging gadget is equally barred.

sec09-F04-card.question_text: May a driver holding a Graduated Driver License use a hands-free phone or electronic device while driving?
sec09-F04-card.teaching_text: New drivers face the highest distraction crash risk, so GDL holders are barred from all phone or electronic use behind the wheel, including Bluetooth.

sec09-F05-card.question_text: Which urgent situations or roles are exempted from Delaware's driving device-use ban?
sec09-F05-card.teaching_text: Lawmakers carve out urgent 911 reporting and on-duty emergency operators so life-saving calls are never delayed by handheld enforcement.

sec09-F06-card.question_text: Which farm-vehicle operators and radio users are specifically exempted from the electronic device restriction?
sec09-F06-card.teaching_text: Agricultural field equipment and licensed amateur radio operators rely on specialized communications that Delaware explicitly excludes from the distracted-driving statute.

sec09-F07-card.question_text: When may a business or government worker legally use a two-way radio while operating a vehicle?
sec09-F07-card.teaching_text: Fleet and municipal workers can talk with dispatch or coworkers only when the two-way unit is attached or mounted inside the vehicle.

sec09-F08-card.question_text: How far ahead must you give a hand or turn signal before stopping, turning, or changing lanes?
sec09-F08-card.teaching_text: Delaware's 300-foot rule is longer than many states' 100-foot distance, making this exact number a favorite permit-test trap.

sec09-F09-card.question_text: When overtaking another vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
sec09-F09-card.teaching_text: Cutting back too early clips the front bumper of the vehicle you just passed or forces its driver to slam on the brakes.

sec09-F10-card.question_text: What minimum lateral clearance must you maintain throughout the entire pass around a bicyclist?
sec09-F10-card.teaching_text: Wind buffeting or a sudden pothole swerve can knock a rider down if your mirror skims closer than three feet.

sec09-F11-card.question_text: How must you pass a cyclist on a multilane road whenever traffic conditions allow?
sec09-F11-card.teaching_text: Moving fully into the adjacent lane gives a rider maximum cushion instead of squeezing past inside the same shared travel lane.

sec09-F12-card.question_text: What must you do with your lane position and speed when another driver is overtaking you?
sec09-F12-card.teaching_text: Speeding up while someone passes strands the overtaking car in oncoming traffic and turns a routine pass into a head-on hazard.

sec09-F13-card.question_text: How must you respond to an approaching emergency vehicle using a siren or alternating red lights unless an officer directs otherwise?
sec09-F13-card.teaching_text: Stopping inside a junction blocks the responder's turn path, so move immediately to the right curb clear of cross streets until it passes.

sec09-F14-card.question_text: Which transportation-agency operators are also covered by the approaching-emergency-vehicle yield law during an incident?
sec09-F14-card.teaching_text: Highway response trucks rushing to assist police or firefighters carry emergency protection so crews can secure crash scenes quickly.

sec09-F15-card.question_text: What is your primary duty when approaching a stopped emergency, DelDOT, tow, or warning-displaying vehicle on the roadside?
sec09-F15-card.teaching_text: Roadside responders work inches from live traffic, so vacating the adjacent lane whenever possible prevents deadly shoulder strikes.

sec09-F16-card.question_text: What must you do under the move-over law if changing lanes is unsafe or impossible?
sec09-F16-card.teaching_text: Never force a blind swerve into neighboring cars; instead drop to a safe reduced speed and stay alert past the roadside crew.

sec09-F17-card.question_text: Which alternating warning-light color combinations trigger the move-over rule for stationary emergency vehicles?
sec09-F17-card.teaching_text: Police, fire, and ambulance fleets run red, blue, or paired white strobes, and every one of those alternating patterns commands move-over protection.

sec09-F18-card.question_text: Which alternating light colors identify a stationary DelDOT vehicle under the move-over law?
sec09-F18-card.teaching_text: Drivers sometimes ignore amber highway-maintenance strobes, forgetting that stopped DelDOT trucks carry the exact same move-over mandate as police cruisers.

sec09-F19-card.question_text: Which alternating warning lights on a stationary tow truck require drivers to move over or slow down?
sec09-F19-card.teaching_text: Winching a disabled car puts tow operators directly on the lane line, so flashing amber or white beacons demand immediate lane clearance.

sec09-F20-card.question_text: Which roadside signals on any ordinary stopped vehicle also trigger Delaware's move-over requirement?
sec09-F20-card.teaching_text: Delaware protects stranded motorists changing a flat tire just like first responders whenever hazards, flares, cones, or warning markers are out.

sec09-F21-card.question_text: How must you position your car when passing a protected stopped vehicle on a multilane roadway?
sec09-F21-card.teaching_text: Holding the farther lane until you are fully past the scene keeps wide mirrors and wind blast away from people on the shoulder.

sec09-F22-card.question_text: What speed adjustment is required when passing a stopped roadside vehicle on a two-lane road?
sec09-F22-card.teaching_text: Without an extra same-direction lane to shift into, reducing speed below the posted limit is your main safeguard until completely past.

sec09-F23-card.question_text: Which groups of roadway users are bound by Delaware traffic laws on public highways?
sec09-F23-card.teaching_text: Predictable traffic flow works only when everyone sharing the right-of-way follows uniform rules, whether behind a steering wheel, on handlebars, or on foot.

sec09-F24-card.question_text: What must you do when a police officer's hand direction conflicts with a traffic light, sign, or pavement marking?
sec09-F24-card.teaching_text: Live officers see crashes, blocked lanes, or emergency convoys that automated signals cannot detect, so human police commands always win.

sec09-F25-card.question_text: Is it legal to cut through a gas station or private lot to avoid waiting at a traffic sign or red light?
sec09-F25-card.teaching_text: Dodging an intersection through a corner parking lot surprises pedestrians and store customers where nobody expects fast through-traffic.

sec09-F26-card.question_text: What emergency contact resource is posted at every railroad grade crossing?
sec09-F26-card.teaching_text: Calling the railroad directly reaches train dispatchers faster than general channels when a vehicle stalls or a gate malfunctions on the rails.

sec09-F27-card.question_text: Where do you normally find the railroad emergency notification phone number at a crossing?
sec09-F27-card.teaching_text: Knowing to scan the crossbuck post for the blue ENS plaque saves precious seconds if a car gets stuck on the rails.

sec09-F28-card.question_text: What information on the blue ENS sign pinpoints the exact railroad crossing for responders and rail crews?
sec09-F28-card.teaching_text: Rural and suburban tracks look identical for miles, so the unique DOT crossing code tells dispatchers the exact intersection instantly.

sec09-F29-card.question_text: How does reading the crossing's DOT number to the railroad dispatcher help prevent a train collision?
sec09-F29-card.teaching_text: Freight and passenger trains need massive braking distance, so immediate location data lets dispatchers radio approaching engineers before arrival.

sec09-F30-card.question_text: Should you ever try to beat an approaching train across a railroad grade crossing?
sec09-F30-card.teaching_text: Large locomotives create an optical illusion that makes them appear slower and farther away than they truly are.

sec09-F31-card.question_text: When must you wait before starting across railroad tracks even if no train is currently visible?
sec09-F31-card.teaching_text: Queueing bumper-to-bumper behind a red light ahead can trap your rear bumper on the rails with nowhere to escape when bells start ringing.

sec09-F32-card.question_text: Why does the Delaware handbook advise against shifting gears while crossing railroad tracks?
sec09-F32-card.teaching_text: Missing a shift or popping the clutch mid-crossing can stall your engine right across live rails.

sec09-F33-card.question_text: What shape, color, and markings identify an advance railroad-crossing warning sign?
sec09-F33-card.teaching_text: Round yellow geometry appears nowhere else on the road, giving you an unmistakable early cue to listen and prepare to stop.

sec09-F34-card.question_text: Which three elements commonly appear in advance pavement markings before a railroad crossing?
sec09-F34-card.teaching_text: Pavement symbols reinforce roadside signs right in your sightline and mark the exact line where your front bumper must halt.

sec09-F35-card.question_text: Which standard traffic sign shares the exact same legal meaning as a white X-shaped railroad crossbuck?
sec09-F35-card.teaching_text: Many learners treat a passive crossbuck as mere decoration, missing the exam fact that it legally commands yielding to any train.

sec09-F36-card.question_text: What action is required when side-by-side red lights begin flashing at a railroad crossing?
sec09-F36-card.teaching_text: Alternating red crossing beacons mean a train is closing fast, making a complete stop mandatory before the gate even drops.

sec09-F37-card.question_text: May you weave around a lowered railroad crossing gate if you do not see a train coming?
sec09-F37-card.teaching_text: Driving around a gate arms you against fast trains hidden by curves, trees, or a train that just passed on a nearer track.

sec09-F38-card.question_text: When a railroad crossing bell is ringing, how long must you wait before driving across?
sec09-F38-card.teaching_text: Continuing bell chimes warn that a second train may be approaching from the opposite direction even after the first caboose clears.

sec09-F39-card.question_text: What does a track-count plaque warn you about, and what should you verify even if none is posted?
sec09-F39-card.teaching_text: One departing train easily hides a second fast train on an adjacent set of rails, so verify every track is clear before moving.

sec09-F40-card.question_text: What part of the roadway is marked by a solid white line along the right side?
sec09-F40-card.teaching_text: Fog lines guide your peripheral vision at night against oncoming glare so you do not drift onto soft shoulders.

sec09-F41-card.question_text: What direction of traffic flow is separated by white lane markings?
sec09-F41-card.teaching_text: Checking stripe color tells you instantly whether the lane beside you flows with you or carries head-on opposing vehicles.

sec09-F42-card.question_text: When may you cross a broken white line between travel lanes?
sec09-F42-card.teaching_text: Dashed white paint signals open lane movement once mirrors, blind spots, and a 300-foot turn signal confirm clear space.

sec09-F43-card.question_text: What does a single solid white line between same-direction lanes tell drivers about changing lanes?
sec09-F43-card.teaching_text: Engineers paint single solid white lines near intersections and merges where last-second weaving sparks sideswipe crashes.

sec09-F44-card.question_text: What is the legal rule for crossing a double solid white line between lanes?
sec09-F44-card.teaching_text: Unlike a single solid white stripe that merely discourages movement, paired solid white lines create a strict legal barrier against lane changes.

sec09-F45-card.question_text: Where must your vehicle come to rest when a sign or traffic signal requires a stop?
sec09-F45-card.teaching_text: Rolling over the painted stop bar pushes your hood right into pedestrian walking lanes and cross-traffic turning arcs.

sec09-F46-card.question_text: Do crosswalks only exist where white lines are painted across the pavement?
sec09-F46-card.teaching_text: Sidewalk extensions create legal unmarked crosswalks at intersections, so drivers cannot use missing paint as an excuse for failing to yield.

sec09-F47-card.question_text: What does yellow center-line paint tell you about the traffic on the other side of the line?
sec09-F47-card.teaching_text: Spotting yellow on your left prevents turning onto a two-way road as if it were a one-way street.

sec09-F48-card.question_text: When is a driver allowed to cross a single broken yellow center line?
sec09-F48-card.teaching_text: Dashed yellow indicates sightlines are long enough to overtake, provided oncoming pavement ahead is completely clear.

sec09-F49-card.question_text: May you cross center lines to pass when the solid yellow stripe is on your side and the broken stripe is opposite?
sec09-F49-card.teaching_text: Hills and curves block sight distance asymmetrically, so a solid stripe on your side warns you cannot see oncoming cars far enough ahead.
sec09-F49-card.must_match_memory_hook: Solid side on yours forbids passing

visual_sync.text_span: Solid side on yours forbids passing

sec09-F50-card.question_text: When a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line sit side by side, which direction of traffic may pass?
sec09-F50-card.teaching_text: Having the dashed stripe closest to your tires confirms open sight distance for your direction once oncoming traffic clears.

sec09-F51-card.question_text: What passing rule applies where two solid yellow lines divide the roadway?
sec09-F51-card.teaching_text: Paired solid yellow lines lock down passing for both directions wherever blind hills, curves, or heavy driveways make overtaking perilous.

sec09-F52-card.question_text: When is it legal to cross a solid yellow line on the roadway?
sec09-F52-card.teaching_text: Permit questions love testing that solid yellow bans overtaking slower cars yet still lets you turn safely into a private driveway.

sec09-F53-card.question_text: How are reversible rush-hour lanes normally marked on the pavement, and what must you verify before entering?
sec09-F53-card.teaching_text: Because direction flips between morning and evening commutes, entering paired dashed yellow lanes without reading overhead signals risks a head-on crash.

sec09-F54-card.question_text: What does a downward green arrow displayed over a reversible lane indicate?
sec09-F54-card.teaching_text: Overhead lane-control gantries override guesswork during rush hour by confirming that traffic in your direction owns that lane right now.

sec09-F55-card.question_text: What does a steady red X over a reversible lane command?
sec09-F55-card.teaching_text: A red X warns that oncoming commuters or emergency crews hold that lane, so never enter it even briefly to pass.

sec09-F56-card.question_text: What must you do when an overhead lane signal displays a steady yellow X?
sec09-F56-card.teaching_text: A steady yellow X signals that lane direction is about to flip to red, giving you a brief window to merge out safely.

sec09-F57-card.question_text: Who may use lanes marked Transit or Bus, and who may use lanes marked Bicycle?
sec09-F57-card.teaching_text: Keeping cars out of dedicated bus and bike corridors prevents right-hook collisions and keeps public transit moving on schedule.

sec09-F58-card.question_text: What two details do HOV lane signs post, and how many occupants are needed for an HOV 3 lane?
sec09-F58-card.teaching_text: Carpool signs specify both active hours and minimum headcount, so driving solo during restricted times draws an immediate lane citation.

sec09-F59-card.question_text: In which direction does all traffic circulate around the central island of a roundabout?
sec09-F59-card.teaching_text: Every entry curves right into a one-way counterclockwise ring, eliminating high-speed left-turn T-bone angles.

sec09-R01-card.question_text: Which approach lane should you pick before a two-lane roundabout for a right turn, left turn, U-turn, or straight path?
sec09-R01-card.teaching_text: Choosing your lane before entering prevents dangerous mid-circle lane changes, while straight-through traffic can use either approach lane.
sec09-R01-card.must_match_memory_hook: Right turns right, left turns left

visual_sync.text_span: Right turns right, left turns left

sec09-R02-card.question_text: Which side of the splitter island do you pass on, and to what speed should you slow when approaching a roundabout?
sec09-R02-card.teaching_text: Dropping to a calm 10 to 15 miles per hour beside the right of the splitter island gives everyone time to merge smoothly.

sec09-R03-card.question_text: How should you treat bicyclists as you approach a roundabout entrance?
sec09-R03-card.teaching_text: Bike lanes often end at the circle ramp, so riders legitimately take the full travel lane through the roundabout for visibility.

sec09-R04-card.question_text: Who has priority at the pedestrian crosswalk set back from a roundabout entrance?
sec09-R04-card.teaching_text: Roundabout crosswalks sit one car-length back from the yield line so you can stop for walkers first before scanning circular traffic.

sec09-R05-card.question_text: Who must yield when an approaching vehicle meets vehicles already circulating inside a roundabout?
sec09-R05-card.teaching_text: Looking left and waiting for a safe gap in circulating traffic keeps the circle flowing without gridlock.

sec09-R06-card.question_text: Once you are circulating inside a roundabout, when is stopping appropriate?
sec09-R06-card.teaching_text: Halting politely inside the circle to wave an entering car forward causes instant rear-end pileups behind you.

sec09-R07-card.question_text: May you overtake or pass another vehicle while traveling inside a roundabout?
sec09-R07-card.teaching_text: Curved lanes and frequent exits shrink side visibility, so passing inside a roundabout invites immediate sideswipes across exit paths.

sec09-R08-card.question_text: Which vulnerable road users must you watch for and yield to as you exit a roundabout?
sec09-R08-card.teaching_text: Drivers accelerating out of a roundabout often fixate down the road and miss people stepping into the exit-leg crosswalk.

sec09-R09-card.question_text: Why does a diverging diamond interchange temporarily shift traffic onto the left side of the road?
sec09-R09-card.teaching_text: Crossing traffic to the left between two signalized crossovers lets drivers turn left onto highway ramps without cutting across oncoming lanes.

sec09-R10-card.question_text: Which maneuvers are permitted from a shared center turn lane, and by which directions of traffic?
sec09-R10-card.teaching_text: Shared two-way left-turn lanes buffer turning cars out of fast through-lanes, serving left turns and legal U-turns from both directions.

sec09-R11-card.question_text: What arrow pattern and yellow boundary lines identify a shared center left-turn lane?
sec09-R11-card.teaching_text: Solid outer yellow lines with dashed inner yellow lines and opposing arrows distinguish a two-way turn pocket from a reversible lane.

sec09-R12-card.question_text: What rush-hour operational change can affect a shared center lane before you pull into it?
sec09-R12-card.teaching_text: Some corridors convert center turn lanes into one-way commute lanes at peak hours, so always verify overhead signs before entering.

sec09-R13-card.question_text: What are the only two exceptions that allow reversing inside an active travel lane?
sec09-R13-card.teaching_text: Drivers behind you never expect reverse lights in a moving lane, making backing illegal except when parallel parking or exiting a driveway.

sec09-R14-card.question_text: What should you do if you accidentally drive past your intended turn or highway exit?
sec09-R14-card.teaching_text: Backing up on a ramp or highway shoulder causes catastrophic high-speed rear-end crashes; taking the next exit costs only minutes.

sec09-R15-card.question_text: May you stop inside an active travel lane if you get lost, experience a breakdown, or let out a passenger?
sec09-R15-card.teaching_text: Stationary cars in live lanes trigger chain-reaction collisions, so keep rolling onto a safe shoulder or lot whenever your car can move.

sec09-R16-card.question_text: Which lane should you normally travel in when a road has two or more lanes moving in the same direction?
sec09-R16-card.teaching_text: Camping in the left lane forces faster drivers to weave on the right and builds dangerous tailgating clusters.

sec09-R17-card.question_text: Which lane is recommended on a three-or-more-lane highway when heavy traffic is merging on and exiting off?
sec09-R17-card.teaching_text: Holding the middle lane leaves the right lane open for ramp merges and the far-left lane clear for overtaking.

sec09-R18-card.question_text: What is the intended purpose of the far-left lane on a multilane highway?
sec09-R18-card.teaching_text: Treating the leftmost lane strictly as a passing corridor keeps traffic sorted by speed and reduces road-rage bottlenecks.

sec09-R19-card.question_text: Does Delaware allow passing a left-turning vehicle on its right side?
sec09-R19-card.teaching_text: Oncoming left-turners or hidden cross-traffic may not see you emerging around the stopped car, demanding extra vigilance.

sec09-R20-card.question_text: Unlike many states, what does Delaware allow regarding the paved shoulder when passing a left-turning vehicle on the right?
sec09-R20-card.teaching_text: Because opposing drivers turning across the gap rarely expect a car on the right shoulder, proceed slowly and scan every angle.

sec09-R21-card.question_text: When no signs or arrows direct otherwise, which lane must you start a turn from and finish in?
sec09-R21-card.teaching_text: Turning curb-to-curb or median-to-median crosses the fewest conflict paths and keeps adjacent lanes predictable.

sec09-R22-card.question_text: If you need a different lane after turning at an intersection, when should you make that lane change?
sec09-R22-card.teaching_text: Drifting across lane stripes mid-intersection cuts off drivers turning beside you or making a legal right turn from the cross street.

sec09-R23-card.question_text: Which two steering errors must you avoid before and during a right turn?
sec09-R23-card.teaching_text: Swinging left fakes out drivers behind you into passing on your right, while swinging wide enters oncoming or adjacent lanes.

sec09-R24-card.question_text: Why must you avoid cutting a left turn sharply across the corner of the cross street?
sec09-R24-card.teaching_text: Clipping the inside corner puts your front bumper nose-to-nose with cross-street cars waiting at the stop line and blocks opposing left-turners.

sec09-R25-card.question_text: What lane-keeping rule applies when two or more side-by-side lanes are marked to turn together?
sec09-R25-card.teaching_text: Side-by-side turning cars sit right in each other's blind spots, so drifting across dashed turn guides causes instant fender-benders.

sec09-R26-card.question_text: May everyday motorists turn around using a highway median opening posted for emergency vehicles only?
sec09-R26-card.teaching_text: Short unpaved or narrow turnarounds lack deceleration lanes, turning a civilian U-turn into a high-speed left-lane collision.

sec09-R27-card.question_text: Which side of a legal median crossover opening must you stay on unless signs direct otherwise?
sec09-R27-card.teaching_text: Staying to the right side of a wide median crossover prevents head-on tangles with drivers turning simultaneously from the opposite highway.

sec09-R28-card.question_text: Does having technical right-of-way ever excuse failing to avoid a preventable crash with a vehicle or pedestrian?
sec09-R28-card.teaching_text: Delaware law treats right-of-way as something others yield to you, never a license to plow ahead when someone makes a mistake.

sec09-R29-card.question_text: What must drivers do whenever yielding is necessary to avoid striking pedestrians crossing the street?
sec09-R29-card.teaching_text: Steel frames versus unprotected human bodies leave zero margin for stubbornness, even if a walker misjudged the signal.

sec09-R30-card.question_text: Who holds right-of-way when your car crosses a sidewalk into or out of a lot, alley, or driveway?
sec09-R30-card.teaching_text: Sidewalks belong to foot traffic first, so pause before the concrete apron rather than rolling out to the street curb first.

sec09-R31-card.question_text: When is a motor vehicle legally allowed on a sidewalk?
sec09-R31-card.teaching_text: Crossing perpendicularly into a legal driveway is permitted, whereas driving lengthwise down a walkway endangers everyone on foot.

sec09-R32-card.question_text: What priority belongs to a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, and why must you never honk?
sec09-R32-card.teaching_text: Blind pedestrians navigate by traffic sound cues, so blasting your horn startles service dogs and scrambles directional orientation.

sec09-R33-card.question_text: Who must yield when a driver turning left meets oncoming traffic continuing straight?
sec09-R33-card.teaching_text: Misjudging oncoming speed during a left turn is a leading intersection crash cause; wait for a generous, unmistakable gap.

sec09-R34-card.question_text: Who has right-of-way when entering a traffic circle or rotary?
sec09-R34-card.teaching_text: Just like modern roundabouts, vehicles already circulating inside a rotary hold priority over drivers waiting at entry legs.

sec09-R35-card.question_text: At an intersection with no signs or signals, who gets right-of-way and what extra precaution does the handbook advise?
sec09-R35-card.teaching_text: Yielding to traffic on your right settles legal priority, while checking every approach protects you from drivers who miss the rule.

sec09-R36-card.question_text: Who proceeds first at a four-way stop when vehicles arrive at slightly different times?
sec09-R36-card.teaching_text: Arrival order still requires a complete wheel halt first; rolling through because you got there earliest remains a stop-sign violation.

sec09-R37-card.question_text: Which vehicle proceeds first when two drivers reach a four-way stop at the exact same moment?
sec09-R37-card.teaching_text: Yielding to the driver on your right resolves simultaneous arrivals cleanly without hesitant hand-wave standoffs.

sec09-R38-card.question_text: Who must yield when a vehicle pulls onto a street from a driveway, alley, or roadside shoulder?
sec09-R38-card.teaching_text: Main-road drivers travel at full cruising speed, so anyone merging out of a private drive or shoulder must wait for clear lanes.

sec09-R39-card.question_text: What must drivers entering a roadway from a dedicated turn-only lane be prepared to do?
sec09-R39-card.teaching_text: Channelized turn lanes rarely guarantee a free merge lane ahead, requiring you to yield and halt whenever cross traffic is close.

sec09-R40-card.question_text: When must you stay behind the stop line even though the traffic signal ahead is green?
sec09-R40-card.teaching_text: Pulling into backed-up traffic traps your car perpendicular to cross streets when the light changes, paralyzing emergency and cross flow.

sec09-R41-card.question_text: What duty falls on a driver overtaking another vehicle traveling in the same direction if the lead car slows or stops?
sec09-R41-card.teaching_text: Lead drivers may brake suddenly for pedestrians, animals, or turns, so the following or passing driver carries the duty to avoid contact.

sec09-R42-card.question_text: How must you yield to an emergency vehicle using an air horn, siren, flashing red or blue light, or loudspeaker?
sec09-R42-card.teaching_text: Emergency crews sometimes need the right turn pocket or a specific lane, so keep windows quiet enough to hear PA instructions.

sec09-R43-card.question_text: What should you do if you are already inside an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches?
sec09-R43-card.teaching_text: Freezing mid-junction turns your car into an obstacle right where the fire truck or ambulance needs room to swing wide.

sec09-R44-card.question_text: When is opposing traffic not required to stop for a loading school bus in Delaware, and how must those drivers proceed?
sec09-R44-card.teaching_text: Delaware's four-or-more-lane highway rule is classic exam gold, letting opposing lanes roll slowly without stopping.

sec09-R45-card.question_text: How many seconds before flashing red lights do a school bus's overhead yellow lights activate?
sec09-R45-card.teaching_text: Ten seconds of alternating yellow warns you to brake smoothly right away instead of accelerating to beat the stop arm.

sec09-R46-card.question_text: Which two clues confirm you may cautiously proceed after stopping for a school bus?
sec09-R46-card.teaching_text: Children frequently drop papers or dart back near the bumper, so wait until flashing reds stop and the stop arm folds flat.

sec09-R47-card.question_text: Who is legally presumed responsible if a witness reports a car passing a stopped school bus and the driver cannot be identified?
sec09-R47-card.teaching_text: Bus drivers and crossing guards record license plates first, placing legal responsibility squarely on the vehicle's registered owner.

sec09-R48-card.question_text: What fine range applies to a first conviction for passing a stopped school bus with red lights and stop arm active?
sec09-R48-card.teaching_text: Passing active red bus lights triggers steep mandatory statutory fines starting at $115 on the very first conviction.

sec09-R49-card.question_text: How much jail time can be imposed on a first conviction for illegally passing a stopped school bus?
sec09-R49-card.teaching_text: Courts can impose one to two months behind bars either instead of or right alongside the monetary fine.

sec09-R50-card.question_text: What fine range applies to a repeat stopped-school-bus passing conviction within three years?
sec09-R50-card.teaching_text: Picking up a similar bus-stop conviction inside a three-year window more than doubles the top fine ceiling to $575.

sec09-R51-card.question_text: What imprisonment range applies to a subsequent stopped-school-bus passing offense within three years?
sec09-R51-card.teaching_text: Repeat disregard for loading schoolchildren escalates jail exposure from sixty days all the way up to half a year.

sec09-R52-card.question_text: How long is your license suspended upon a first conviction for passing a stopped school bus with flashing red lights?
sec09-R52-card.teaching_text: Even a single lapse around a stopped school bus immediately strips your driving privileges for a full month.

sec09-R53-card.question_text: What suspension length applies to a second school-bus stop violation within three years?
sec09-R53-card.teaching_text: The penalty table jumps sixfold from one month to six months if a second violation happens within three years.

sec09-R54-card.question_text: How long does the conviction table suspend a driver for a third or later school-bus violation within three years?
sec09-R54-card.teaching_text: Three school-bus convictions inside three years sideline your license for an entire twelve-month stretch.

sec09-R55-card.question_text: After a second school-bus conviction, how long must you serve with zero driving authority before qualifying for a conditional license?
sec09-R55-card.teaching_text: Half of the six-month second-offense suspension is a hard lockout with zero hardship or work driving allowed.

sec09-R56-card.question_text: After a third or later school-bus offense, how long must you go without any driving authority before a conditional license is possible?
sec09-R56-card.teaching_text: During a one-year third-offense suspension, no restricted driving authority can be granted during the first six months.

sec09-R57-card.question_text: Can you obtain a conditional or hardship license during the one-month suspension for a first school-bus offense?
sec09-R57-card.teaching_text: Unlike longer repeat suspensions that allow later conditional relief, the entire one-month first suspension carries zero driving authority.

sec09-R58-card.question_text: What civil dollar penalty applies to a first ticket under the Red Clay school-bus camera pilot?
sec09-R58-card.teaching_text: Stop-arm cameras capture plate violations automatically and issue a $100 civil administrative assessment on the first offense.

sec09-R59-card.question_text: What civil assessment applies to each subsequent violation within ten years under the school-bus camera pilot?
sec09-R59-card.teaching_text: Unlike the three-year criminal lookback, the camera pilot tracks repeat violations across ten years and charges $500 each time.

sec09-R60-card.question_text: How much can be added to a school-bus camera pilot assessment left unpaid for twenty days?
sec09-R60-card.teaching_text: Ignoring a mailed stop-arm camera notice past twenty days starts stacking extra administrative late fees onto the base assessment.

sec09-R61-card.question_text: What is the maximum late-payment fee after forty-five days under the school-bus camera pilot?
sec09-R61-card.teaching_text: Letting an unpaid camera citation pass the forty-five-day mark doubles the late-payment ceiling up to twenty dollars.

sec09-R62-card.question_text: What maximum late-payment charge applies once a school-bus camera assessment goes unpaid past ninety days?
sec09-R62-card.teaching_text: At ninety days overdue, the late-payment surcharge hits its top statutory ceiling of thirty dollars.

sec09-R63-card.question_text: Up to how much in court or administrative costs may be added after losing a camera-pilot hearing or missing the deadline?
sec09-R63-card.teaching_text: Failing to pay or contest on time, or losing a contested hearing, allows up to thirty-five dollars in extra administrative costs.

sec09-R64-card.question_text: Does a civilly assessed school-bus camera pilot ticket count as criminal or affect your driving record and insurance?
sec09-R64-card.teaching_text: Camera-issued owner assessments carry steep dollar bills yet stay civil, staying off both your DMV point record and insurance rates.

sec10-F01-card.question_text: Which four securing steps are required before walking away from a car parked on a street?
sec10-F01-card.teaching_text: Shutting off power, locking the ignition, taking your key, and setting the brake prevent rollaways and joyride thefts.

sec10-F02-card.question_text: What two additional precautions does the Delaware handbook recommend when leaving a parked car?
sec10-F02-card.teaching_text: Even with the ignition locked, cracked windows or unlocked latches invite cabin break-ins and stolen registration papers.

sec10-F03-card.question_text: How close to the curb or road edge must you park parallel on a two-way highway?
sec10-F03-card.teaching_text: Parking more than a foot away leaves your street-side fenders sticking out into active travel lanes and bike paths.

sec10-F04-card.question_text: What should you do before parallel parking if you check your mirror and spot a car following too closely?
sec10-F04-card.teaching_text: Braking abruptly next to an open curb space when someone rides your bumper sets up an immediate rear-end crash.

sec10-F05-card.question_text: How do you line up your car to begin parallel parking into a curb space?
sec10-F05-card.teaching_text: Matching your rear bumper with the lead vehicle's rear bumper sets the exact pivot point needed to swing cleanly into the gap.

sec10-F06-card.question_text: Which way do you steer while reversing first into a right-side parallel-parking space, and where do you aim?
sec10-F06-card.teaching_text: Turning right in reverse angles your tail smoothly into the open bay toward the parked vehicle behind the space.

sec10-F07-card.question_text: Once your front bumper clears the car ahead during right-curb parallel parking, how do you steer?
sec10-F07-card.teaching_text: Counter-steering sharply left tucks your nose behind the lead car without scraping its rear bumper or jumping the curb.

sec10-F08-card.question_text: How do you complete a parallel-parking maneuver once your car is inside the space?
sec10-F08-card.teaching_text: Centering between both cars leaves exit room for neighbors, while Park and the parking brake lock the car on any grade.

sec10-F09-card.question_text: Is it legal in Delaware to leave keys inside a running, unattended vehicle?
sec10-F09-card.teaching_text: Warming up an unattended car in winter or dashing into a store invites opportunistic theft in seconds and draws a ticket.

sec10-F10-card.question_text: How do the steering inputs change when parallel parking along the left curb of a one-way street?
sec10-F10-card.teaching_text: Approaching a left-side curb mirrors the geometry, so cut left first into the bay and counter-steer right once clear.

sec10-F11-card.question_text: Which gear should a manual-transmission vehicle be left in when parked facing uphill?
sec10-F11-card.teaching_text: Engaging first or low gear uses engine compression to resist rolling backward if the handbrake cable ever slackens.

sec10-F12-card.question_text: Which gear should you select before leaving a manual-transmission vehicle parked facing downhill?
sec10-F12-card.teaching_text: Selecting reverse opposes forward gravity on a downgrade, backing up the parking brake mechanically.

sec10-F13-card.question_text: What sequence must you follow before pulling out of a parallel-parking space into traffic?
sec10-F13-card.teaching_text: Passing cars and cyclists hold right-of-way in the active lane, so signal early, check blind spots, and merge out gradually.

sec10-F14-card.question_text: Which two credentials legally authorize parking in a designated accessible space?
sec10-F14-card.teaching_text: Accessible bays keep wide transfer zones open near building ramps, and parking there without a plate or hanging ID draws steep fines.

sec10-F15-card.question_text: What lighting must a vehicle parked along a highway display between sunset and sunrise?
sec10-F15-card.teaching_text: Unlit dark steel along an unlit shoulder disappears at highway speeds until oncoming headlights are too close to swerve.

sec10-F16-card.question_text: At what daytime visibility threshold must a vehicle parked along a highway turn on parking lights or four-way flashers?
sec10-F16-card.teaching_text: Heavy fog, rain, or snow hides roadside cars during daylight whenever people or objects are unclear at one thousand feet.

sec10-F17-card.question_text: May a parked vehicle leave a single-side turn signal blinking while stationary?
sec10-F17-card.teaching_text: A single blinking directional tricks approaching motorists into thinking you are actively pulling out or turning.

sec10-F18-card.question_text: When is stopping on the paved travel portion of a highway outside business or residential areas allowed, and where must you position the car?
sec10-F18-card.teaching_text: High-speed rural lanes leave no expectation of parked cars, so pull completely off pavement unless a breakdown immobilizes your car.

sec10-F19-card.question_text: Which way must you turn your front wheels when parking facing downhill?
sec10-F19-card.teaching_text: Whether a raised curb or open shoulder sits beside you, angling wheels right guides any forward roll away from live traffic.

sec10-F20-card.question_text: How must you position your front wheels when parking uphill next to a curb?
sec10-F20-card.teaching_text: Turning away from the curb lets the back of your right front tire catch solidly against the concrete lip if the car rolls back.

sec10-F21-card.question_text: Which way do you turn your front wheels when parking uphill on a road that has no curb?
sec10-F21-card.teaching_text: Without a concrete curb to catch a left-angled tire, turning right makes a rolling car swing off the shoulder instead of across traffic.

sec10-F22-card.question_text: How does Delaware law protect passing traffic and bicyclists when exiting a parked car?
sec10-F22-card.teaching_text: Flinging a street-side door into a bike lane causes severe dooring crashes, so use the curb side or check mirrors and blind spots first.

sec10-F23-card.question_text: What three exceptions excuse stopping in prohibited zones, and does leaving a passenger inside make illegal parking legal?
sec10-F23-card.teaching_text: Sitting behind the wheel with hazards blinking is still illegal stopping unless signs, police orders, or crash avoidance require it.

sec10-F24-card.question_text: May you stop or park where an official sign prohibits it if no emergency or police order applies?
sec10-F24-card.teaching_text: Posted restrictions protect sightlines, loading zones, and emergency turn radii even when the curb looks wide open.

sec10-F25-card.question_text: What do a yellow-painted curb or yellow road-edge stripe mean for stopping and parking?
sec10-F25-card.teaching_text: Yellow curb and edge paint marks restricted zones where parked cars block turning trucks, hydrants, or corner visibility.

sec10-F26-card.question_text: How far back from an intersection crosswalk is stopping or parking prohibited?
sec10-F26-card.teaching_text: Parking right up to corner stripes hides children and pedestrians until they step directly into moving lanes.

sec10-F27-card.question_text: Is stopping or parking two wheels or all four wheels on a sidewalk allowed?
sec10-F27-card.teaching_text: Blocking a sidewalk forces wheelchair users and parents with strollers off the curb into live motor-vehicle traffic.

sec10-F28-card.question_text: May you park or stop across the entrance to a private driveway, alley, or intersecting road?
sec10-F28-card.teaching_text: Both public and private aprons must stay clear at all times so residents, deliveries, and ambulances are never trapped.

sec10-F29-card.question_text: What minimum distance must you leave when stopping or parking near a fire hydrant?
sec10-F29-card.teaching_text: Firefighters need fast clearance to wrench caps and run thick pressurized supply hoses without kink angles.

sec10-F30-card.question_text: How close to a fire-station driveway entrance is stopping or parking banned on the same side of the street?
sec10-F30-card.teaching_text: Heavy ladder trucks swing wide right off the apron and need twenty feet of unobstructed curb on either side.

sec10-F31-card.question_text: When signs are posted across the street from a fire-station entrance, how far does the no-parking zone extend?
sec10-F31-card.teaching_text: Long fire apparatus need deep swing room across the opposite curb to pull out onto narrow city streets.

sec10-R01-card.question_text: How far must you stay from a stop sign, traffic signal, or flashing beacon when stopping or parking?
sec10-R01-card.teaching_text: Tall SUVs and vans parked closer than thirty feet hide stop signs and red beacons from approaching drivers.

sec10-R02-card.question_text: Where is parking banned around a pedestrian or transit safety island unless signs state otherwise?
sec10-R02-card.teaching_text: Parking between a safety zone and the curb pinches traffic shut, and thirty feet at the island end preserves clear sightlines.

sec10-R03-card.question_text: Within what distance of a railroad crossing is stopping or parking prohibited unless posted otherwise?
sec10-R03-card.teaching_text: Fifty feet keeps parked cars from blocking crossing gates, flashing red lights, and sightlines down the tracks.

sec10-R04-card.question_text: When is stopping or parking prohibited beside or across from a street excavation or road obstruction?
sec10-R04-card.teaching_text: Trench plates and cones already squeeze lane width, so parking opposite an excavation chokes two-way flow completely.

sec10-R05-card.question_text: Is stopping on the street side of another car already parked at the curb ever legal?
sec10-R05-card.teaching_text: Double-parking blocks a live travel lane, traps the curbed motorist inside, and forces dangerous blind swerves.

sec10-R06-card.question_text: What parking rule applies on highway bridges, elevated structures, and inside tunnels?
sec10-R06-card.teaching_text: Bridges, viaducts, and tunnels have zero shoulder escape space, making any voluntary stop an extreme collision and fire hazard.

sec10-R07-card.question_text: What general rule applies to stopping, standing, or parking anywhere that obstructs moving traffic?
sec10-R07-card.teaching_text: Even without a red sign or painted curb, blocking normal vehicle passage violates Delaware's core parking statute.

sec10-R08-card.question_text: May you park in the median strip or crossover between roadways of a divided highway?
sec10-R08-card.teaching_text: Pulling into or out of a grassy median places slow vehicles directly beside the fastest left-hand passing lanes.

sec10-R09-card.question_text: May you stop or park inside a designated fire lane at a store or building?
sec10-R09-card.teaching_text: Curbside fire zones directly in front of entrances are reserved exclusively for fire engines and ambulances.

sec10-R10-card.question_text: Which two speed standards must every Delaware driver satisfy at the same time?
sec10-R10-card.teaching_text: Staying under the white sign is only half the law; your pace must also stay reasonable for real-time road conditions.

sec10-R11-card.question_text: What does Delaware's basic speed rule require when rain, snow, fog, or glare makes the posted limit unsafe?
sec10-R11-card.teaching_text: A 55-mph sign sets the ceiling for dry clear pavement, so driving 55 on black ice still earns a speeding-for-conditions citation.

sec10-R12-card.question_text: Do heavy traffic, bad weather, or running late ever excuse failing to control speed to avoid a collision?
sec10-R12-card.teaching_text: Every driver carries an affirmative legal duty to regulate speed so they never strike people, cars, or other road users.

sec10-R13-card.question_text: Can emergency conditions alter statutory speed limits, and may you ever exceed a posted limit?
sec10-R13-card.teaching_text: State emergencies can temporarily drop highway limits, and under all conditions the posted sign remains a strict legal maximum.

sec10-R14-card.question_text: What statutory speed limit does the Delaware speed table set for school zones?
sec10-R14-card.teaching_text: At 20 miles per hour your stopping distance shrinks dramatically when children step out between buses or crossing cones.

sec10-R15-card.question_text: What default speed limit applies in Delaware business districts unless posted or altered by emergency?
sec10-R15-card.teaching_text: Frequent storefronts, delivery trucks, jaywalkers, and curb parking make 25 miles per hour essential through commercial blocks.

sec10-R16-card.question_text: What default speed limit applies in Delaware residential districts unless otherwise posted?
sec10-R16-card.teaching_text: Hidden driveways, parked cars, and kids playing near curbs demand the same calm 25-mph pace as business streets.

sec10-R17-card.question_text: What speed limit does the Delaware table assign to open two-lane roads unless posted otherwise?
sec10-R17-card.teaching_text: Undivided two-lane highways carry head-on oncoming traffic feet away, capping statutory speed at 50 rather than 55.

sec10-R18-card.question_text: What statutory speed limit applies on divided highways and roads with four or more lanes unless posted otherwise?
sec10-R18-card.teaching_text: Extra lanes and medians separate opposing traffic, raising the statutory speed ceiling five miles per hour above two-lane roads.

sec10-R19-card.question_text: What default speed limit does the table list for controlled-access expressways and turnpikes unless posted higher or lower?
sec10-R19-card.teaching_text: Learners often guess 65 for every expressway, missing that Delaware's general controlled-access baseline is 55 unless specifically posted.

sec10-R20-card.question_text: Which two specific Delaware highways are listed at 65 miles per hour in the handbook's speed table?
sec10-R20-card.teaching_text: Memorizing Route 1 and I-495 locks in the exact two named 65-mph corridors tested from Delaware's statutory speed chart.

sec10-R21-card.question_text: How are drivers notified when authorities reduce an unsafe speed limit for local conditions?
sec10-R21-card.teaching_text: Work zones, sharp curves, or storm hazards allow DelDOT to lower statutory speeds, enforceable as soon as reduced-limit signs appear.

sec10-R22-card.question_text: When is driving far below normal traffic flow prohibited, and what two reasons excuse slow travel?
sec10-R22-card.teaching_text: Creeping along a dry clear highway sparks sudden braking and risky passing behind you unless safety or legal compliance requires slowing.

sec10-R23-card.question_text: When may you legally travel slower than a posted minimum speed sign?
sec10-R23-card.teaching_text: Posted minimums keep expressway speeds uniform in clear weather, yet ice, fog, or heavy rain always justify slowing down.

sec10-R24-card.question_text: What shape and color scheme identify an enforceable legal speed-limit sign?
sec10-R24-card.teaching_text: Vertical white regulatory rectangles state binding legal limits, separating them visually from yellow warning advisories.

sec10-R25-card.question_text: What colors are used on advisory-speed signs, and where are they usually mounted?
sec10-R25-card.teaching_text: Yellow square plaques beneath curve or exit-ramp diamonds recommend the safe cornering speed engineered for dry pavement.

sec10-R26-card.question_text: If an advisory speed plaque is not a statutory limit, what legal consequence can follow if you exceed it and crash?
sec10-R26-card.teaching_text: Losing control above a curve's yellow advisory number gives investigators strong evidence that you violated Delaware's reasonable-speed law.

sec10-R27-card.question_text: Besides cars and trucks, which other users and equipment operators share Delaware highways?
sec10-R27-card.teaching_text: Rural and suburban Delaware roads mix fast cars with farm tractors, road graders, horse-drawn buggies, cyclists, and motorcyclists.

sec10-R28-card.question_text: Do traffic laws govern only motor-vehicle drivers, or pedestrians and bicyclists as well?
sec10-R28-card.teaching_text: Safe road sharing works because drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians are all legally bound to follow traffic rules.

sec10-R29-card.question_text: When must you stop for a pedestrian at a crosswalk, and when is cautious forward progress permitted?
sec10-R29-card.teaching_text: Anyone actively crossing a marked or unmarked crosswalk commands a full stop, whereas someone remaining safely halted on the sidewalk lets you pass cautiously.

sec10-R30-card.question_text: Does honking your horn satisfy your legal obligation to yield to a pedestrian?
sec10-R30-card.teaching_text: Warning blasts do not shift right-of-way; your foot belongs on the brake pedal whenever a pedestrian is crossing.

sec10-R31-card.question_text: How should you respond to pedestrians who are deaf, hard of hearing, or using mobility aids or service animals?
sec10-R31-card.teaching_text: Walkers using wheelchairs, walkers, canes, or service animals cannot sprint clear when signals change, so hold your stop patiently.

sec10-R32-card.question_text: Which two pedestrian areas must you never drive through or block with your vehicle?
sec10-R32-card.teaching_text: Pedestrian safety islands shelter transit riders in traffic, and blocking a crosswalk forces walkers out around your bumper into blind lanes.

sec11-F01-card.question_text: What must a driver do for a pedestrian occupying a crosswalk?
sec11-F01-card.teaching_text: Slowing slightly is never enough when your vehicle path crosses a walker's lane; come to a full stop whenever required.

sec11-F02-card.question_text: May you pass a vehicle that has stopped ahead at a crosswalk to let a pedestrian cross?
sec11-F02-card.teaching_text: The stopped car's body hides the walker stepping across into your adjacent lane, making overtaking at crosswalks a classic fatal trap.

sec11-F03-card.question_text: Where should drivers watch with extra care for children, and what speed rule applies near schools?
sec11-F03-card.teaching_text: Kids chase balls or dart between parked cars unpredictably near houses and playgrounds, leaving zero margin for speeding past schools.

sec11-F04-card.question_text: What check is essential right before opening your door and stepping out of a parked vehicle?
sec11-F04-card.teaching_text: Looking back through mirrors and over your shoulder prevents stepping or swinging a door directly into passing cars or cyclists.

sec11-F05-card.question_text: Where must a pedestrian walk when a sidewalk is present, and where when no sidewalk exists?
sec11-F05-card.teaching_text: Walking on the far left shoulder facing oncoming cars lets you make eye contact and step off pavement if a driver drifts.

sec11-F06-card.question_text: What visibility item must a pedestrian carry when walking along a Delaware road at night?
sec11-F06-card.teaching_text: Delaware makes carrying a flashlight or retroreflective item mandatory at night because dark clothing vanishes outside low-beam headlight range.

sec11-F07-card.question_text: What type of clothing does the handbook recommend for pedestrians whenever practical?
sec11-F07-card.teaching_text: Pale or bright fabric contrasts sharply against dark asphalt, helping drivers spot walkers seconds earlier.

sec11-F08-card.question_text: Is walking along a public highway legal while impaired by alcohol or narcotic drugs?
sec11-F08-card.teaching_text: Intoxication ruins balance and depth perception along high-speed shoulders, making impaired highway walking explicitly illegal.

sec11-F09-card.question_text: May a person stand on a highway to hitchhike or conduct roadside business?
sec11-F09-card.teaching_text: Standing in live roadway space to thumb rides or sell items causes sudden highway braking and pedestrian strikes.

sec11-F10-card.question_text: What three-step order of preference should pedestrians follow when choosing where and how to cross a street?
sec11-F10-card.teaching_text: Drivers expect foot traffic most at painted crosswalks and street corners, so mid-block crossing requires looking both ways and moving briskly.

sec11-F11-card.question_text: What does a blinking DON'T WALK pedestrian signal forbid?
sec11-F11-card.teaching_text: Flashing countdown phases give walkers already in the street time to finish, not permission to step off the curb late.

sec11-F12-card.question_text: Which vehicles must pedestrians watch out for before stepping across an intersection?
sec11-F12-card.teaching_text: Even when you hold a fresh WALK light, right-on-red and permissive left-turning drivers may be looking at cross traffic instead of you.

sec11-F13-card.question_text: When is a pedestrian legally allowed to cross an intersection diagonally from corner to corner?
sec11-F13-card.teaching_text: Cutting corner-to-corner puts walkers across active lanes unless an all-way pedestrian scramble phase halts every approach.

sec11-F14-card.question_text: When do pedestrians hold right-of-way at a signalized intersection?
sec11-F14-card.teaching_text: Turning vehicles sharing the green phase must wait until walkers crossing on green or WALK clear the lane.

sec11-F15-card.question_text: Does pedestrian crosswalk priority apply only inside painted lines, or at unmarked crosswalks too?
sec11-F15-card.teaching_text: Missing white paint at a residential corner never strips a crossing pedestrian of legal right-of-way.

sec11-F16-card.question_text: Who holds right-of-way where a public sidewalk crosses a driveway, alley, or lot entrance?
sec11-F16-card.teaching_text: Cars turning off the street or backing out of a garage cross pedestrian territory and must yield every time.

sec11-F17-card.question_text: Which two mobility cues identify a blind pedestrian who holds priority while crossing?
sec11-F17-card.teaching_text: Spotting a white cane or harness-led guide dog requires an immediate patient yield without honking.

sec11-F18-card.question_text: Who must yield when a pedestrian crosses mid-block outside any marked or unmarked intersection crosswalk?
sec11-F18-card.teaching_text: Stepping across open pavement away from corners places the legal duty to wait for clear lanes on the pedestrian.

sec11-F19-card.question_text: What right-of-way rule applies if a pedestrian crosses on the asphalt where an overhead bridge or pedestrian tunnel is provided?
sec11-F19-card.teaching_text: Grade-separated overpasses and underpasses are built on fast arterial roads, so walkers bypassing them on pavement must yield.

sec11-F20-card.question_text: Which public roadways in Delaware are off-limits to bicyclists?
sec11-F20-card.teaching_text: Controlled-access freeways carry high-speed ramp traffic incompatible with pedal speeds, while ordinary public roads remain open to bikes.

sec11-F21-card.question_text: What does Delaware law allow and require when you pass a bicycle in a lane too narrow to share safely, even with a double yellow center line?
sec11-F21-card.teaching_text: Delaware explicitly authorizes crossing double solid yellow lines when safe and clear so you can give cyclists a full lane change and three feet.

sec11-F22-card.question_text: When is a driver allowed to sound the horn at a bicyclist?
sec11-F22-card.teaching_text: Close loud horn blasts startle riders and can make handlebars twitch straight into your bumper.

sec11-F23-card.question_text: How far to the right should a bicyclist ride under normal conditions?
sec11-F23-card.teaching_text: Riders stay right when pavement is clean yet may move left away from broken glass, storm grates, or opening car doors.

sec11-F24-card.question_text: What is an intersection bike box, and what two benefits does it give cyclists?
sec11-F24-card.teaching_text: Placing cyclists directly ahead of stopped hoods at red lights puts riders in clear view and simplifies left or through positioning.

sec11-F25-card.question_text: Which turning conflict and crosswalk issue do intersection bike boxes help prevent?
sec11-F25-card.teaching_text: Keeping cars stopped behind the box prevents right-turning hoods from cutting across unseen riders and keeps crosswalk stripes open.

sec11-F26-card.question_text: How does a two-way cycle track arrange bicycle flow along a street?
sec11-F26-card.teaching_text: Turning drivers must scan both left and right across a two-way cycle track because riders approach from both directions along one curb.

sec11-F27-card.question_text: What physical features can separate a curb-height protected cycle track from moving motor traffic?
sec11-F27-card.teaching_text: Shifting the curb parking row outward or adding posts shields cyclists behind steel or barriers rather than paint alone.

sec11-F28-card.question_text: What aerodynamic hazard arises when cars, buses, or trucks pass a cyclist too closely at high speed?
sec11-F28-card.teaching_text: Large flat front ends push a violent bow wave of air that can destabilize a lightweight bicycle without physical contact.

sec11-F29-card.question_text: How far over must you move to pass a bike when the lane cannot safely hold your car and the bicycle side by side?
sec11-F29-card.teaching_text: Straddling the center stripe leaves your right mirror dangerously close; commit to a full lane change, even across double yellow when clear.

sec11-F30-card.question_text: Under what two conditions may you pass a bicycle inside the same unusually wide travel lane?
sec11-F30-card.teaching_text: Even when a wide suburban lane fits both comfortably, slowing down and holding at least three feet prevents wind wobble.

sec11-F31-card.question_text: What must you do behind a cyclist on a two-lane road when oncoming traffic or a curve blocks safe passing?
sec11-F31-card.teaching_text: Ten seconds of patience at bike pace beats risking either a head-on crash on a blind crest or sideswiping a rider.

sec11-F32-card.question_text: Why must you leave generous room before pulling back right in front of a cyclist you just passed?
sec11-F32-card.teaching_text: Road bikes descending hills or sprinting easily top twenty miles per hour, closing tight cut-ins far quicker than drivers expect.

sec11-F33-card.question_text: According to Delaware's bicycle-passing rules, what is the sole reason to honk while overtaking a bike?
sec11-F33-card.teaching_text: Tapping the horn just to announce your presence violates the passing guidance and risks startling the rider sideways.

sec11-F34-card.question_text: What dangerous maneuver must you never perform right after overtaking a bicyclist?
sec11-F34-card.teaching_text: Racing ahead of a cyclist just to brake and turn right across their front wheel causes classic intersection right-hook crashes.

sec11-F35-card.question_text: For which two cycling violations can Delaware hold a parent or guardian legally responsible?
sec11-F35-card.teaching_text: Delaware places legal accountability on parents and guardians when minors break road rules or ride under age eighteen without a helmet.

sec11-F36-card.question_text: Which three handling skills should a bicyclist master before riding alongside street traffic?
sec11-F36-card.teaching_text: Holding a steady line while glancing back or braking smoothly keeps a rider predictable next to passing cars.

sec11-F37-card.question_text: How should cyclists approach intersections even when traffic rules give the bicycle right-of-way?
sec11-F37-card.teaching_text: Being legally right offers zero armor against a distracted driver, so defensive riders stay poised on the brake levers.

sec11-F38-card.question_text: Which front and rear devices are mandatory on a bicycle at night, and what extras help?
sec11-F38-card.teaching_text: A forward white beam and rear red reflector meet legal minimums, while adding an active red taillight boosts rear visibility further.

sec11-F39-card.question_text: Which three habits define predictable bicycling in traffic?
sec11-F39-card.teaching_text: Traveling with flow, signaling turns early, and picking a line free of sudden swerves lets drivers anticipate every move.

sec11-F40-card.question_text: Where should a cyclist ride inside an unusually wide lane when comfortable letting cars pass within the lane?
sec11-F40-card.teaching_text: Tracking steadily along the right portion of an extra-wide lane makes three-foot in-lane passing smooth when safe.

sec11-F41-card.question_text: From what minimum distance must a bicycle's white front headlight be visible at night?
sec11-F41-card.teaching_text: Five hundred feet of forward beam visibility warns oncoming left-turners and cross-street drivers before they pull out.

sec11-F42-card.question_text: From how far back must a bicycle's red rear reflector be visible at night?
sec11-F42-card.teaching_text: Notice the 500-front versus 600-rear exam contrast because overtaking headlights must catch the red rear reflector at 600 feet.

sec11-F43-card.question_text: Which two options satisfy Delaware's nighttime side-visibility requirement for bicycles, including their distances?
sec11-F43-card.teaching_text: Cross-street headlights strike bikes broadside, so night riders need 600-foot two-sided reflectors or a 500-foot two-sided lamp.

sec11-F44-card.question_text: Is a red bicycle taillight legally mandatory or recommended in the Delaware handbook?
sec11-F44-card.teaching_text: Exam questions separate mandatory gear from upgrades, making the red rear reflector required while an active taillight stays recommended.

sec11-F45-card.question_text: How must a bicyclist be positioned on the bicycle while riding?
sec11-F45-card.teaching_text: Perching on handlebars, top tubes, or cargo racks ruins center-of-gravity balance and emergency braking leverage.

sec11-F46-card.question_text: When may a bicycle legally carry an extra passenger?
sec11-F46-card.teaching_text: Tandems or proper child seats support extra weight safely, whereas riding double on pegs or handlebars causes crashes.

sec11-F47-card.question_text: May a bicyclist hold onto or tow behind a moving car or truck on the highway?
sec11-F47-card.teaching_text: Grabbing a bumper or truck rail at motor-vehicle speed guarantees a catastrophic fall at the first pothole or brake tap.

sec11-F48-card.question_text: Unlike pedestrians without sidewalks, may a bicyclist ride facing oncoming highway traffic?
sec11-F48-card.teaching_text: Wrong-way cycling multiplies closing speed and puts riders directly where driveway and right-turning motorists never look.

sec11-F49-card.question_text: How many hands must a bicyclist keep on the handlebars at minimum while riding?
sec11-F49-card.teaching_text: Riding no-handed or carrying bulky packages with both arms leaves you helpless if the front wheel hits gravel or a crack.

sec11-F50-card.question_text: What two duties apply when a bicyclist approaches pedestrians on a sidewalk or crosswalk?
sec11-F50-card.teaching_text: Silent bikes surprise walkers from behind, so slow to yield and call out or ring a bell before passing.

sec11-F51-card.question_text: What rule governs wearing headphones or earbuds while riding a bicycle?
sec11-F51-card.teaching_text: Blocking both ears masks approaching engines, sirens, and tire noise that alert riders before hazards enter view.

sec11-F52-card.question_text: Under what age must every Delaware bicyclist wear a properly fitted and fastened helmet?
sec11-F52-card.teaching_text: An unbuckled or tilted helmet flies off on impact, so Delaware mandates a snug, strapped fit for everyone under eighteen.

sec11-F53-card.question_text: At how many lanes on an intersecting major road must a bicyclist come to a full stop at a stop sign?
sec11-F53-card.teaching_text: Delaware's bicycle yield law turns back into a mandatory full stop whenever the cross road carries three or more travel lanes.

sec11-F54-card.question_text: What must a bicyclist do at a stop sign if a motor vehicle is already stopped ahead at that same sign?
sec11-F54-card.teaching_text: Filtering past a stopped car at a stop sign surprises its driver mid-turn, so cyclists must stop in turn.

sec11-F55-card.question_text: What must a cyclist do at a stop sign whenever heavy traffic makes rolling through unsafe?
sec11-F55-card.teaching_text: Safety overrides the bicycle yield option whenever cross traffic is heavy, requiring a full foot-down stop at the sign.

sec11-F56-card.question_text: How may a cyclist treat a minor-road stop sign when no car is stopped ahead and cross traffic is clear?
sec11-F56-card.teaching_text: At qualifying two-lane minor stops with nobody ahead, slowing to yield speed preserves momentum while respecting cross-street priority.

sec11-F57-card.question_text: What message does a painted shared-lane bicycle marking communicate to drivers and riders?
sec11-F57-card.teaching_text: Sharrows guide cyclists away from the door zone and remind drivers that bikes lawfully occupy the travel lane.

sec11-F58-card.question_text: When is checking blind spots for motorcycles especially critical?
sec11-F58-card.teaching_text: Narrow bike silhouettes hide easily behind windshield pillars and side mirrors right when you turn or pull out of driveways.

sec11-F59-card.question_text: How do a motorcyclist's legal rights and duties compare with those of four-wheeled drivers?
sec11-F59-card.teaching_text: Two wheels carry identical right-of-way and lane protections as full-size sedans and trucks on every Delaware highway.

sec11-F60-card.question_text: Why do drivers frequently misjudge an approaching motorcycle?
sec11-F60-card.teaching_text: A single headlight and slim front profile fool human eyes into thinking a motorcycle is farther away and slower than reality.

sec11-R01-card.question_text: What should you do before turning left across the path of an oncoming motorcycle?
sec11-R01-card.teaching_text: Left-turning cars cause the deadliest multi-vehicle motorcycle crashes because drivers glance once and misread closing speed.

sec11-R02-card.question_text: Why shouldn't you pull out immediately just because an approaching motorcycle's turn signal is blinking?
sec11-R02-card.teaching_text: Many motorcycles lack self-canceling turn signals, so wait until the rider actually slows and leans into the turn.

sec11-R03-card.question_text: What minimum following gap does the handbook specify behind a motorcycle below forty miles per hour?
sec11-R03-card.teaching_text: Motorcycles stop faster than heavier passenger cars, requiring at least two full seconds of cushion at town speeds.

sec11-R04-card.question_text: How many seconds of following distance should you keep behind a motorcycle above forty miles per hour?
sec11-R04-card.teaching_text: Doubling your cushion to four seconds above 40 mph gives you stopping room if a rider swerves or brakes hard.

sec11-R05-card.question_text: How should you adjust your following gap behind a motorcycle when pavement is wet or slick?
sec11-R05-card.teaching_text: Wet asphalt lengthens your four-wheel braking distance right when a two-wheeled rider is most vulnerable to surface traction loss.

sec11-R06-card.question_text: May a car share a lane side by side with a motorcycle when extra asphalt seems open?
sec11-R06-card.teaching_text: Riders constantly shift left and right inside their lane to dodge potholes, oil streaks, and wind gusts.

sec11-R07-card.question_text: Besides extra following space, what visual hazard should you watch for behind motorcycles during bad weather?
sec11-R07-card.teaching_text: Reflected headlight sheen off rain-soaked pavement easily swallows a motorcycle's single taillight in spray.

sec11-R08-card.question_text: How can strong crosswinds or air blasts from passing tractor-trailers affect a motorcycle?
sec11-R08-card.teaching_text: Sudden wind buffeting off bridges, open fields, or semi trailers can shove a light bike across its lane instantly.

sec11-R09-card.question_text: Why might a motorcyclist suddenly slow down or weave inside the lane on seemingly open pavement?
sec11-R09-card.teaching_text: Loose gravel, slick iron manhole lids, pavement grooves, and small animals pose serious slide hazards on two narrow tires.

sec11-R10-card.question_text: What two legitimate moves might a motorcyclist make when crossing rough or angled railroad tracks?
sec11-R10-card.teaching_text: Crossing steel rails at ninety degrees prevents front-tire trapping, and standing slightly on footpegs absorbs violent track jolts.

sec11-R11-card.question_text: How do metal or open-grate bridge decks affect motorcycle tires and riders?
sec11-R11-card.teaching_text: Open steel bridge grates make motorcycle tires wander slightly, often prompting newer riders to slow down or shift line.

sec11-R12-card.question_text: Which traffic rights and duties apply to animal riders and drivers of animal-drawn vehicles on Delaware highways?
sec11-R12-card.teaching_text: Horseback riders and buggy operators hold full roadway rights and follow standard traffic laws except provisions impossible for animals.

sec11-R13-card.question_text: How do traffic laws treat operators of farm tractors and self-propelled agricultural equipment on public roads?
sec11-R13-card.teaching_text: Farm machinery operators carry standard driver rights and duties alongside dedicated equipment rules covered in a separate supplement.

sec11-R14-card.question_text: May minibikes, go-carts, golf carts, dirtbikes, motorized scooters, or non-registrable ATVs operate on Delaware highways?
sec11-R14-card.teaching_text: Recreational machines that the DMV cannot register lack highway safety equipment and are strictly banned from public roads.

sec11-R15-card.question_text: What does a fluorescent orange and red reflective triangle on the back of a vehicle mean, and how should you react?
sec11-R15-card.teaching_text: Tractors and buggies wearing the orange triangle often cruise under 25 mph, closing highway gaps shockingly fast.

sec11-R16-card.question_text: What must you verify ahead and behind before pulling out to pass a large truck?
sec11-R16-card.teaching_text: Long tractor-trailers require far more passing pavement than sedans, so confirm legal markings and plenty of open space first.

sec11-R17-card.question_text: How can you alert a truck driver before passing, especially after dark?
sec11-R17-card.teaching_text: A brief headlight flick catches the trucker's side mirror without blinding them like a sustained high-beam glare.

sec11-R18-card.question_text: How quickly should you complete a pass rather than cruising beside another vehicle?
sec11-R18-card.teaching_text: Hanging beside another vehicle traps you inside its side blind spot and eliminates escape lanes if debris appears ahead.

sec11-R19-card.question_text: Even if a trucker blinks headlights after you pass, what visual check must you see before pulling back in?
sec11-R19-card.teaching_text: Heavy rigs need huge stopping distance; wait until the whole front grille appears in your inside rear-view mirror.

sec11-R20-card.question_text: What should you do with your speed immediately after pulling back in front of a truck you passed?
sec11-R20-card.teaching_text: Easing off the gas right in front of an eighty-thousand-pound rig steals its braking buffer instantly.

sec11-R21-card.question_text: How can you make it safer and faster when a large truck is overtaking your vehicle?
sec11-R21-card.teaching_text: Keeping toward the outer edge of your lane and easing slightly off the gas shortens time spent in wind turbulence.

sec11-R22-card.question_text: Where should you position your car when meeting a large oncoming truck on an undivided road?
sec11-R22-card.teaching_text: Maximizing lateral separation cuts both mirror-clip risk and the wind blast between opposing vehicles.

sec11-R23-card.question_text: Does air turbulence between two meeting vehicles pull them together or push them apart?
sec11-R23-card.teaching_text: Drivers often over-correct away from oncoming semis thinking suction pulls cars inward, when compressed air actually pushes outward.

sec11-R24-card.question_text: What does the term No-Zone describe around a large commercial truck?
sec11-R24-card.teaching_text: Front, rear, and wide side No-Zones mark the exact areas where a trucker loses sight of smaller cars or lacks stopping room.

sec11-R25-card.question_text: How should you manage speed and lane return when overtaking any large commercial vehicle?
sec11-R25-card.teaching_text: Holding consistent throttle clears side blind spots predictably, and spotting the cab in your rear-view mirror protects front stopping space.

sec11-R26-card.question_text: Why must you never slip closely behind a truck that is actively backing up?
sec11-R26-card.teaching_text: Box trailers block rear visibility completely, leaving both you and the truck driver blind to each other behind the bumper.

sec11-R27-card.question_text: What minimum following time gap should you keep behind a large truck?
sec11-R27-card.teaching_text: Tailgating hides your car inside the trailer's deep rear blind spot and blocks your own view of signals ahead.

sec11-R28-card.question_text: Why is cruising alongside either side of a tractor-trailer hazardous?
sec11-R28-card.teaching_text: If a blown tire or stalled car forces the rig to swerve lanes suddenly, the driver cannot see a car tucked beside the trailer.

sec11-R29-card.question_text: Why might a truck swing left right before an intersection, and what mistake must you avoid?
sec11-R29-card.teaching_text: Long trailers track sharply inward across the right lane and curb, crushing any car that sneaks into that right-hand gap.

sec11-R30-card.question_text: What should you do when a truck ahead angles across lanes preparing to back into a loading bay?
