sec11-R30-card.teaching_text: Darting behind a positioning trailer puts your car directly into the blind path the rig is about to back through.

sec13-F01-card.question_text: Why must you check your speedometer often right after exiting a fast highway onto a slower local road?
sec13-F01-card.teaching_text: Cruising at 65 numbs your speed perception so 40 on an exit town street feels like a crawl without glancing at the gauge.

sec13-F02-card.question_text: What basic duty applies to every posted speed-limit sign along your route?
sec13-F02-card.teaching_text: Posted limits set the legal maximum engineered for sightlines, curves, and roadside access under ideal dry conditions.

sec13-F03-card.question_text: Which two crash risks arise when you slam on the brakes at the last second instead of anticipating stops early?
sec13-F03-card.teaching_text: Sudden panic braking can break tire traction into a slide and steals reaction seconds from the driver behind you.

sec13-F04-card.question_text: Which two smooth alternatives replace a panic stop when you scan far ahead down the road?
sec13-F04-card.teaching_text: Spotting brake lights or lane closures blocks ahead lets you lift off the gas smoothly or merge cleanly around trouble.

sec13-F05-card.question_text: How should you brake and steer during an emergency or on slick pavement in a vehicle equipped with anti-lock brakes?
sec13-F05-card.teaching_text: Anti-lock computers pulse wheel pressure rapidly so tires keep rolling, letting you brake hard and steer around obstacles simultaneously.

sec13-F06-card.question_text: How must you brake during an emergency or on slippery pavement if your vehicle does not have anti-lock brakes?
sec13-F06-card.teaching_text: Locked front tires slide straight ahead regardless of steering angle, so hold threshold pressure just short of wheel lockup.

sec13-F07-card.question_text: Which four directional zones around your car require continuous observation for unexpected hazards?
sec13-F07-card.teaching_text: Tunnel vision straight over the hood misses side-street runners, blind-spot motorcycles, and fast-closing tailgaters.

sec13-F08-card.question_text: Besides nighttime darkness, when should you turn on your headlights?
sec13-F08-card.teaching_text: Turning low beams on in dusk, gloom, or overcast rain helps oncoming and cross-street drivers spot your car early.

sec13-F09-card.question_text: Why must you keep interior glances brief, and what must you do before reading a map or route screen?
sec13-F09-card.teaching_text: At 55 miles per hour, looking down for four seconds drives the length of a football field completely blind.

sec13-F10-card.question_text: What emotional mindset should you keep when another motorist drives aggressively around you?
sec13-F10-card.teaching_text: Treating someone else's impatience as an impersonal hazard rather than an insult keeps your own judgment cool.

sec13-F11-card.question_text: Which two interpersonal triggers should you avoid around an aggressive driver?
sec13-F11-card.teaching_text: Staring back, gesturing, or matching speed escalates an angry stranger into dangerous highway retaliation.

sec13-F12-card.question_text: What is the safest spacing response when you spot a vehicle weaving, speeding, or behaving erratically?
sec13-F12-card.teaching_text: Erratic lane drift often signals impairment, distraction, or medical distress, so drop back or change lanes away.

sec13-F13-card.question_text: Why does the handbook advise avoiding phone or CB-radio chats while moving, even on hands-free audio?
sec13-F13-card.teaching_text: Mental attention narrows during active conversation, slowing brake reaction times even while both hands stay on the wheel.

sec13-F14-card.question_text: What does Delaware law prohibit regarding headphones or earbuds while operating a motor vehicle?
sec13-F14-card.teaching_text: Wearing over-ear headphones or dual earbuds seals off emergency sirens, train horns, and screeching tires.

sec13-F15-card.question_text: How should you drive past a roadside crash, police stop, or work scene instead of slowing just to stare?
sec13-F15-card.teaching_text: Gawking at flashing lights takes eyes off brake lights directly ahead and causes secondary rear-end collisions.

sec13-F16-card.question_text: Which three categories of critical information does active scanning ahead, sideways, and behind reveal early?
sec13-F16-card.teaching_text: Keeping your eyes moving catches warning signs, merging pedestrians, and developing road hazards before they crowd your bumper.

sec13-F17-card.question_text: At least how many seconds ahead does the Delaware handbook recommend scanning down the road?
sec13-F17-card.teaching_text: A ten-second visual lead gives you ample space to ease off the gas or signal a lane change smoothly.

sec13-F18-card.question_text: What physical roadway distance does a ten-second look-ahead represent?
sec13-F18-card.teaching_text: Measuring visual lead in seconds scales automatically with speed, stretching farther down the highway as pace climbs.

sec13-F19-card.question_text: How far ahead does a ten-second visual lead roughly correspond to in urban city traffic?
sec13-F19-card.teaching_text: Watching a full city block ahead reveals stale green lights, double-parked delivery vans, and jaywalkers early.

sec13-F20-card.question_text: How do you begin checking whether you are actually looking far enough ahead while driving?
sec13-F20-card.teaching_text: Selecting a sign, pole, or overpass right where your gaze lands gives a fixed reference point to time.

sec13-F21-card.question_text: Once you pick a roadside landmark at your gaze horizon, how do you confirm your look-ahead time?
sec13-F21-card.teaching_text: If your car passes the chosen sign before you count to ten, lift your eyes higher up the roadway.

sec13-R01-card.question_text: How does looking well ahead reduce both front-end and rear-end collision risks?
sec13-R01-card.teaching_text: Eliminating panic braking and jerky turns keeps you from hitting cars ahead or getting rear-ended from behind.

sec13-R02-card.question_text: How does spotting traffic slowdowns early help your fuel economy?
sec13-R02-card.teaching_text: Every hard brake tap converts paid gasoline momentum into brake-pad heat instead of coasting smoothly toward a clearing light.

sec13-R03-card.question_text: How does reacting early to traffic ahead benefit drivers following behind you?
sec13-R03-card.teaching_text: Tapping brake lights early and slowing gradually lets following traffic match pace smoothly without accordion pileups.

sec13-R04-card.question_text: At which two types of crossings is scanning left and right especially vital?
sec13-R04-card.teaching_text: Cross-street red-light runners and fast trains strike from ninety-degree angles that straight-ahead staring never catches.

sec13-R05-card.question_text: Beyond street-to-street corners, what everyday access points count as intersections where traffic merges or crosses?
sec13-R05-card.teaching_text: Shoppers pulling out of strip-mall aprons or residential driveways create identical conflict angles to named side streets.

sec13-R06-card.question_text: When stopped before an intersection, when should you perform one final left-and-right scan?
sec13-R06-card.teaching_text: A jogger or speeding scooter can enter the corner in the two seconds between your first glance and lifting off the brake.

sec13-R07-card.question_text: What space check beyond the crosswalk is required before pulling into any intersection?
sec13-R07-card.teaching_text: Even on a fresh green light, backed-up cars beyond the far crosswalk will strand your tail across cross-street lanes.

sec13-R08-card.question_text: Which three checks belong right before turning left across oncoming lanes?
sec13-R08-card.teaching_text: Confirming the receiving crosswalk is open prevents getting pinned sideways in oncoming lanes waiting for a pedestrian.

sec13-R09-card.question_text: Which three conflict sources must you check right before making a right turn?
sec13-R09-card.teaching_text: Drivers turning right often stare left for a traffic gap and miss opposing left-turners or walkers stepping off the right curb.

sec13-R10-card.question_text: Why must you still glance left and right when entering an intersection on a green light or priority road?
sec13-R10-card.teaching_text: Green paint and green bulbs never build a physical wall against distracted or impaired cross-street red-light runners.

sec13-R11-card.question_text: How should you handle a stop sign where hedges, buildings, or parked vans block your cross-street view?
sec13-R11-card.teaching_text: After your required legal stop behind the line, inching forward slowly reveals cross traffic before your hood enters fast lanes.

sec13-R12-card.question_text: Around which six busy roadside environments should you intensify side scanning?
sec13-R12-card.teaching_text: Crowded walkways, storefronts, parking rows, work zones, playgrounds, and schools generate constant surprise doors, bumpers, and darting feet.

sec13-R13-card.question_text: Why must you slow and look both ways down railroad tracks even on routes where you have never seen a train?
sec13-R13-card.teaching_text: Freight, maintenance, and work trains run irregular hours without fixed commuter timetables, turning complacency at familiar crossings fatal.

sec13-R14-card.question_text: What far-side clearance condition must exist before your front wheels touch a railroad crossing?
sec13-R14-card.teaching_text: Waiting short of the near rail costs nothing, whereas stopping with your trunk overhanging steel tracks risks disaster.

sec13-R15-card.question_text: At a crossing with two or more tracks, why shouldn't you pull out the instant the first train's rear car clears?
sec13-R15-card.teaching_text: A long freight train blocks sight and sound of a fast passenger or freight train approaching in the opposite direction on parallel rails.

sec13-R16-card.question_text: During which five driving situations should you check your rear mirrors more frequently than usual?
sec13-R16-card.teaching_text: Knowing who sits right behind your bumper matters most in dense traffic and before lane shifts, braking, backing, or steep downgrades.

sec13-R17-card.question_text: Which two traffic zones around your car must you check before changing lanes, merging off a ramp, or leaving a curb?
sec13-R17-card.teaching_text: Vehicles closing fast from behind or riding parallel beside your quarter panel hold right-of-way in the active lane.

sec13-R18-card.question_text: What do you confirm in your inside and outside mirrors right after signaling an intended lane change?
sec13-R18-card.teaching_text: A car two back may accelerate out to overtake just as you click your turn signal.

sec13-R19-card.question_text: Why must every lane change include a quick head turn over your shoulder in addition to mirror checks?
sec13-R19-card.teaching_text: Even well-set mirrors leave rear-corner pockets where a compact car or motorcycle can sit completely invisible.

sec13-R20-card.question_text: How should you manage head checks so looking back does not cause a rear-end crash ahead?
sec13-R20-card.teaching_text: Staring backward over your shoulder too long blinds you if lead traffic brakes hard right as you begin merging.

sec13-R21-card.question_text: In what exact order do you use mirrors and your over-the-shoulder glance when merging or changing lanes?
sec13-R21-card.teaching_text: Mirrors track gaps early without turning your head, while the final split-second shoulder glance confirms nobody slipped beside you.

sec13-R22-card.question_text: On a three-or-more-lane highway, why must you also check the lane beyond your target middle lane?
sec13-R22-card.teaching_text: Two cars converging from left and right into the same open center pocket at once cause classic highway sideswipes.

sec13-R23-card.question_text: When is glancing at your rear-view mirror while braking especially important?
sec13-R23-card.teaching_text: Braking hard or slowing for an unmarked driveway catches tailgaters off guard; mirror awareness lets you adjust brake modulation.

sec13-R24-card.question_text: How can parking-lot space selection help you avoid backing hazards altogether?
sec13-R24-card.teaching_text: Pulling forward into an open facing bay lets you drive straight out with full windshield visibility instead of backing blind.

sec13-R25-card.question_text: What check should you perform before climbing into a parked vehicle that you will have to back out?
sec13-R25-card.teaching_text: Toddlers, pets, and tricycles sit below rear trunk glass where mirrors cannot spot them from the driver's seat.

sec13-R26-card.question_text: Where should your eyes look while actively backing up your vehicle?
sec13-R26-card.teaching_text: Pivoting to look directly through the back glass gives a wide field of view that small flat mirrors cannot match.

sec13-R27-card.question_text: Why should you always keep speed very low while reversing?
sec13-R27-card.teaching_text: Front-wheel steering swings the nose wide and responds more twitchily in reverse, making slow walking pace essential.

sec13-R28-card.question_text: What extra assistance does the handbook recommend using when backing in tight or obscured spots?
sec13-R28-card.teaching_text: A reliable helper standing safely in view off to the side sees low curbs, cross traffic, and tight corners clearly.

sec13-R29-card.question_text: What specific hazard should you watch for in your mirrors while descending a long or steep hill?
sec13-R29-card.teaching_text: Overheated heavy-vehicle brakes can fade on long grades, so spotting a fast-closing truck or bus lets you clear its lane.

sec13-R30-card.question_text: When should you use high-beam headlights at night, and when do traffic conditions require low beams?
sec13-R30-card.teaching_text: High beams maximize sight distance on dark empty roads, while low beams prevent blinding oncoming or lead drivers in traffic.

sec13-R31-card.question_text: Where are high beams particularly helpful at night so long as you dim for approaching traffic?
sec13-R31-card.teaching_text: Extra throw illuminates unlit curves, orange barrels, and dark-clothed shoulder pedestrians long before low beams reach them.

sec13-R32-card.question_text: By what distance must you dim your high beams for an oncoming vehicle at night?
sec13-R32-card.teaching_text: Five hundred feet prevents your bright beams from dazzling the opposing driver right as the two cars close at highway speed.

sec13-R33-card.question_text: Which headlight setting must you use when following behind another car or driving in heavy night traffic?
sec13-R33-card.teaching_text: High beams behind another vehicle bounce directly off all three of its mirrors and blind the driver ahead of you.

sec13-R34-card.question_text: Why must you select low-beam headlights rather than high beams in fog, snow, or heavy rain?
sec13-R34-card.teaching_text: High-angled beams bounce straight back off airborne water droplets and snowflakes, creating a blinding white wall.

sec13-R35-card.question_text: When does Delaware's weather rule require turning your headlights on during daytime or nighttime precipitation?
sec13-R35-card.teaching_text: Any rain, mist, or snow thick enough to run your windshield wipers legally requires full headlights, not daytime running lamps alone.

sec13-R36-card.question_text: May you drive using only your amber or dim parking lights instead of full headlights?
sec13-R36-card.teaching_text: Parking lamps mark a stationary car and cast almost zero forward beam, making moving cars look stopped to others.

sec13-R37-card.question_text: What polite cue may you give if an approaching night driver forgets to dim high beams?
sec13-R37-card.teaching_text: Two quick flicks remind a forgetful driver to drop to low beams without blinding both lanes continuously.

sec13-R38-card.question_text: Where should you look, and what must you avoid doing, if an oncoming driver refuses to dim high beams?
sec13-R38-card.teaching_text: Tracking the white right road-edge stripe preserves your night vision, while blasting high beams back creates two blind drivers.

sec15-F01-card.question_text: What speed changes should you expect from heavy trucks and underpowered cars on hills or merges?
sec15-F01-card.teaching_text: Gravity saps momentum on steep upgrades and stretches acceleration time when heavy loads enter traffic.

sec15-F02-card.question_text: At what speeds do farm tractors, animal-drawn carts, and road-maintenance rigs commonly travel?
sec15-F02-card.teaching_text: Closing on a twenty-five-mile-per-hour tractor from highway pace shrinks your gap in seconds.

sec15-F03-card.question_text: What rear emblem marks slow-moving farm, animal-drawn, or maintenance vehicles?
sec15-F03-card.teaching_text: Spotting a bright orange rear triangle warns you immediately to shed speed well ahead.

sec15-F04-card.question_text: How should you adjust speed in crowded areas with limited room to steer?
sec15-F04-card.teaching_text: Tight side margins leave nowhere to swerve, making lower speed your main collision buffer.

sec15-F05-card.question_text: Why do shopping centers, parking lots, and downtown streets call for lower speeds?
sec15-F05-card.teaching_text: Backing bumpers, jaywalkers, and turning shoppers converge from multiple angles at once.

sec15-F06-card.question_text: How should rush-hour congestion and hurried commuters influence your pace?
sec15-F06-card.teaching_text: Impatient rush-hour lane-weavers brake suddenly, rewarding calm drivers who ease off speed.

sec15-F07-card.question_text: Why can narrow bridges and tunnels require reduced speed?
sec15-F07-card.teaching_text: Missing shoulders and tight opposing clearance leave tiny margin for steering drift.

sec15-F08-card.question_text: What traffic changes must you watch for approaching and leaving toll plazas?
sec15-F08-card.teaching_text: Booth approaches fan out then squeeze back down while drivers dart toward shorter or electronic lanes.

sec15-F09-card.question_text: What hazard must you stay ready for near schools, playgrounds, and residential blocks?
sec15-F09-card.teaching_text: Kids focused on games or friends step off curbs without checking either direction.

sec15-F10-card.question_text: Which three precautions apply whenever you approach railroad tracks?
sec15-F10-card.teaching_text: Confirming clear exit space beyond rough rails ensures traffic ahead never traps your tail on tracks.

sec15-F11-card.question_text: How does nighttime change object detection and familiar daytime streets?
sec15-F11-card.teaching_text: Shadows erase daytime landmarks and shrink how far ahead hazards stand out.

sec15-F12-card.question_text: How does oncoming headlight glare affect your eyes after bright beams pass?
sec15-F12-card.teaching_text: Pupils constricted by bright glare need dark-adaptation moments before dim obstacles reappear.

sec15-F13-card.question_text: What does avoiding outdriving your headlights mean?
sec15-F13-card.teaching_text: Cruising faster than your headlight reach guarantees hitting dark obstacles before your car can halt.

sec15-F14-card.question_text: How should you monitor oncoming vehicles at night without blinding yourself?
sec15-F14-card.teaching_text: Quick flicks check opposing lane placement without locking your eyes onto dazzling bulbs.

sec15-F15-card.question_text: What quick visual reference helps keep your lane position steady against night glare?
sec15-F15-card.teaching_text: Tracking the white right-edge line guides your steering away from oncoming glare.

sec15-F16-card.question_text: What must you continue scanning for ahead even while managing oncoming headlight glare?
sec15-F16-card.teaching_text: Pedestrians, deer, or road debris in your lane never pause while oncoming brights pass.

sec15-F17-card.question_text: How should you plan around another vehicle displaying a flashing turn signal?
sec15-F17-card.teaching_text: Drivers forget active signals or change plans mid-block, so pulling out early causes T-bone hits.

sec15-F18-card.question_text: Why must you scan cross streets even when cross traffic faces a stop sign or red light?
sec15-F18-card.teaching_text: Distracted or speeding motorists blow past signs and signals, making intersection glances lifesaving.

sec15-F19-card.question_text: When should you identify shoulders and surrounding escape routes while driving?
sec15-F19-card.teaching_text: Knowing whether a firm shoulder or open lane sits beside you saves crucial split seconds in crisis.

sec15-F20-card.question_text: How should you react if an oncoming car pulls out to pass without enough room?
sec15-F20-card.teaching_text: Shedding speed immediately opens gap for the passer while readying your pre-checked roadside exit.

sec15-R01-card.question_text: About how many feet can reacting and stopping from fifty miles per hour take on dry pavement?
sec15-R01-card.teaching_text: Even with sharp brakes and dry grip, fifty miles per hour eats roughly four hundred feet to halt.

sec15-R02-card.question_text: About how many feet does the handbook estimate for stopping from thirty miles per hour on dry pavement?
sec15-R02-card.teaching_text: Even town speeds around thirty miles per hour need roughly two hundred feet to spot, react, and stop.

sec15-R03-card.question_text: What danger arises when your sight distance falls shorter than your speed's stopping distance?
sec15-R03-card.teaching_text: By the moment a stalled car emerges from fog or darkness, physics leaves too few feet to stop.

sec15-R04-card.question_text: What distance limits how fast you may safely drive at night?
sec15-R04-card.teaching_text: Matching night pace to illuminated pavement guarantees you can halt before reaching unlit hazards.

sec15-R05-card.question_text: When heavy rain, snow, or fog cuts sight to two hundred feet or less, what speed ceiling applies?
sec15-R05-card.teaching_text: Because thirty miles per hour already takes about two hundred feet to stop, faster travel outruns vision.

sec15-R06-card.question_text: What should you do when torrential rain makes seeing the road safely impossible?
sec15-R06-card.teaching_text: Pushing blind through sheet rain risks pileups, so park well clear of lanes until visibility returns.

sec15-R07-card.question_text: Why must you ease off speed approaching a view-blocking hill crest or curve?
sec15-R07-card.teaching_text: A stopped delivery truck or fallen branch could sit right beyond the blind crest.

sec15-R08-card.question_text: Why should you steer with maximum safe clearance past a line of parked vehicles?
sec15-R08-card.teaching_text: Swinging doors and pedestrians stepping from between bumpers give almost zero advance warning.

sec15-R09-card.question_text: What does Delaware's four-second sight-distance rule test?
sec15-R09-card.teaching_text: Counting four seconds to your farthest clear landmark reveals whether you are outrunning your sightline.

sec15-R10-card.question_text: How do you perform the four-second sight-distance check on the road?
sec15-R10-card.teaching_text: Timing your approach to the farthest lit or visible fixed object measures sight cushion directly.

sec15-R11-card.question_text: What must you do if your car reaches your sight-distance landmark before four seconds finish?
sec15-R11-card.teaching_text: Arriving under four seconds proves your stopping distance outstrips how far ahead you can see.

sec15-R12-card.question_text: How does the four-second sight-distance check help specifically after dark?
sec15-R12-card.teaching_text: Counting four seconds to the edge of your headlight pool keeps speed safely inside lit asphalt.

sec15-R13-card.question_text: Which roadway realities are built into posted speed limits?
sec15-R13-card.teaching_text: Engineers set limits around curve geometry, hidden driveways, and traffic volume you might overlook.

sec15-R14-card.question_text: What weather and traffic conditions do posted speed-limit signs assume?
sec15-R14-card.teaching_text: Rain, ice, glare, or congestion demand driving slower than the number printed on roadside signs.

sec15-R15-card.question_text: Can you receive a speeding citation while driving below the posted speed limit?
sec15-R15-card.teaching_text: Driving too fast for fog, snow, or bumper-to-bumper traffic violates basic speed law even below posted signs.

sec15-R16-card.question_text: What benefit does keeping open space around your vehicle create?
sec15-R16-card.teaching_text: Extra feet on every side buy calm seconds to brake or steer when nearby drivers slip up.

sec15-R17-card.question_text: How does Delaware distinguish the three-second rule from the four-second check?
sec15-R17-card.teaching_text: Mixing up three-second following gaps with four-second sight-distance timing is a classic permit pitfall.

sec16-F01-card.question_text: How do you time your following distance behind a leading vehicle?
sec16-F01-card.teaching_text: Starting your count as the lead bumper clears a signpost measures exact time spacing.

sec16-F02-card.question_text: What must you do if your car reaches the roadside marker before three seconds finish?
sec16-F02-card.teaching_text: Easing back until a full three-second count clears restores baseline dry-pavement stopping margin.

sec16-F03-card.question_text: How many seconds of following distance may demanding conditions require beyond the baseline?
sec16-F03-card.teaching_text: Adding at least another full second covers slick asphalt, glare, or impaired sightlines ahead.

sec16-F04-card.question_text: Why must you widen your following gap on slippery roads?
sec16-F04-card.teaching_text: Reduced tire friction means your car travels much farther after hitting the brakes.

sec16-F05-card.question_text: How should you respond when a trailing driver pulls out to overtake your vehicle?
sec16-F05-card.teaching_text: Easing off gas opens front reentry space so the passing car clears oncoming lanes sooner.

sec16-F06-card.question_text: Why should you leave extra space behind a motorcycle, especially on wet, icy, gravel, or metal surfaces?
sec16-F06-card.teaching_text: Bridge grates, loose stones, or ice can spill a two-wheeled bike right in front of your bumper.

sec16-F07-card.question_text: Behind which tall or towing vehicles should you drop farther back because drivers may miss you?
sec16-F07-card.teaching_text: Wide cargo boxes and campers block center rearview sight, hiding cars tucked close astern.

sec16-F08-card.question_text: What two visibility advantages come from holding a wider gap behind a large vehicle?
sec16-F08-card.teaching_text: Dropping back opens sightlines around wide trailer walls and places your car inside side mirrors.

sec16-F09-card.question_text: How does carrying a heavy load or pulling a trailer affect your own following distance?
sec16-F09-card.teaching_text: Added mass pushes forward harder under braking, stretching the pavement needed to stop.

sec16-F10-card.question_text: How should you adjust following distance when darkness or foul weather obscures the road ahead?
sec16-F10-card.teaching_text: When you cannot see past the bumper ahead, extra distance keeps sudden stops manageable.

sec16-F11-card.question_text: How should you adjust your front gap when another driver tailgates closely behind you?
sec16-F11-card.teaching_text: Opening room ahead lets you slow down gradually so the tailgater never rams your trunk.

sec16-F12-card.question_text: Why must you hold extra following room behind police cars, ambulances, and fire trucks?
sec16-F12-card.teaching_text: Emergency responders may stop suddenly, turn sharply, or deploy rescue gear without advance warning.

sec16-F13-card.question_text: Behind which three vehicle types must you leave extra room approaching railroad crossings?
sec16-F13-card.teaching_text: Expecting mandatory track stops prevents rear-ending heavy buses or hazmat tankers at rails.

sec16-F14-card.question_text: Why should you leave extra bumper room when stopped behind another car on an uphill slope?
sec16-F14-card.teaching_text: Manual transmissions and heavy trucks often drift back slightly as the driver moves off the brake.

sec16-F15-card.question_text: Which two driving habits help trailing motorists maintain a safe gap behind you?
sec16-F15-card.teaching_text: Predictable speed and early blinkers spare following traffic from guessing your next move.

sec16-F16-card.question_text: Where should you stop to pick up or let out passengers?
sec16-F16-card.teaching_text: Loading riders inside active travel lanes invites rear-end hits and dooring hazards.

sec16-F17-card.question_text: How should you handle trailing traffic before backing into a parallel parking space?
sec16-F17-card.teaching_text: Letting close followers clear past your bumper gives you open room to reverse into the stall.

sec16-F18-card.question_text: What should you do when necessary slow driving delays traffic behind you?
sec16-F18-card.teaching_text: Pulling into a designated turnout clears lines safely without forcing risky two-lane overtaking.

sec16-F19-card.question_text: How can you encourage a tailgater to pass on a multilane road versus a single-lane road?
sec16-F19-card.teaching_text: Changing right opens the passing lane, while gentle slowing on a clear two-lane prompts a safe overtake.

sec16-F20-card.question_text: Why must you never slam your brakes to warn off a tailgater?
sec16-F20-card.teaching_text: A close follower already lacks stopping time, so brake-checking practically guarantees getting hit.

sec16-F21-card.question_text: Why shouldn't you cruise right alongside another vehicle on a multilane road?
sec16-F21-card.teaching_text: Staggering your position keeps side escape space open if the adjacent driver swerves for debris.

sec16-F22-card.question_text: Where in your lane should you avoid riding on a two-lane road with opposing traffic?
sec16-F22-card.teaching_text: Crowding the yellow centerline erases margin if an oncoming mirror or tire drifts wide.

sec16-F23-card.question_text: Where inside your travel lane does the Delaware handbook generally advise driving?
sec16-F23-card.teaching_text: Centering your car between lane stripes balances side buffers equally during normal hazard-free driving.

sec16-F24-card.question_text: How can you help ramp traffic merge onto a multilane highway when the next lane over is clear?
sec16-F24-card.teaching_text: Shifting one lane left opens the right lane cleanly for accelerating ramp traffic.

sec16-F25-card.question_text: Which three sudden hazards justify leaving extra room beside parked cars?
sec16-F25-card.teaching_text: Any parked vehicle can pop a door, hide a child, or nose out into traffic without warning.

sec16-F26-card.question_text: Why do pedestrians and bicyclists, especially children, require extra lateral space?
sec16-F26-card.teaching_text: Children on foot or bicycles often change direction abruptly without checking behind for approaching cars.

sec16-R01-card.question_text: How should you position your car between two non-vulnerable hazards on opposite sides?
sec16-R01-card.teaching_text: Shifting slightly farther away from the riskier side balances survival margin when passing two obstacles.

sec16-R02-card.question_text: How should you handle an oncoming car arriving right as you reach a cyclist ahead?
sec16-R02-card.teaching_text: Waiting behind the bike until the oncoming car clears avoids squeezing three wide.

sec16-R03-card.question_text: At least how many feet of clearance must you keep when passing a cyclist, and what should you use on multilane roads?
sec16-R03-card.teaching_text: Giving at least three feet or shifting fully into the adjacent lane prevents mirror-clipping riders.

sec16-R04-card.question_text: Why must you reject squeezing into a tight merge gap?
sec16-R04-card.teaching_text: Shoehorning between bumpers erases both your own front gap and the trailing car's braking room.

sec16-R05-card.question_text: How must you cross several lanes on a wide roadway?
sec16-R05-card.teaching_text: Sweeping diagonally across multiple lanes blinds you to fast cars merging from the far side.

sec16-R06-card.question_text: How do gap requirements differ between crossing straight across a road and turning into its flow?
sec16-R06-card.teaching_text: Turning into traffic takes longer because you must complete the turn and build up to road speed.

sec16-R07-card.question_text: When is stopping halfway across a divided highway median acceptable?
sec16-R07-card.teaching_text: Stopping inside a narrow divider leaves your nose or tail jutting into high-speed lanes.

sec16-R08-card.question_text: Beyond oncoming gaps, what must you check along your target street before starting a left turn?
sec16-R08-card.teaching_text: Starting a left turn only to halt for crosswalk walkers strands your side across oncoming lanes.

sec16-R09-card.question_text: May you pull into a backed-up intersection on a green light, and what penalty can follow?
sec16-R09-card.teaching_text: Entering without exit room traps your car across cross traffic when lights switch and brings citations.

sec16-R10-card.question_text: When another vehicle flashes a turn signal near your corner, when is it safe to pull out?
sec16-R10-card.teaching_text: Waiting to see wheels slow and angle confirms the blinker wasn't left on accidentally.

sec16-R11-card.question_text: Why might a motorcycle's turn signal keep flashing even when the rider plans to go straight?
sec16-R11-card.teaching_text: Many motorcycles lack self-canceling switches, leaving an earlier turn blinker flashing down the block.

sec16-R12-card.question_text: What clearance condition must be met before you drive onto railroad tracks?
sec16-R12-card.teaching_text: Rolling onto rails behind stopped traffic traps your cabin with nowhere to go if gates drop.

sec16-R13-card.question_text: Where is overtaking allowed, and how many vehicles does the handbook generally advise passing at once?
sec16-R13-card.teaching_text: Trying to leapfrog a multi-car line stretches exposure in oncoming lanes if gaps shrink.

sec16-R14-card.question_text: Roughly how many seconds of clear opposing road does a fifty-five-mile-per-hour pass require?
sec16-R14-card.teaching_text: Overtaking at highway pace eats roughly ten full seconds while you still verify safe distance.

sec16-R15-card.question_text: How far does one vehicle travel during ten seconds at fifty-five miles per hour?
sec16-R15-card.teaching_text: Ten seconds at highway pace swallows nearly three football fields, proving how rapidly oncoming gaps shrink.

sec16-R16-card.question_text: How much road do you and an oncoming fifty-five-mile-per-hour car close together in ten seconds, and what if unsure?
sec16-R16-card.teaching_text: An oncoming car looks distant at over sixteen hundred feet yet meets your bumper in ten seconds.

sec16-R17-card.question_text: Within what distance of a blind hill or curve does the handbook advise against starting a pass?
sec16-R17-card.teaching_text: Within one-third of a mile, a hidden oncoming car can pop over the crest mid-pass.

sec16-R18-card.question_text: Why is passing hazardous near intersections, railroad crossings, or shopping-center entrances?
sec16-R18-card.teaching_text: Drivers turning out from driveways rarely expect a passing vehicle coming down the opposing lane.

sec16-R19-card.question_text: What roadside or traffic factors should you scan ahead for before pulling out to pass?
sec16-R19-card.teaching_text: A parked delivery van or merging car ahead could force the vehicle you are passing leftward.

sec16-R20-card.question_text: Which roadside obstacles can shrink available passing room ahead?
sec16-R20-card.teaching_text: Drivers ahead naturally swerve left around potholes, cyclists, or narrow bridge rails.

sec16-R21-card.question_text: What lane-return requirement must be met before you start overtaking?
sec16-R21-card.teaching_text: Counting on tight line-drivers to brake and let you squeeze back in invites head-on traps.

sec16-R22-card.question_text: May you overtake another vehicle when approaching a railroad crossing?
sec16-R22-card.teaching_text: Passing near rails hides warning flashers and risks getting trapped beside stopped vehicles.

sec16-R23-card.question_text: What interior mirror check tells you there is enough room to pull back in after passing?
sec16-R23-card.teaching_text: Spotting both passed headlights in your center mirror prevents clipping the other car's front bumper.

sec16-R24-card.question_text: How should you drive past intersections or driveways where cross-drivers have blocked views?
sec16-R24-card.teaching_text: Drivers edging past hedges or parked trucks must nose out before they can spot you.

sec16-R25-card.question_text: Why do reversing vehicles and cars entering or exiting parking stalls need extra space?
sec16-R25-card.teaching_text: Roof pillars and neighboring SUVs block sightlines while a driver concentrates on parking angles.

sec16-R26-card.question_text: Which visual clues warn you a driver or pedestrian cannot see surrounding traffic clearly?
sec16-R26-card.teaching_text: Snow-covered glass and tilted storm umbrellas blind people right beside your lane.

sec16-R27-card.question_text: Around which busy or distracted groups should you widen clearance and caution?
sec16-R27-card.teaching_text: Workers hauling packages or cones focus on tasks rather than approaching bumpers.

sec16-R28-card.question_text: Which behaviors mark a confused driver who needs extra space?
sec16-R28-card.teaching_text: Motorists busy scanning street numbers frequently brake suddenly or turn across lanes without signaling.

sec16-R29-card.question_text: What should you do if another motorist misjudges a pass and runs short of room?
sec16-R29-card.teaching_text: Easing off the gas prevents a multi-car head-on wreck right beside your door.

sec16-R30-card.question_text: How should you respond when a nearby driver urgently needs to merge into your lane?
sec16-R30-card.teaching_text: Yielding a few car lengths beats turning someone else's late lane shift into a crash.

sec17-F01-card.question_text: Which five personal factors determine whether you are fit to drive?
sec17-F01-card.teaching_text: Weakness in eyesight, sleep, sobriety, health, or mood degrades safe control behind the wheel.

sec17-F02-card.question_text: How does poor vision affect hazard handling in traffic?
sec17-F02-card.teaching_text: Blurry sight steals precious seconds before you recognize brake lights, pedestrians, or slick patches.

sec17-F03-card.question_text: What minimum visual acuity passes Delaware's licensing vision screening?
sec17-F03-card.teaching_text: Scoring at least twenty over forty in one eye, with or without lenses, clears unrestricted screening.

sec17-F04-card.question_text: What driving restriction applies to Delaware applicants with twenty-over-fifty vision?
sec17-F04-card.teaching_text: Reduced acuity at twenty over fifty restricts driving privileges strictly to daytime hours.

sec17-F05-card.question_text: What helps peripheral vision catch side hazards while you look ahead?
sec17-F05-card.teaching_text: Peripheral sight spots motion early, yet mirrors and quick head checks confirm blind-spot clearance.

sec17-F06-card.question_text: Does sharp eyesight automatically guarantee accurate speed and distance judgment?
sec17-F06-card.teaching_text: Even drivers with crisp eyes need on-road practice to gauge how fast oncoming gaps close.

sec17-F07-card.question_text: In which three driving situations is accurate speed and distance judgment critical?
sec17-F07-card.teaching_text: Misjudging closing speed on highway merges, two-lane passes, or train crossings causes severe crashes.

sec17-F08-card.question_text: Why doesn't crisp daytime eyesight guarantee easy nighttime driving?
sec17-F08-card.teaching_text: Low contrast and oncoming headlight glare strain eyes far differently than bright afternoon sun.

sec17-F09-card.question_text: What does the handbook advise if you struggle to see clearly at night?
sec17-F09-card.teaching_text: Cutting optional after-dark errands and slowing down when night trips are unavoidable reduces risk.

sec17-F10-card.question_text: How often does the Delaware handbook recommend getting your eyes checked by a specialist?
sec17-F10-card.teaching_text: Gradual vision changes sneak up unnoticed without an eye exam every one or two years.

sec17-F11-card.question_text: What happens if you drive without glasses or contacts required on your license?
sec17-F11-card.teaching_text: Skipping mandatory corrective lenses compromises road safety and violates your license restriction.

sec17-F12-card.question_text: Why should corrective-lens wearers keep a spare pair of glasses inside the car?
sec17-F12-card.teaching_text: Broken frames or a lost contact lens miles from home never strands you if spares ride in the glovebox.

sec17-F13-card.question_text: Why must you avoid wearing sunglasses or tinted contact lenses at night?
sec17-F13-card.teaching_text: Tinted lenses cut scarce nighttime light even further, hiding dark pedestrians and unlit hazards.

sec17-F14-card.question_text: Which three traffic sounds can alert you to nearby danger?
sec17-F14-card.teaching_text: Screeching rubber, wailing sirens, or warning horns often signal trouble before it enters view.

sec17-F15-card.question_text: How can drivers compensate when gradual hearing difficulty develops?
sec17-F15-card.teaching_text: Stepping up mirror checks and active visual scanning offsets quieter awareness of horns or sirens.

sec17-F16-card.question_text: How does fatigue weaken your mental and visual performance behind the wheel?
sec17-F16-card.teaching_text: Exhausted drivers miss peripheral cues and hesitate longer when sudden hazards demand brisk action.

sec17-F17-card.question_text: What mood shift and severe crash risk rise as driver fatigue deepens?
sec17-F17-card.teaching_text: Tiredness frays patience first and can tip into nodding off at highway speed without warning.

sec17-R01-card.question_text: How should you prepare your sleep schedule before starting a long road trip?
sec17-R01-card.teaching_text: Starting a multi-hour drive right after a full work shift invites early highway drowsiness.

sec17-R02-card.question_text: Why does the handbook suggest eating lightly before a long drive?
sec17-R02-card.teaching_text: Light snacks sustain alertness, whereas big heavy meals often bring post-lunch drowsiness.

sec17-R03-card.question_text: How often should you plan rest breaks on a long drive?
sec17-R03-card.teaching_text: Building hourly stops into your travel schedule keeps eyes fresh without rushing to beat the clock.

sec17-R04-card.question_text: What should you do during a highway rest stop to refresh alertness?
sec17-R04-card.teaching_text: Stretching your legs outdoors restores circulation far better than staying slumped in the seat.

sec17-R05-card.question_text: Which nighttime hours should you try to avoid driving?
sec17-R05-card.teaching_text: Your circadian body clock pulls hardest toward sleep during overnight hours when you usually rest.

sec17-R06-card.question_text: What are the safe options once you start feeling sleepy behind the wheel?
sec17-R06-card.teaching_text: Coffee or cold air never replaces genuine sleep, so park safely or hand keys to a rested driver.

sec17-R07-card.question_text: Does years of driving experience make driving after drinking alcohol safe?
sec17-R07-card.teaching_text: Alcohol slows brain processing and coordination regardless of how many miles a driver has logged.

sec17-R08-card.question_text: Which four legal and financial penalties can follow driving after drinking?
sec17-R08-card.teaching_text: Beyond crash danger, impaired driving triggers steep fines, soaring rates, revocation, and jail time.

sec17-R09-card.question_text: How can minor ailments like a cold, stiff neck, or sore leg affect driving?
sec17-R09-card.teaching_text: A stiff neck blocks blind-spot head turns while a sore right leg slows emergency pedal transfers.

sec17-R10-card.question_text: What does the handbook recommend when you feel unwell yet have to travel?
sec17-R10-card.teaching_text: Handing over the wheel when sick keeps fever, sneezing, or medication drowsiness out of traffic.

sec17-R11-card.question_text: Which intense emotional states can interfere with safe driving?
sec17-R11-card.teaching_text: Intense feelings hijack mental focus away from scanning mirrors, signals, and changing traffic.

sec17-R12-card.question_text: What should you do before driving if you feel angry or overly excited?
sec17-R12-card.teaching_text: Taking a brisk walk lets adrenaline fade before you touch the accelerator.

sec17-R13-card.question_text: How can trip planning prevent impatience and risky speeding?
sec17-R13-card.teaching_text: Giving yourself a time cushion removes the temptation to tailgate, speed, or force tight yellow lights.

sec17-R14-card.question_text: What two deadly mistakes must impatience never push you into at a railroad crossing?
sec17-R14-card.teaching_text: Saving two minutes at lowered crossing gates is never worth risking a fatal locomotive strike.

sec18-F01-card.question_text: How can you lower the chance of suffering a mechanical breakdown on the road?
sec18-F01-card.teaching_text: Routine fluid, brake, and tire service catches worn parts in a shop rather than on highways.

sec18-F02-card.question_text: Why must you never turn the ignition to Lock while your vehicle is rolling?
sec18-F02-card.teaching_text: Clicking into Lock latches the steering column rigid, sending a rolling car helplessly off course.

sec18-F03-card.question_text: What is your first pedal move if your service brakes suddenly stop working?
sec18-F03-card.teaching_text: Rapid pedal pumps can build enough residual hydraulic pressure for one controlled roadside stop.

sec18-F04-card.question_text: How should you apply the parking brake if pumping failed foot brakes builds zero pressure?
sec18-F04-card.teaching_text: Easing on the parking brake slows rear wheels without snapping them into an uncontrollable spin.

sec18-F05-card.question_text: What two steps remain if neither pedal pumping nor the parking brake stops a brake-failure roll?
sec18-F05-card.teaching_text: Lower gears add engine drag while you aim toward an open uphill or clear roadside spot.

sec18-F06-card.question_text: Once you bring a vehicle with failed brakes to rest, may you keep driving it?
sec18-F06-card.teaching_text: Attempting to limp home without working hydraulic brakes risks catastrophic intersection or downhill collisions.

sec18-F07-card.question_text: Why must you check your brakes right after driving through deep water?
sec18-F07-card.teaching_text: Soaked linings grab unevenly on one side or lose stopping bite completely until dried.

sec18-F08-card.question_text: Which three inputs make up Delaware's procedure for drying wet brakes?
sec18-F08-card.teaching_text: Gentle friction heat evaporates water off brake rotors and drums without overheating hardware.

sec18-F09-card.question_text: How often should you recheck brake action while drying soaked brakes?
sec18-F09-card.teaching_text: Brief checks every two hundred feet confirm when straight, firm stopping bite returns.

sec18-F10-card.question_text: What should you avoid and do immediately if your wheels run off the pavement?
sec18-F10-card.teaching_text: Slamming the brake pedal across uneven half-gravel, half-asphalt grip spins your car violently sideways.

sec18-F11-card.question_text: Why is a strong grip on the steering wheel vital when tires drop onto a rough shoulder?
sec18-F11-card.teaching_text: Soft dirt and ruts tug front tires sideways unless both hands hold steady.

sec18-F12-card.question_text: Which three conditions must be met before steering from a shoulder back onto pavement?
sec18-F12-card.teaching_text: Dropping to fifteen miles per hour or under under full control with clear lanes prevents overcorrection.

sec18-F13-card.question_text: What lane boundary must you avoid crossing as your tires climb back onto the roadway?
sec18-F13-card.teaching_text: Cranking too hard up a pavement lip launches cars across center paint into oncoming traffic.

sec18-F14-card.question_text: How should you steer and manage speed when a tire suddenly deflates?
sec18-F14-card.teaching_text: Keeping the car tracking straight while momentum bleeds off prevents rolling the flat off its rim.

sec18-F15-card.question_text: How should you use your pedals and where should you head with a sudden flat tire?
sec18-F15-card.teaching_text: Coasting down before gentle braking guides you onto firm flat ground clear of moving lanes.

sec18-F16-card.question_text: How do steering and braking feel when your engine dies while moving, and where should you go?
sec18-F16-card.teaching_text: Loss of vacuum and hydraulic assist requires stronger arm pull and firmer foot pressure while coasting off.

sec18-F17-card.question_text: What quick control action should you try first if your headlights suddenly go dark?
sec18-F17-card.teaching_text: Working a dirty contact or tripped breaker switch a few times can relight beams instantly.

sec18-F18-card.question_text: What lights should you use and what should you do if cycling the switch fails to restore headlights?
sec18-F18-card.teaching_text: Turn signals, four-way flashers, or fog lamps mark your car just long enough to pull off.

sec18-F19-card.question_text: What four-part sequence handles a stuck accelerator safely?
sec18-F19-card.teaching_text: Eyes stay up while neutral disconnects power, letting you park safely before killing ignition.

sec18-F20-card.question_text: What immediate action does smoke rising from under your hood require?
sec18-F20-card.teaching_text: Under-hood smoke can flash into engine fire within seconds, demanding an immediate roadside exit.

sec18-F21-card.question_text: How should everyone evacuate if a train approaches your car stalled on railroad tracks?
sec18-F21-card.teaching_text: Moving far clear toward the approaching locomotive keeps you behind forward-flying crash wreckage.

sec18-F22-card.question_text: Which three vehicle actions can avert a threatened collision?
sec18-F22-card.teaching_text: Remembering steering and acceleration alongside braking gives you three ways out of sudden traps.

sec18-F23-card.question_text: Where should you verify how your specific vehicle's antilock brake system operates?
sec18-F23-card.teaching_text: Reading your car's manual beforehand prevents confusion when emergency ABS pulsing kicks in.

sec18-F24-card.question_text: How should you use the brake pedal during an emergency stop with working ABS?
sec18-F24-card.teaching_text: Keeping steady foot force lets ABS cycle valves rapidly even while the pedal pushes against your shoe.

sec18-F25-card.question_text: How hard should you apply non-ABS brakes in an emergency stop?
sec18-F25-card.teaching_text: Rolling tires right near their grip limit stop shorter and steer cleaner than locked sliding rubber.

sec18-F26-card.question_text: What must you do if non-ABS emergency braking locks your wheels into a skid?
sec18-F26-card.teaching_text: Quickly easing off restores rolling grip so you can squeeze firm brake pressure again.

sec18-F27-card.question_text: How should you grip the wheel and prepare when steering quickly around a collision?
sec18-F27-card.teaching_text: Two-handed control lets you stabilize weight transfer immediately after dodging the initial obstacle.

sec18-F28-card.question_text: Where should your eyes and steering aim during an evasive swerve?
sec18-F28-card.teaching_text: Dodging one bumper without aiming into a clean lane sends cars straight into trees or oncoming traffic.

sec18-R01-card.question_text: How does emergency steering differ between ABS-equipped cars and non-ABS cars?
sec18-R01-card.teaching_text: ABS lets you brake and steer together, whereas non-ABS drivers must release the pedal before turning.

sec18-R02-card.question_text: Which two mistakes cause a non-ABS vehicle to plow straight ahead during a quick turn?
sec18-R02-card.teaching_text: Cranking locked or over-angled front tires breaks cornering bite, sliding the nose straight forward.

sec18-R03-card.question_text: When can pressing the gas help avoid a crash, and what comes right afterward?
sec18-R03-card.teaching_text: Brisk acceleration clears an open intersection or rear threat, followed promptly by easing back to safe speed.

sec18-R04-card.question_text: What road conditions and driver pace multiply skid risk during sudden stops or turns?
sec18-R04-card.teaching_text: High speed demands heavy cornering force right when water, snow, or ice slashes available grip.

sec18-R05-card.question_text: What physical event defines a vehicle skid?
sec18-R05-card.teaching_text: Once braking, acceleration, or cornering force exceeds tire friction, rubber slides instead of rolling.

sec18-R06-card.question_text: Which restraints cut injury risk when a crash cannot be avoided?
sec18-R06-card.teaching_text: Tucking a shoulder strap behind your back forfeits upper-body protection when impact hits.

sec18-R07-card.question_text: Beyond cushioning first impact, how else do lap and shoulder restraints help in multi-impact crashes?
sec18-R07-card.teaching_text: Staying pinned behind the wheel lets you steer or brake instead of bouncing across seats before hit two.

sec18-R08-card.question_text: What must uninvolved drivers avoid doing when emergency crews are already working a crash scene?
sec18-R08-card.teaching_text: Sightseeing stops clog lanes needed by ambulances and trigger secondary rear-end pileups.

sec18-R09-card.question_text: Where must your focus stay while driving past a roadside crash?
sec18-R09-card.teaching_text: Dazed occupants, tow operators, or police officers may step near live lanes around wreckage.

sec18-R10-card.question_text: What is the first legal duty of any driver involved in a crash?
sec18-R10-card.teaching_text: Driving off from any collision turns an accident into a serious hit-and-run offense.

sec18-R11-card.question_text: What must you try to do first after striking an unattended parked vehicle?
sec18-R11-card.teaching_text: Checking nearby storefronts or homes lets you exchange details directly before leaving a note.

sec18-R12-card.question_text: What must you do with police when a crash involves injury or death?
sec18-R12-card.teaching_text: Officers must investigate serious crashes firsthand and collect full statements before anyone departs.

sec18-R13-card.question_text: Which three groups of supplies does the handbook suggest packing in a vehicle emergency kit?
sec18-R13-card.teaching_text: Reflectors, bandages, and basic tools handle minor roadside trouble safely until help arrives.

sec18-R14-card.question_text: When must a driver try to move or arrange removal of a damaged car blocking traffic?
sec18-R14-card.teaching_text: Promptly clearing non-injury fender-benders off live travel lanes prevents high-speed secondary rear-end crashes.

sec18-R15-card.question_text: Where must you avoid standing or walking at a collision scene?
sec18-R15-card.teaching_text: Inspecting bumper damage while standing in an active lane invites getting struck by passing cars.

sec18-R16-card.question_text: Why must nobody smoke near wrecked vehicles?
sec18-R16-card.teaching_text: One spark or cigarette ash can ignite invisible gasoline vapors leaking under crushed hoods.

sec18-R17-card.question_text: How should you treat downed power lines or wires lying across the road?
sec18-R17-card.teaching_text: Even silent, spark-free wires can carry lethal high voltage across wet pavement.

sec18-R18-card.question_text: Why should you warn approaching traffic after a collision?
sec18-R18-card.teaching_text: Flashers and triangles alert oncoming traffic before one wreck turns into a multi-car pileup.

sec18-R19-card.question_text: Which responders must be called for crash injuries, and what extra hazard must police be told?
sec18-R19-card.teaching_text: Immediate dispatcher fire alerts send fire engines rolling right alongside paramedics and patrol officers.

sec18-R20-card.question_text: When a crash causes apparent property damage, when and where must a driver stop?
sec18-R20-card.teaching_text: Even minor fender scrapes require an immediate stop right at the scene.

sec18-R21-card.question_text: Which six details must drivers exchange after a property-damage, injury, or fatal crash?
sec18-R21-card.teaching_text: Swapping full identity, registration, license, insurer name, and policy number satisfies Delaware law.

sec18-R22-card.question_text: Whose names and addresses should you gather at a crash scene?
sec18-R22-card.teaching_text: Independent witness contacts and injured-party records document facts accurately after cars clear.

sec18-R23-card.question_text: What information must go on a visible note if you cannot locate a struck parked car's owner?
sec18-R23-card.teaching_text: Leaving clear contact details alongside exact crash date and time fulfills your reporting duty.

sec18-R24-card.question_text: Which police agency must receive an immediate report of an injury or fatal crash?
sec18-R24-card.teaching_text: Notifying the police agency covering the crash scene dispatches local investigators without jurisdictional delay.

sec18-R25-card.question_text: At what apparent property-damage dollar amount on a public highway must you notify police immediately?
sec18-R25-card.teaching_text: Modern bumper repairs cross five hundred dollars fast, making immediate police reporting standard.

sec18-R26-card.question_text: What dual condition involving impairment and damage triggers mandatory immediate police reporting?
sec18-R26-card.teaching_text: Apparent alcohol or drug impairment paired with one thousand dollars or more in damage mandates immediate police notice.

sec18-R27-card.question_text: Where should you directly report urgent Delaware road issues like dead signals, debris, damaged signs, or unsafe work zones?
sec18-R27-card.teaching_text: Alerting the DelDOT Transportation Management Center dispatches road crews straight to dangerous signal or debris hazards.

sec08-F01-card.question_text: What do Delaware right-of-way laws identify, and should you still yield to prevent a crash when someone else ought to?
sec08-F01-card.teaching_text: Delaware statutes never grant anyone absolute right-of-way—insisting on your turn into an oncoming mistake causes avoidable wrecks.

sec08-F02-card.question_text: Which three groups of road users must obey traffic signs and signals on Delaware streets and highways?
sec08-F02-card.teaching_text: Predictable intersections depend on pedestrians, bicyclists, and motorists following the same traffic-control network.

sec08-F03-card.question_text: What three steps does Delaware's red-light camera program perform when a driver runs a signal?
sec08-F03-card.teaching_text: Automated intersection cameras capture clear tag evidence and mail citations even when no patrol car is nearby.

sec08-F04-card.question_text: What core action does each basic signal color—red, yellow, and green—stand for?
sec08-F04-card.teaching_text: Green never means floor it blindly—it calls for cautious progress while yellow means prepare to stop.

sec08-F05-card.question_text: Which traffic movements are governed by an illuminated signal arrow?
sec08-F05-card.teaching_text: Drivers in through lanes must never roll forward just because an adjacent turn-lane green arrow illuminates.

sec08-F06-card.question_text: In what exact order of pavement landmarks must you stop at a steady red signal?
sec08-F06-card.teaching_text: Creeping past the painted stop bar blocks crosswalk ramps and puts your bumper into turning truck paths.

sec08-F07-card.question_text: When is a right turn at a steady red light permitted in Delaware?
sec08-F07-card.teaching_text: Either a posted no-turn-on-red sign or a steady red arrow makes turning right on red illegal.

sec08-F08-card.question_text: Between what street types is a left turn on red legal after a full stop unless barred?
sec08-F08-card.teaching_text: Turning left on red onto or from a two-way street crosses opposing lanes and is illegal.

sec08-F09-card.question_text: What transition does a steady yellow signal announce, and when may you cross instead of stopping?
sec08-F09-card.teaching_text: Slamming brakes inside the dilemma zone risks rear-end crashes, so clear cautiously only when too close to stop safely.

sec08-F10-card.question_text: What movements does a steady green light permit, and what overrides a turn on green?
sec08-F10-card.teaching_text: A green ball allows straight or turning movement unless a separate turn sign or red arrow forbids turning.

sec08-F11-card.question_text: Who still has priority over you when your signal turns green?
sec08-F11-card.teaching_text: Launching on a fresh green without letting leftover cross-traffic or pedestrians clear causes intersection T-bones.

sec08-F12-card.question_text: Which two road-user groups demand special care when you turn on a green light?
sec08-F12-card.teaching_text: Unprotected green turns share phase time with oncoming straight cars and parallel crosswalk pedestrians.

sec08-F13-card.question_text: How must you treat a flashing red traffic signal?
sec08-F13-card.teaching_text: Rolling through a flashing red without stopping completely carries the same crash and ticket risk as blowing a stop sign.

sec08-F14-card.question_text: What three responses does a flashing yellow traffic signal call for?
sec08-F14-card.teaching_text: Cross-street traffic usually faces a stop sign or flashing red, so ease off the throttle and scan cross-lanes.

sec08-F15-card.question_text: What must you do when an installed intersection signal has no lights illuminated?
sec08-F15-card.teaching_text: Storm power outages turn busy signalized crossroads into conflict zones where approaching cars may not stop.

sec08-F16-card.question_text: How does a round signal lens differ in scope from an arrow lens?
sec08-F16-card.teaching_text: Reading round balls versus arrows quickly prevents misapplying a turn-only phase to straight lanes.

sec08-F17-card.question_text: What does a steady red arrow require, and can you turn in its direction on red?
sec08-F17-card.teaching_text: Unlike a round red ball, a steady red arrow completely bans turning in that arrow's direction.

sec08-F18-card.question_text: When does a flashing red arrow allow you to turn in its pointed direction?
sec08-F18-card.teaching_text: Contrast steady and flashing red arrows carefully because steady forbids turning while flashing permits turning after stopping.

sec08-F19-card.question_text: What interval does a steady yellow arrow end, and when should you continue through?
sec08-F19-card.teaching_text: Your protected turn phase is ending, meaning oncoming through lanes are seconds away from getting green.

sec08-F20-card.question_text: What must you do before turning on a flashing yellow arrow?
sec08-F20-card.teaching_text: Flashing yellow arrows mean permissive turning—oncoming traffic has green, so wait for a clean gap.

sec08-F21-card.question_text: What movement does a steady green arrow allow, and to whom must you still yield?
sec08-F21-card.teaching_text: Even on a protected green arrow, anyone still lawfully finishing in the intersection or crosswalk keeps priority.

sec08-F22-card.question_text: Where vehicle and pedestrian signals operate together, which indication governs drivers and which governs walkers?
sec08-F22-card.teaching_text: Watching pedestrian countdowns to jump a red light causes crashes when delayed-green or turn phases run first.

sec08-F23-card.question_text: What should a pedestrian still watch out for while crossing on a WALK signal?
sec08-F23-card.teaching_text: Right-turning and permissive left-turning vehicles often cross active WALK crosswalks during the same cycle.

sec08-F24-card.question_text: What duty does a driver owe to a pedestrian crossing with a WALK indication?
sec08-F24-card.teaching_text: Turning across a pedestrian's WALK phase without yielding is a prime urban collision and road-test failure.

sec08-F25-card.question_text: What should a pedestrian already in the street do if DON'T WALK starts flashing?
sec08-F25-card.teaching_text: The flashing clearance interval gives walkers already in the roadway time to reach the far curb before cross-traffic starts.

sec08-F26-card.question_text: May a pedestrian still on the curb step out once DON'T WALK is flashing?
sec08-F26-card.teaching_text: Stepping off the curb late into the clearance phase leaves too few seconds before cross-traffic gets green.

sec08-F27-card.question_text: What does a steady DON'T WALK signal mean to a pedestrian?
sec08-F27-card.teaching_text: Steady DON'T WALK means conflicting vehicle lanes actively hold green through your crosswalk.

sec08-F28-card.question_text: Through what three nonvisual channels do accessible pedestrian signals share crossing information?
sec08-F28-card.teaching_text: Tactile vibrating pushbuttons and locator tones let pedestrians with vision loss cross complex intersections independently.

sec08-F29-card.question_text: What specific timing do accessible pedestrian signals communicate to blind or visually impaired walkers?
sec08-F29-card.teaching_text: Extra patience around accessible crossings matters because visually impaired pedestrians rely on audible start-and-end cues.

sec08-F30-card.question_text: At which two tricky intersection layouts can audible pedestrian signals also guide crossing direction?
sec08-F30-card.teaching_text: Skewed corners and multi-lane boulevards make staying aligned inside crosswalk lines hard without directional audio.

sec08-F31-card.question_text: What triggers a HAWK crossing sequence, and what happens after pedestrians finish and traffic resumes?
sec08-F31-card.teaching_text: HAWK beacons stay dark until pressed, cycle to stop vehicles for walkers, and return dark afterward.

sec08-F32-card.question_text: How are rectangular rapid-flashing beacons activated at pedestrian or bicycle crossings?
sec08-F32-card.teaching_text: Because RRFBs only flash when someone actively presses the crossing button, treat active strobes as an immediate person-present alert.

sec08-F33-card.question_text: What distinctive light pattern distinguishes a rectangular rapid-flashing beacon from a standard round beacon?
sec08-F33-card.teaching_text: That irregular high-frequency stutter catches peripheral driver vision far faster than a slow steady blink.

sec08-F34-card.question_text: What three steps must you take when a rapid-flashing crossing beacon is operating?
sec08-F34-card.teaching_text: Check both curbs and every adjacent lane so you never pass a stopped car hiding a crossing cyclist.

sec08-F35-card.question_text: Who is governed by circular or arrow signals paired with a bicycle sign?
sec08-F35-card.teaching_text: Dedicated bike signals separate straight-ahead cyclists from right-turning motor vehicles at busy corners.

sec08-F36-card.question_text: What do red, yellow, and green bicycle-shaped signal lenses mean for riders in designated bike lanes or paths?
sec08-F36-card.teaching_text: Red, yellow, and green bike-icon lenses carry identical stop, prepare, and proceed rules inside bike facilities.

sec08-F37-card.question_text: Which signals govern bicyclists riding inside general motor-vehicle traffic lanes?
sec08-F37-card.teaching_text: Outside dedicated bike lanes, cyclists share regular travel lanes and obey standard vehicle signals.

sec08-F38-card.question_text: Which four visual features help drivers recognize a highway sign's message quickly?
sec08-F38-card.teaching_text: Standardized silhouettes and colors let you read a sign's category through rain, snow, or glare before reading text.

sec08-F39-card.question_text: What kind of rules do regulatory signs communicate, and what five examples are listed?
sec08-F39-card.teaching_text: Unlike advisory warnings, disobeying a regulatory sign's speed, turn, lane, direction, or parking rule is a traffic violation.

sec08-F40-card.question_text: Which colors and shapes are commonly used for regulatory signs?
sec08-F40-card.teaching_text: Vertical white rectangles dominate speed and lane rules, while special octagons and triangles reserve Stop and Yield.

sec08-F41-card.question_text: Which highway sign is the only eight-sided shape, and what are its colors?
sec08-F41-card.teaching_text: Even from behind or covered in frost, an eight-sided silhouette identifies a stop sign unmistakably.

sec08-F42-card.question_text: In what order of pavement positions must you come to a full stop at a stop sign?
sec08-F42-card.teaching_text: Stop signs use the exact same three-tier stopping hierarchy as a steady red traffic light.

sec08-F43-card.question_text: Who must you yield to and check for before pulling away from a stop sign?
sec08-F43-card.teaching_text: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians hide easily behind windshield A-pillars if you only scan for large SUVs.

sec08-F44-card.question_text: What must you do for cross-traffic and pedestrians at a yield sign?
sec08-F44-card.teaching_text: Treating a yield sign as a rolling merge when cross-traffic is close causes right-angle and ramp collisions.

sec08-F45-card.question_text: How should you approach a yield sign as you near the intersection?
sec08-F45-card.teaching_text: Slowing early gives you space to scan left and right smoothly without slamming brakes at the line.

sec08-F46-card.question_text: What does a posted speed-limit sign establish?
sec08-F46-card.teaching_text: Posted speed signs set the legal ceiling under ideal conditions rather than a target during storms.

sec08-F47-card.question_text: Which three turning maneuvers can international red-circle-and-slash signs prohibit in Delaware?
sec08-F47-card.teaching_text: A red circle with a diagonal slash over a curved arrow bans that exact turn instantly across any language.

sec08-R01-card.question_text: What must you do when an overhead lane sign shows an arrow marked ONLY?
sec08-R01-card.teaching_text: Diving straight out of an ONLY turn lane sideswipes adjacent drivers following proper lane arrows.

sec08-R02-card.question_text: What color scheme and shape characterize most standard highway warning signs?
sec08-R02-card.teaching_text: Spotting a yellow diamond ahead gives early notice of curves, merges, or surface changes.

sec08-R03-card.question_text: What driver response do warning signs call for?
sec08-R03-card.teaching_text: Easing speed before reaching the hazard keeps braking margin in reserve if the road ahead is blocked.

sec08-R04-card.question_text: What is the exclusive meaning of a five-sided warning sign, and what two background colors may it use?
sec08-R04-card.teaching_text: A house-shaped five-sided sign always means a school zone or school crossing, often in high-visibility fluorescent yellow-green.

sec08-R05-card.question_text: What three actions are required when approaching a school-warning sign?
sec08-R05-card.teaching_text: Children dart unpredictably near school crosswalks and buses, demanding lower speed and instant stopping readiness.

sec08-R06-card.question_text: What hazard does a circular yellow sign with black markings warn of in advance?
sec08-R06-card.teaching_text: Only advance railroad warnings use a yellow circle, giving you early notice before reaching the tracks.

sec08-R07-card.question_text: How should you respond to an advance rail-crossing sign, and when is extra caution emphasized?
sec08-R07-card.teaching_text: Dark freight cars straddling unlit rural tracks can swallow oncoming headlights until you are dangerously close.

sec08-R08-card.question_text: What action does a sharp-right-turn warning sign call for?
sec08-R08-card.teaching_text: Braking before entering a tight ninety-degree bend keeps tires gripping instead of skidding wide mid-corner.

sec08-R09-card.question_text: What adjustment does a winding-road warning sign call for?
sec08-R09-card.teaching_text: Linked S-curves shift weight side to side rapidly, requiring steady adjusted speed before the first bend.

sec08-R10-card.question_text: What should you prepare for when you pass a yield-ahead warning sign?
sec08-R10-card.teaching_text: Advance yield signs protect blind curves or hills where the upcoming yield triangle appears late.

sec08-R11-card.question_text: Where should you scan when passing a bicycle warning sign on a shared roadway?
sec08-R11-card.teaching_text: Trails and cross-streets feed riders from left and right alike along shared-road corridors.

sec08-R12-card.question_text: What driver response does a narrowing-road warning call for?
sec08-R12-card.teaching_text: Narrowing shoulders and tighter lane widths shrink error margins with oncoming vehicles.

sec08-R13-card.question_text: Which side must you steer toward when a divided-highway-ahead warning appears?
sec08-R13-card.teaching_text: Drifting left of the median nose puts you head-on into wrong-way oncoming lanes.

sec08-R14-card.question_text: What two steps apply at a warning of an unpaved or unknown road surface?
sec08-R14-card.teaching_text: Dropping off asphalt onto loose gravel cuts tire traction sharply and lengthens stopping distances.

sec08-R15-card.question_text: How must you drive where the roadway narrows down to room for only one traffic lane?
sec08-R15-card.teaching_text: One-lane bridges and narrow underpasses require yielding cooperatively so opposing cars never meet mid-span.

sec08-R16-card.question_text: What two precautions apply at a warning for a potentially hazardous two-lane passage?
sec08-R16-card.teaching_text: Tight two-lane bridges or culverts leave minimal mirror clearance when wide trucks approach opposite you.

sec08-R17-card.question_text: At an added-lane warning sign, do you have to merge, and what must you still watch for?
sec08-R17-card.teaching_text: Unlike a merge sign, an added-lane diamond gives incoming traffic its own lane while drivers still cross over.

sec08-R18-card.question_text: How should you prepare for a steep hill warning to control speed without overheating brakes?
sec08-R18-card.teaching_text: Engine braking in a lower gear holds downhill speed steady instead of cooking brake pads to fade.

sec08-R19-card.question_text: Which time window of rainfall is identified as the most hazardous on slippery-when-wet pavement?
sec08-R19-card.teaching_text: Fresh rain floats accumulated oil and grease to the top of asphalt before heavier downpours wash residue away.

sec08-R20-card.question_text: What transition does a two-way-traffic warning sign mark?
sec08-R20-card.teaching_text: Staying in the left lane past the end of a one-way or divided stretch puts oncoming traffic head-on.

sec08-R21-card.question_text: Why does a bump warning sign call for adjusting your speed?
sec08-R21-card.teaching_text: Hitting a sharp frost heave or speed bump fast bottoms suspension out and jolts steering control.

sec08-R22-card.question_text: Why must drivers exercise heightened caution near a playground warning sign?
sec08-R22-card.teaching_text: Chasing balls or riding scooters around parks can send children into the street without looking.

sec08-R23-card.question_text: Where should you scan when driving past a deer-crossing warning sign?
sec08-R23-card.teaching_text: Deer travel in small groups across wooded shoulders, so spotting one often means another follows right behind.

sec08-R24-card.question_text: What speed and yielding rules apply when approaching a roundabout warning sign?
sec08-R24-card.teaching_text: Traffic already circling inside the ring plus crosswalk walkers at the entry splitter island always hold right-of-way.

sec08-R25-card.question_text: What two things should you watch for after seeing a four-way crossroad warning sign?
sec08-R25-card.teaching_text: Hidden rural crossroads may pair with stop signs, flashing beacons, or fast cross-traffic emerging behind hedgerows.

sec08-R26-card.question_text: What does an advisory-speed plaque communicate, and where is it usually mounted?
sec08-R26-card.teaching_text: Yellow square speed plaques beneath curve or exit diamonds show the safe engineered speed for that bend.

sec08-R27-card.question_text: How should you drive after passing a farm-machinery warning on a shared rural road?
sec08-R27-card.teaching_text: Tractors and combines move well under highway speed, so closing distances shrink surprisingly fast over hillcrests.

sec08-R28-card.question_text: What driver readiness does a horse-drawn-vehicle warning sign call for?
sec08-R28-card.teaching_text: Delaware rural routes share lanes with slow horse-drawn buggies where sudden closing speed or horn blasts startle animals.

sec08-R29-card.question_text: How do drivers perform a proper zipper merge when a lane drops ahead?
sec08-R29-card.teaching_text: Using both open lanes up to the taper point and alternating smoothly cuts backup length and road-rage blocking.

sec08-R30-card.question_text: What shape and color combination do most highway destination guide signs use?
sec08-R30-card.teaching_text: White-on-green rectangles let you separate exit directions and mileage guides from yellow warnings or white laws.

sec08-R31-card.question_text: What does an arrow on a green destination guide sign tell you?
sec08-R31-card.teaching_text: Reading guide arrows early lets you position smoothly in the right exit or turn lane ahead of the junction.

sec08-R32-card.question_text: What colors and emblem identify a United States numbered highway marker?
sec08-R32-card.teaching_text: Distinguish white U.S. shields like Route thirteen from white circles used for Delaware state routes.

sec08-R33-card.question_text: What color and shape identify a state route marker in Delaware?
sec08-R33-card.teaching_text: Exam questions contrast the white circle state marker directly against the U.S. shield and red-and-blue Interstate shield.

sec08-R34-card.question_text: How are colors and text arranged on an Interstate route shield?
sec08-R34-card.teaching_text: White INTERSTATE text sits in the red upper crest while the white route number sits over blue below.

sec08-R35-card.question_text: What shape and colors identify motorist-service signs for fuel, food, lodging, or hospitals?
sec08-R35-card.teaching_text: Spotting blue rectangles ahead tells travelers where gas, rest areas, lodging, or medical help sit off an exit.

sec08-R36-card.question_text: What color combination identifies public recreation and cultural-interest guide signs?
sec08-R36-card.teaching_text: Brown backgrounds mark parks, beaches, campgrounds, and historic sites without competing with green highway exit signs.

sec08-R37-card.question_text: What two purposes can flashing beacons mounted on a sign serve?
sec08-R37-card.teaching_text: School-speed signs often use flashing beacons to show drivers the exact minutes reduced limits are enforced.

sec08-R38-card.question_text: What color are flashing beacons that supplement warning or speed-limit signs?
sec08-R38-card.teaching_text: Yellow supplementary flashers call for heightened attention and speed compliance rather than a mandatory stop.

sec08-R39-card.question_text: What color are flashing beacons mounted with Stop or Do Not Enter signs?
sec08-R39-card.teaching_text: Red beacons reinforce mandatory stopping or wrong-way prohibitions at high-crash rural intersections and ramps.
