sec08-R40-card.question_text: At roughly what flash rate do supplementary circular beacons blink?
sec08-R40-card.teaching_text: Contrast this steady once-per-second circular pulse against the rapid stuttering flash of rectangular crossing beacons.

sec08-R41-card.question_text: Which three types of highway activity define a work zone?
sec08-R41-card.teaching_text: Utility bucket trucks and mowing or pothole crews count as active work zones just like major bridge rebuilds.

sec08-R42-card.question_text: Where do work-zone traffic-control devices start and end relative to the work activity?
sec08-R42-card.teaching_text: Advance warning signs and termination tapers bracket the crew so drivers slow early and stay channeled past hazards.

sec08-R43-card.question_text: Do highway work zones always stay fixed in one location?
sec08-R43-card.teaching_text: Line-painting, sweeping, and patching convoys roll slowly down active lanes, demanding early lane changes.

sec08-R44-card.question_text: Which six types of traffic-control devices may guide drivers through a work zone?
sec08-R44-card.teaching_text: Temporary striping, arrow boards, cones, drums, and barricades override normal lane lines until you clear the zone.

sec08-R45-card.question_text: What background color is usually used for warning signs in highway work zones?
sec08-R45-card.teaching_text: Seeing orange ahead immediately signals temporary construction or utility hazards where workers stand feet from traffic.

sec08-R46-card.question_text: What hidden traffic danger behind hills or curves must you stay alert for in work zones?
sec08-R46-card.teaching_text: Cresting a blind rise at full speed into a stopped work-zone backup causes severe chain-reaction crashes.

sec08-R47-card.question_text: How must drivers respond to police officers and flaggers directing traffic in a work zone?
sec08-R47-card.teaching_text: Live flagger or officer hand and paddle commands override painted lines and standard green signals.

sec08-R48-card.question_text: What should you start preparing to do when you pass a lane-closure warning sign?
sec08-R48-card.teaching_text: Checking mirrors and matching adjacent traffic pace early avoids panicked last-second swerves into cones.

sec08-R49-card.question_text: How are speeding fines penalized inside a Delaware highway work zone?
sec08-R49-card.teaching_text: Doubled fines protect roadside crews who have no steel cabin shielding them from speeding traffic.

sec08-R50-card.question_text: Why should you avoid weaving or abrupt moves and brake gradually inside a work zone?
sec08-R50-card.teaching_text: Rear-end collisions are the top work-zone crash type when sudden panic braking catches trailing cars off guard.

sec08-R51-card.question_text: How should you steer and brake over rough surfaces, metal plates, uneven lanes, or edge drop-offs in work zones?
sec08-R51-card.teaching_text: Jerking the wheel across an uneven lane lip or slick steel plate can pitch tires sideways.

sec08-R52-card.question_text: Why are reasonable speed and extra following cushion critical through a work zone?
sec08-R52-card.teaching_text: Narrow barrier-lined lanes leave zero shoulder escape route, so forward space is your only crash buffer.

sec08-R53-card.question_text: For what three operational reasons might traffic be brought to a full stop in a work zone?
sec08-R53-card.teaching_text: Expect full stops on two-lane repaving jobs where both directions share one alternating open lane.

sec08-R54-card.question_text: Which three controls may manage stopped traffic inside a highway work zone?
sec08-R54-card.teaching_text: Treat a portable red trailer signal or certified flagger's paddle with the exact authority of a permanent intersection light.

sec08-R55-card.question_text: What do regulatory signs inside work zones communicate about speed and rules?
sec08-R55-card.teaching_text: White regulatory speed signs posted inside orange work zones set legally reduced limits carrying doubled fines.

sec08-R56-card.question_text: Which shapes are used for orange warning signs in highway work zones?
sec08-R56-card.teaching_text: Orange diamonds warn of upcoming lane shifts or flaggers while orange rectangles mark road-work distances and ends.

sec08-R57-card.question_text: What two jobs do barricades, drums, cones, and tubular markers perform in a work zone?
sec08-R57-card.teaching_text: Channelizing lines separate live travel lanes from open trenches, wet concrete, and roadside workers.

sec08-R58-card.question_text: Why are steady or flashing lights often mounted atop work-zone channelizing devices?
sec08-R58-card.teaching_text: Amber drum lamps trace shifted lane edges after dark when glare or rain hides painted markings.

sec08-R59-card.question_text: What do flashing or sequencing arrow panels do day and night in work zones?
sec08-R59-card.teaching_text: High-mounted illuminated arrow boards are visible far upstream, letting drivers merge well before the taper.

sec08-R60-card.question_text: Which two signaling tools do work-zone flaggers use to stop, slow, or guide traffic?
sec08-R60-card.teaching_text: Octagonal STOP and orange SLOW paddles give unmistakable instructions supplemented by red flags in emergencies.

sec08-R61-card.question_text: What high-visibility clothing color and garments identify work-zone flaggers?
sec08-R61-card.teaching_text: Fluorescent yellow-green outerwear stands out sharply against orange drums and dark asphalt.

sec12-F01-card.question_text: Why can't reading a driver manual by itself make someone a safe driver?
sec12-F01-card.teaching_text: Books build rule knowledge, while coached behind-the-wheel hours wire muscle memory, hazard timing, and smooth pedal control.

sec12-F02-card.question_text: Which five preparation checks belong in your routine before shifting into gear?
sec12-F02-card.teaching_text: Handling adjustments, inspection, clear glass, restraints, and loose items while parked keeps both hands focused once rolling.

sec12-F03-card.question_text: What two basic questions start smart trip planning before you grab your car keys?
sec12-F03-card.teaching_text: Skipping unneeded drives or hopping on transit cuts traffic exposure, fuel cost, and crash risk.

sec12-F04-card.question_text: Which two benefits come from scheduling drives outside heavy rush-hour periods?
sec12-F04-card.teaching_text: Stop-and-go congestion taxes brakes, transmissions, and driver patience far harder than steady off-peak cruising.

sec12-F05-card.question_text: When does the handbook recommend choosing carpools or shared rides?
sec12-F05-card.teaching_text: Consolidating commuters into fewer vehicles eases highway congestion, qualifies for carpool lanes, and trims fuel burn.

sec12-F06-card.question_text: How can planning your stops ahead of time cut down total driving?
sec12-F06-card.teaching_text: Grouping nearby errands into a single planned loop eliminates cold-engine restarts and extra intersection miles.

sec12-F07-card.question_text: What quick step before leaving home prevents wasted pickup or shopping trips?
sec12-F07-card.teaching_text: Confirming an order or part is actually on the counter spares you a pointless round trip in traffic.

sec12-F08-card.question_text: Who bears legal responsibility for making sure a vehicle is mechanically safe to drive?
sec12-F08-card.teaching_text: Even when borrowing a family car, the person behind the wheel answers legally for bald tires, dead lights, or bad brakes.

sec12-F09-card.question_text: What reference sets your car's service schedule, and who should handle complex mechanical repairs?
sec12-F09-card.teaching_text: Factory intervals keep safety systems reliable, and trained technicians handle critical brake, steering, or suspension repairs safely.

sec12-F10-card.question_text: Which four warning signs mean a mechanic should inspect your brakes right away?
sec12-F10-card.teaching_text: Grinding metal, burnt odors, weak stopping bite, or a pedal dropping toward the carpet warn of imminent brake failure.

sec12-F11-card.question_text: How should you verify that headlights, taillights, brake lights, and turn signals actually illuminate?
sec12-F11-card.teaching_text: Dashboard indicator arrows cannot reveal every burnt rear bulb, making an exterior walkaround or reflection check essential.

sec12-F12-card.question_text: What vital messages do working brake lamps and turn signals send to surrounding drivers?
sec12-F12-card.teaching_text: Burned-out rear lamps leave following traffic guessing until the gap shrinks dangerously fast.

sec12-F13-card.question_text: Which two clues suggest your headlights are misaligned and need a mechanic's aim check?
sec12-F13-card.teaching_text: High-aimed beams blind oncoming traffic into flashing you repeatedly, while low-aimed beams starve your own night sightline.

sec12-F14-card.question_text: Why should chipped or cracked windshield glass be replaced promptly?
sec12-F14-card.teaching_text: Structural glass weakens around stone chips and spider cracks, breaking far more readily during a minor impact.

sec12-F15-card.question_text: What maintenance rule applies to your windshield wipers and rubber blades?
sec12-F15-card.teaching_text: Hardened rubber that smears rain turns oncoming night headlights into a blinding sheet across the glass.

sec12-F16-card.question_text: How do worn or bald tires hurt vehicle control on wet pavement?
sec12-F16-card.teaching_text: Shallow tread grooves cannot channel rain out from under the rubber contact patch, hurting both braking and steering grip.

sec12-F17-card.question_text: Which three problems result from driving on underinflated or unbalanced tires?
sec12-F17-card.teaching_text: Low air pressure flexes sidewalls hot, burns extra fuel, wears tread unevenly, and dulls emergency steering and braking.

sec12-F18-card.question_text: What three ride symptoms tell you to take your car to a mechanic for tire, wheel, or alignment service?
sec12-F18-card.teaching_text: Steering wheel shimmy, rhythmic bouncing, or drifting sideways signals unbalanced wheels, worn shocks, or crooked alignment.

sec12-F19-card.question_text: Which two specific tire emergencies become far more likely when tread wears thin?
sec12-F19-card.teaching_text: Thin rubber skims atop standing water easily and offers almost no barrier against nails, glass, or sharp potholes.

sec12-F20-card.question_text: When should you check tire pressure with a gauge, and where do you find the right PSI target?
sec12-F20-card.teaching_text: Driving heats air and artificially raises gauge readings, and the tire sidewall lists max pressure rather than your car's spec.

sec12-F21-card.question_text: How do you insert a penny to check tread depth, and what visual result means the tire must be replaced?
sec12-F21-card.teaching_text: If rubber grooves fail to touch the top of Abraham Lincoln's head, tread is worn below safe wet-weather depth.

sec12-F22-card.question_text: Which two steering-wheel behaviors call for an immediate mechanical inspection?
sec12-F22-card.teaching_text: Heavy effort or loose free-play before front tires respond warns of failing power-steering fluid, tie rods, or rack gears.

sec12-F23-card.question_text: What symptoms after hitting bumps or braking indicate your suspension needs service?
sec12-F23-card.teaching_text: Worn shocks and struts let tires hop off asphalt after bumps, lengthening stopping distance and destabilizing turns.

sec12-F24-card.question_text: Which three functions does a vehicle's exhaust system perform?
sec12-F24-card.teaching_text: Intact pipes and mufflers muffle combustion roar, cool hot gases, and vent toxic fumes safely behind the bumper.

sec12-F25-card.question_text: How dangerous are leaking exhaust gases if they seep inside the passenger cabin?
sec12-F25-card.teaching_text: Colorless, odorless carbon monoxide poisons bloodstream oxygen rapidly, causing drowsiness, unconsciousness, and death quickly.

sec12-F26-card.question_text: May you warm up or run an engine inside a closed garage?
sec12-F26-card.teaching_text: Lethal carbon monoxide fills an enclosed garage within minutes and seeps into attached living spaces even faster.

sec12-F27-card.question_text: Why should you have your exhaust system inspected periodically even when the muffler sounds quiet?
sec12-F27-card.teaching_text: Pinholes in underbody pipes or gaskets can seep deadly carbon monoxide into floorboards without making a loud roar.

sec12-F28-card.question_text: What muffler requirement applies to a commercial vehicle equipped with an engine-compression brake?
sec12-F28-card.teaching_text: Unmuffled engine retarders create jarring staccato noise blasts, so Delaware requires continuous spec-compliant muffling.

sec12-F29-card.question_text: Which three traffic hazards can result from neglecting routine engine maintenance?
sec12-F29-card.teaching_text: Having an engine hesitate or stall halfway across a busy highway intersection turns deferred maintenance into an acute safety crisis.

sec12-F30-card.question_text: Which two dangers come from leaving loose bottles, bags, or gear unsecured inside the cabin?
sec12-F30-card.teaching_text: Hard braking launches rear-shelf items forward at highway speed and rolls loose floor bottles straight underneath your brake pedal.

sec12-F31-card.question_text: What is the proper safety role of a vehicle's horn?
sec12-F31-card.teaching_text: Horns exist strictly as collision-prevention alerts rather than venting frustration or greeting neighbors.

sec12-F32-card.question_text: Under Delaware rules, what defines a properly secured cargo load?
sec12-F32-card.teaching_text: Dropped lumber, mattresses, or gravel turns highway lanes into obstacle courses and makes the hauling driver liable.

sec12-F33-card.question_text: How should general cargo and heavy large items be fastened onto a pickup bed or trailer?
sec12-F33-card.teaching_text: Relying on gravity fails at the first bump; tie cargo with rope, straps, or nets and anchor bulky items directly to frame tie-downs.

sec12-F34-card.question_text: What three additional cargo steps protect against highway spills and weight instability?
sec12-F34-card.teaching_text: Road vibration loosens knots within the first few miles, so cover loose loads with a tarp, respect weight ratings, and recheck tension.

sec12-F35-card.question_text: What supplies does the handbook recommend carrying in your car for clear windshield visibility?
sec12-F35-card.teaching_text: Bug splatter, road salt, or tree sap can blind you mid-trip when sun glare hits a dirty windshield.

sec12-F36-card.question_text: What kind of windshield-washer fluid is needed whenever temperatures can dip below freezing?
sec12-F36-card.teaching_text: Plain water freezes solid in nozzles and coats cold glass with instant opaque ice the moment you spray.

sec12-F37-card.question_text: Why must you clean the inside surfaces of car windows regularly, especially if anyone smokes?
sec12-F37-card.teaching_text: Off-gassing plastics and tobacco smoke leave an oily interior film that scatters night headlights into a milky glare.

sec12-F38-card.question_text: How much window glass must you clear of snow, ice, and frost before driving away?
sec12-F38-card.teaching_text: Peeking through a tiny scraped porthole leaves side streets, mirrors, and crosswalks completely blind.

sec12-F39-card.question_text: Why shouldn't you hang items from your rear-view mirror or cover the windshield with stickers?
sec12-F39-card.teaching_text: Swinging air fresheners, tassels, and decals create surprising foreground blind zones wide enough to hide a cyclist or walker.

sec12-F40-card.question_text: Which four exterior light sets should you wipe clean of mud, salt, and road grime?
sec12-F40-card.teaching_text: Winter slush and mud crust cut lamp brightness by over half, dimming both your forward beam and rear brake warnings.
sec12-F40-card.must_match_memory_hook: Keep head, tail, brake, reverse clean

visual_sync.text_span: Keep head, tail, brake, reverse clean

sec12-F41-card.question_text: When must you check and adjust your driver's seat and mirrors?
sec12-F41-card.teaching_text: Reaching across to tweak a side mirror or sliding a seat latch while rolling causes sudden lane drift and pedal slips.

sec12-F42-card.question_text: How high and how far back from the steering wheel should you position your driver's seat?
sec12-F42-card.teaching_text: Sitting high enough to see over the dash while keeping about twelve inches of chest clearance gives frontal airbags safe room to deploy.

sec12-F43-card.question_text: How does the Delaware handbook advise setting your outside mirrors relative to the side of your own car?
sec12-F43-card.teaching_text: Flaring side mirrors outward so your own quarter panel appears only when leaning forward shrinks rear-quarter blind spots dramatically.

sec12-F44-card.question_text: How should you set the manual tab or mode on a day-night inside rear-view mirror?
sec12-F44-card.teaching_text: Flipping to night mode dims blinding headlights behind you, while returning to day mode restores bright daytime clarity.

sec12-F45-card.question_text: Where should the head restraint make contact when properly adjusted?
sec12-F45-card.teaching_text: A restraint left low behind your neck acts like a fulcrum in a rear-end crash instead of catching your skull against whiplash.

sec12-F46-card.question_text: What restraint check must the driver complete before pulling away?
sec12-F46-card.teaching_text: One unbelted rider becomes a heavy human projectile inside the cabin during a rollover or T-bone crash.

sec12-F47-card.question_text: May a Delaware police officer pull a vehicle over solely for seeing an unbuckled or improperly buckled occupant?
sec12-F47-card.teaching_text: Delaware enforces primary seat-belt stops, meaning an officer needs no other speeding or equipment violation to pull you over.

sec12-F48-card.question_text: What happens legally and physically if someone tucks the shoulder belt behind their back or under their arm?
sec12-F48-card.teaching_text: Routing webbing under the armpit crushes ribs and internal organs in a crash and counts as a ticketable belt violation.

sec12-F49-card.question_text: In older cars with motorized automatic shoulder belts, what must you still buckle manually?
sec12-F49-card.teaching_text: Riding with an automatic shoulder strap alone lets your lower body submarine forward under the dash in a crash.

sec12-R01-card.question_text: How does wearing a seat belt help you maintain control during an abrupt swerve or side impact?
sec12-R01-card.teaching_text: You cannot steer or brake out of a secondary crash if the initial jolt slides you across the console into the passenger seat.

sec12-R02-card.question_text: Do frontal and side airbags eliminate the need to wear a seat belt?
sec12-R02-card.teaching_text: Airbags are supplemental cushions engineered assuming a belt holds your torso back from explosive deployment force.

sec12-R03-card.question_text: How must children younger than age one always ride according to the NHTSA and AAP guidance in the handbook?
sec12-R03-card.teaching_text: Rear-facing shells cradle an infant's heavy head and fragile spine evenly across the seat back during frontal braking forces.

sec12-R04-card.question_text: How do convertible and all-in-one car seats differ from infant-only carriers for rear-facing use?
sec12-R04-card.teaching_text: Higher weight and height shells let toddlers remain in safer rear-facing protection long after outgrowing an infant carrier.

sec12-R05-card.question_text: When should a child aged one through three transition from rear-facing to a forward-facing harnessed seat?
sec12-R05-card.teaching_text: Turning forward at age one is outdated; keep toddlers rear-facing until reaching the seat manufacturer's top height or weight limit.

sec12-R06-card.question_text: What restraint and seating spot are recommended for children ages eight through twelve until an adult belt fits properly?
sec12-R06-card.teaching_text: Age alone never guarantees belt geometry; kids stay in boosters in the back row until adult lap and shoulder straps align on bone.

sec12-R07-card.question_text: Where must the lap belt and shoulder belt rest on the body for a proper adult-belt fit?
sec12-R07-card.teaching_text: Strong pelvic hips and collarbones absorb crash loads safely, whereas straps riding across a soft belly or neck cause severe internal trauma.

sec12-R08-card.question_text: What three criteria define the right child safety seat choice?
sec12-R08-card.teaching_text: Even the highest-rated seat fails if it does not match your child's size, fit your vehicle's contours, and get buckled right every ride.

sec12-R09-card.question_text: Why must a rear-facing child seat never be placed in front of an active frontal airbag?
sec12-R09-card.teaching_text: An inflating passenger airbag strikes the back of a rear-facing shell right where the baby's head rests with lethal speed.

sec12-R10-card.question_text: How do you test whether a child's car-seat harness straps are tightened snugly enough?
sec12-R10-card.teaching_text: If your fingers can pinch a fold of loose webbing at the child's shoulder, slack can let the child slip partially out on impact.

sec12-R11-card.question_text: At what height on a child's torso should you position the car-seat harness chest clip?
sec12-R11-card.teaching_text: Keeping the plastic retainer clip even with the armpits centers shoulder straps over strong ribcage bone rather than neck or belly.

sec12-R12-card.question_text: How much may a properly installed car seat move at the belt path when checked with moderate force?
sec12-R12-card.teaching_text: Testing right at the belt or lower-anchor path confirms the base will not whip excessively forward, backward, or sideways.

sec12-R13-card.question_text: When installing a forward-facing car seat with either lower anchors or a seat belt, what extra strap should be attached?
sec12-R13-card.teaching_text: Anchoring the top tether strap cuts forward head excursion by several inches in a frontal crash regardless of base method.

sec12-R14-card.question_text: Is holding a baby or young child securely in your arms on your lap ever a safe substitute for a car seat?
sec12-R14-card.teaching_text: Crash deceleration multiplies a child's weight many times over, tearing them from adult arms or crushing them against the dash.

sec12-R15-card.question_text: Which two manuals should you consult to install and use a child safety seat properly?
sec12-R15-card.teaching_text: Anchor locations, tether hooks, and locking retractor rules vary across car models just as routing paths vary across seats.

sec12-R16-card.question_text: May you leave children or pets unattended inside a warm or sunny parked vehicle?
sec12-R16-card.teaching_text: Greenhouse solar heating spikes cabin temperatures to lethal heatstroke extremes within minutes even with windows cracked.

sec12-R17-card.question_text: How does preventing head strikes with a seat belt help you immediately after a crash?
sec12-R17-card.teaching_text: If a vehicle lands in water or catches fire, staying conscious lets you unbuckle and get out quickly.

sec12-R18-card.question_text: What deadly crash outcome outside your own car do seat belts prevent?
sec12-R18-card.teaching_text: Being thrown through glass onto live highway lanes exposes unrestrained occupants to secondary strikes from passing vehicles.

sec12-R19-card.question_text: Which way can unrestrained occupants slide inside the cabin during a side-impact collision?
sec12-R19-card.teaching_text: As the struck vehicle gets shoved sideways underneath them, unbuckled riders effectively slam right toward the intruding door.

sec12-R20-card.question_text: How may a police officer signal a traffic stop, and which side of your car might the officer walk up to?
sec12-R20-card.teaching_text: Officers frequently walk up on the passenger curb side to avoid fast highway traffic passing inches off your left mirror.

sec12-R21-card.question_text: What three pieces of information may an officer share upon reaching your window during a traffic stop?
sec12-R21-card.teaching_text: Knowing standard stop protocol keeps new drivers calm while listening respectfully before reaching into pockets or consoles.

sec12-R22-card.question_text: Which three documents will an officer ask you to produce during a routine traffic stop?
sec12-R22-card.teaching_text: Keeping current registration and insurance accessible in one predictable spot prevents frantic rummaging at night.

sec12-R23-card.question_text: Should the driver or passengers step out of the vehicle during a police traffic stop?
sec12-R23-card.teaching_text: Popping a door open unprompted looks threatening to an approaching officer and exposes you to passing roadside traffic.

sec12-R24-card.question_text: How should you respond as soon as police emergency lights activate behind your car?
sec12-R24-card.teaching_text: Signaling right and easing onto a safe right-side shoulder reassures the officer immediately that you intend to comply safely.

sec12-R25-card.question_text: What four actions should you take right after halting on the shoulder for a police stop?
sec12-R25-card.teaching_text: Shutting down power and audio while resting both hands plainly on the wheel keeps communication clear and calm.

sec12-R26-card.question_text: When should you reach into a glove box or wallet for documents during a traffic stop, and what behaviors must you avoid?
sec12-R26-card.teaching_text: Ducking toward a dark console or floorboard before the officer reaches your window mimics hiding or grabbing a weapon.

sec12-R27-card.question_text: When should you tell the officer if any weapons are inside the vehicle during a traffic stop?
sec12-R27-card.teaching_text: Calmly informing the officer at very first contact while keeping both hands on the wheel prevents dangerous surprises.

sec12-R28-card.question_text: What lighting step might an officer use toward your car during a nighttime traffic stop?
sec12-R28-card.teaching_text: Bright takedown lights and spotlights let the officer see inside dark glass safely, so avoid staring backward into the beam.

sec12-R29-card.question_text: Where and when should you direct a compliment or complaint regarding an officer's conduct?
sec12-R29-card.teaching_text: Roadside shoulders are never the place to argue; official agency complaint or commendation channels handle conduct issues properly afterward.

sec12-R30-card.question_text: What brake should be engaged before starting the engine, alongside following your owner's manual?
sec12-R30-card.teaching_text: Engaging the parking brake anchors the car firmly while cranking so it cannot lurch if a gear interlock ever faults.

sec12-R31-card.question_text: Which gear position is required to start a manual-transmission car, and what pedal is often required too?
sec12-R31-card.teaching_text: Neutral plus clutch disengagement disconnects engine cranking torque from the drive wheels so the car cannot jump forward.

sec12-R32-card.question_text: Which gear selector position should you choose to start an automatic-transmission vehicle?
sec12-R32-card.teaching_text: Park mechanically locks the transmission output pawl in addition to keeping drive gears disengaged during startup.

sec12-R33-card.question_text: Why must you press the accelerator smoothly and gradually rather than flooring it from a stop?
sec12-R33-card.teaching_text: Stomping the throttle breaks tire traction loose and whips the car sideways, especially on rain, snow, or gravel.

sec12-R34-card.question_text: Why must a manual-shift driver practice coordinating clutch release with accelerator pressure?
sec12-R34-card.teaching_text: Releasing the clutch smoothly as gentle gas comes on avoids embarrassing intersection stalls and noisy clutch-burning engine revs.

sec12-R35-card.question_text: Which clock positions does the Delaware handbook recommend for your left and right hands on the steering wheel?
sec12-R35-card.teaching_text: Balanced grip across opposite sides between 8-10 and 2-4 maximizes steering leverage while keeping forearms clear of airbag covers.

sec12-R36-card.question_text: How does scanning far ahead and along both roadsides improve your steering?
sec12-R36-card.teaching_text: Spotting curves, merges, or debris early lets you make tiny progressive wheel inputs instead of jerky panic swerves.

sec12-R37-card.question_text: Which steering technique does the handbook recommend for sharp turns, and how should you straighten out afterward?
sec12-R37-card.teaching_text: Letting a spinning wheel slip freely through open fingers sacrifices control and can over-correct past center.

sec06-F01-card.question_text: Does driving experience make drinking and driving safe, and how does alcohol affect new drivers?
sec06-F01-card.teaching_text: New drivers are still building road habits, so alcohol degrades their coordination and judgment even faster than veterans.

sec06-F02-card.question_text: Which serving sizes of beer, wine, and eighty-proof spirits contain equal amounts of alcohol?
sec06-F02-card.teaching_text: Choosing beer or wine over a one-point-five-ounce shot never lowers alcohol intake when serving sizes match.

sec06-F03-card.question_text: What four financial, licensing, and freedom consequences can follow drinking and driving?
sec06-F03-card.teaching_text: One impaired drive triggers compounding court bills, spiked insurance premiums, lost mobility, and potential prison time.

sec06-F04-card.question_text: How is blood alcohol concentration defined and measured?
sec06-F04-card.teaching_text: Forensic chemical testing measures exact bloodstream alcohol percentage rather than relying on how sober someone claims to feel.

sec06-F05-card.question_text: What factor primarily controls bloodstream alcohol, and how much do food or mixing drinks change it?
sec06-F05-card.teaching_text: Food only modestly slows uptake and drink mixing barely matters compared with total pure alcohol consumed.

sec06-F06-card.question_text: Does drink type or mixture change the BAC produced by consuming two ounces of pure alcohol in an hour?
sec06-F06-card.teaching_text: Switching between cocktails, wine, or beer never tricks your bloodstream when total pure alcohol in an hour matches.

sec06-F07-card.question_text: Roughly how much alcohol does a one-hundred-pound person need compared with a two-hundred-pound person for the same BAC?
sec06-F07-card.teaching_text: Smaller body weight concentrates alcohol in less body water, pushing lighter teens to legal thresholds twice as fast.

sec06-F08-card.question_text: Do two people always react identically to the same amount of alcohol and general BAC relationship?
sec06-F08-card.teaching_text: Personal tolerance, fatigue, and metabolism shift how impaired you feel even when general BAC charts predict trends.

sec06-F09-card.question_text: What BAC reading or drug finding counts as conclusive evidence of driving under the influence in Delaware?
sec06-F09-card.teaching_text: Testing at zero-point-zero-eight or having any illicit or recreational drug present proves DUI without needing erratic-driving video.

sec06-F10-card.question_text: Can a Delaware driver still be charged with DUI when their BAC is below zero point zero eight?
sec06-F10-card.teaching_text: Drivers wrongly treat zero-point-zero-eight as a safe zone, yet observable impairment below that mark still brings DUI charges.

sec06-F11-card.question_text: What happens to your driving privilege if you refuse chemical testing in Delaware?
sec06-F11-card.teaching_text: Saying no to breath, blood, or urine testing triggers its own harsh administrative revocation independent of criminal court.

sec06-F12-card.question_text: Does someone under twenty-one have to be driving a vehicle to lose their license for possessing or drinking alcohol?
sec06-F12-card.teaching_text: Holding or drinking alcohol at a party under twenty-one can revoke your Delaware license with keys in your pocket.

sec06-F13-card.question_text: What BAC threshold triggers license revocation for an underage driver in Delaware?
sec06-F13-card.teaching_text: Even trace alcohol from a single drink easily crosses zero-point-zero-two and costs an underage driver their license.

sec06-F14-card.question_text: When does crash risk begin rising as a driver's BAC increases?
sec06-F14-card.teaching_text: Waiting until you feel buzzed is dangerous because collision probability rises well before visible intoxication appears.

sec06-F15-card.question_text: How many minutes does alcohol take to reach the brain and impair judgment and driving skill?
sec06-F15-card.teaching_text: A driver who feels fine leaving a restaurant can have alcohol hit brain judgment centers mid-commute.

sec06-F16-card.question_text: Which four physical and mental driving faculties worsen as alcohol builds in the body?
sec06-F16-card.teaching_text: Slower reaction times combine with dimmer vision and overconfident choices right when emergency hazards demand sharpness.

sec06-F17-card.question_text: Which traffic perceptions and handling tasks become harder under the influence of alcohol?
sec06-F17-card.teaching_text: Misjudging oncoming speed or following gaps leads directly to left-turn and rear-end crashes.

sec06-F18-card.question_text: Why should drivers avoid getting behind the wheel after drinking at all?
sec06-F18-card.teaching_text: Subtle steering and braking delays begin with the very first drink, making complete abstinence before driving safest.

sec06-F19-card.question_text: Why is counting a specialty cocktail as just one drink misleading?
sec06-F19-card.teaching_text: Mixed specialty beverages often combine several shots of liquor in one glass, multiplying your actual BAC.

sec06-F20-card.question_text: What is the only way to sober up, and do coffee, fresh air, exercise, or cold showers speed it up?
sec06-F20-card.teaching_text: Coffee or a cold shower only creates a wide-awake impaired driver while liver metabolism works at a fixed pace.

sec06-F21-card.question_text: What two safe-ride options are recommended when planning a social outing involving alcohol?
sec06-F21-card.teaching_text: Locking in a non-drinking driver, bus, or cab before going out prevents impaired late-night rationalizations.

sec06-F22-card.question_text: What can eating food do to alcohol absorption, and what can it never prevent?
sec06-F22-card.teaching_text: A heavy meal delays peak absorption slightly, yet every ounce you drink still enters your bloodstream.

sec06-F23-card.question_text: What drinking-pace habit slows down alcohol's effects most effectively?
sec06-F23-card.teaching_text: Spacing drinks farther apart gives your body more time between servings instead of flooding your bloodstream rapidly.

sec06-F24-card.question_text: How severely can prescription and over-the-counter medications impair driving compared with alcohol?
sec06-F24-card.teaching_text: Drivers often underestimate pharmacy medications even though legal pills can degrade reaction times as badly as alcohol.

sec06-F25-card.question_text: What driving hazard can medicines for headaches, colds, allergies, or calming nerves trigger?
sec06-F25-card.teaching_text: Antihistamines and nerve-calming pills frequently induce sudden sleepiness that slows hazard recognition behind the wheel.

sec06-F26-card.question_text: What delayed problems can stimulants and diet pills cause after a brief boost in alertness?
sec06-F26-card.teaching_text: Relying on stimulants to stay awake backfires when rebound dizziness, blurred vision, and scattered focus hit mid-drive.

sec06-F27-card.question_text: What two steps should you take before driving on an unfamiliar medicine?
sec06-F27-card.teaching_text: Checking warning labels and consulting a clinician catches hidden drowsiness or vision side effects before you merge.

sec06-F28-card.question_text: Why must you never combine alcohol with other drugs before driving?
sec06-F28-card.teaching_text: Synergistic drug-and-alcohol reactions multiply sedation and coordination loss far beyond what either substance causes alone.

sec06-F29-card.question_text: What two specific driving problems are reported more often among marijuana users?
sec06-F29-card.teaching_text: Slower recovery from oncoming headlight glare makes night driving especially hazardous after cannabis use.

sec06-F30-card.question_text: What does performing any secondary task while driving add to?
sec06-F30-card.teaching_text: Your brain has finite attention bandwidth, so every extra task steals processing power from scanning traffic.

sec06-F31-card.question_text: How far does a vehicle going fifty-five miles per hour travel when you look away for three to four seconds?
sec06-F31-card.teaching_text: Glancing at a text for four seconds at highway speed is equivalent to driving a hundred yards blindfolded.

sec06-F32-card.question_text: How can eating, grooming, changing music, smoking, reading, or intense conversations affect driving?
sec06-F32-card.teaching_text: Non-phone habits like unwrapping food or heated cabin debates overwhelm attention just as dangerously as screens.

sec06-F33-card.question_text: What happens when drivers attend to kids or pets, reach for loose items, or use phones for texts, calls, or selfies?
sec06-F33-card.teaching_text: Reaching for a dropped item or snapping a selfie pulls eyes, hands, and mind off traffic simultaneously.

sec06-F34-card.question_text: Which adjustments and control checks belong before pulling away in an unfamiliar vehicle?
sec06-F34-card.teaching_text: Hunting for wiper or headlight switches mid-storm steals your eyes from traffic right when visibility drops.

sec06-F35-card.question_text: How do long-distance driving and fatigue affect awareness, reaction speed, and thinking?
sec06-F35-card.teaching_text: Exhausted drivers spot brake lights late and make sluggish steering decisions that mimic alcohol impairment.

sec06-F36-card.question_text: What causes the reduced surrounding awareness known as highway hypnosis?
sec06-F36-card.teaching_text: Steady tire hum and unchanging highway scenery can lull your brain into zoning out past hazards.

sec06-F37-card.question_text: What two actions are recommended when you start feeling tired behind the wheel?
sec06-F37-card.teaching_text: Rolling down windows or blasting music never fixes sleep debt, so pull over safely or switch drivers.

sec06-F38-card.question_text: Which physical, memory, and lane-keeping clues warn that drowsiness is overtaking your driving?
sec06-F38-card.teaching_text: Drifting across lane lines or forgetting the last few miles means microsleeps have already started.

sec06-F39-card.question_text: Is drinking alcohol behind the wheel on Delaware highways ever lawful?
sec06-F39-card.teaching_text: Sipping alcohol behind the wheel violates Delaware highway law immediately regardless of whether your BAC stays low.

sec06-F40-card.question_text: Which vehicles, locations, and forms of control fall under Delaware's DUI statute?
sec06-F40-card.teaching_text: Sitting in actual physical control of a car, moped, or off-highway vehicle on private land still triggers DUI.

sec06-F41-card.question_text: Does having a legal prescription or legal right to use alcohol or a drug excuse a DUI charge?
sec06-F41-card.teaching_text: Holding a valid doctor's prescription offers zero courtroom defense if that medication impairs your driving.

sec06-F42-card.question_text: What two separate categories of penalties can result from driving under alcohol or drug influence?
sec06-F42-card.teaching_text: A single DUI arrest launches parallel DMV license revocation proceedings alongside criminal court fines and jail.

sec06-F43-card.question_text: What happens to your Delaware driver license if you are convicted of DUI in another state?
sec06-F43-card.teaching_text: Interstate compact reporting brings out-of-state impaired-driving convictions straight back to revoke your home Delaware card.

sec06-F44-card.question_text: Which three chemical tests has a driver impliedly consented to upon arrest for impaired driving or physical control?
sec06-F44-card.teaching_text: Implied consent covers vehicles, mopeds, and off-highway vehicles alike once probable cause supports an impairment arrest.

sec06-F45-card.question_text: What may happen after an arrested driver refuses the chemical test designated by the officer?
sec06-F45-card.teaching_text: Refusing not only triggers administrative license loss but still may not stop lawful evidence collection.

sec06-F46-card.question_text: For how long can the DMV revoke a license for chemical-test refusal, and what sets the length?
sec06-F46-card.teaching_text: Prior DUI, probable-cause, or test-refusal history pushes a refusal revocation from one year up to two.

sec06-F47-card.question_text: How long must a Family Court revocation order last in a juvenile DUI case?
sec06-F47-card.teaching_text: A teen adjudicated for juvenile DUI loses driving privileges all the way through their twenty-first birthday.

sec06-F48-card.question_text: How long is a first-offense zero-tolerance revocation for driving or physical control under twenty-one after drinking?
sec06-F48-card.teaching_text: Underage drivers face zero tolerance, losing their license for two months on a first alcohol-driving violation.

sec06-F49-card.question_text: What revocation range applies to a repeat underage zero-tolerance violation?
sec06-F49-card.teaching_text: A second underage alcohol-driving violation triples the minimum revocation from two months to at least six.

sec06-F50-card.question_text: Outside narrow statutory exceptions, what is the first-offense fine for underage alcohol possession or consumption?
sec06-F50-card.teaching_text: That hundred-dollar civil penalty pairs with potential license revocation even if no vehicle was involved.

sec06-F51-card.question_text: What fine range applies to each subsequent non-exempt underage alcohol possession or consumption offense?
sec06-F51-card.teaching_text: Repeat underage drinking citations double the minimum fine and climb up to five hundred dollars.

sec06-F52-card.question_text: How are the first two underage possession-and-consumption offenses classified, and how does that affect certified criminal records?
sec06-F52-card.teaching_text: Treating the first two violations as civil keeps certified criminal history clean while still enforcing fines and revocation.

sec06-R01-card.question_text: Which two settings are excluded from the underage alcohol possession-and-consumption offense?
sec06-R01-card.teaching_text: Outside religious ceremonies or same-family supervision inside a relative's private residence, underage possession remains unlawful.

sec06-R02-card.question_text: What does an arresting DUI officer do with a Delaware driver's license, and what temporary document is issued?
sec06-R02-card.teaching_text: Delaware plastic cards are taken at arrest while out-of-state cards are not, starting a strict fifteen-day window.

sec06-R03-card.question_text: How long does a DUI-arrested driver have to request an administrative hearing before revocation takes effect?
sec06-R03-card.teaching_text: Missing that fifteen-day deadline forfeits your hearing right and triggers automatic license revocation on day sixteen.

sec06-R04-card.question_text: When can an eligible fifteen-day temporary license be extended after a DUI arrest?
sec06-R04-card.teaching_text: Timely filing for a DMV hearing keeps eligible temporary driving authority active until the hearing decision.

sec06-R05-card.question_text: What three questions are examined during an administrative DUI hearing?
sec06-R05-card.teaching_text: Hearing officers review stop grounds, proof of impaired control, or whether you refused testing after revocation warnings.

sec06-R06-card.question_text: How long is the revocation after an unfavorable administrative probable-cause ruling on a first offense?
sec06-R06-card.teaching_text: Notice that losing a probable-cause hearing brings three months on a first offense versus twelve for refusal.

sec06-R07-card.question_text: How long is the revocation after an unfavorable probable-cause hearing ruling for a second offense?
sec06-R07-card.teaching_text: A second unfavorable probable-cause ruling quadruples the administrative revocation from three months to a full year.

sec06-R08-card.question_text: What revocation length applies when an unfavorable probable-cause hearing ruling is a third or later offense?
sec06-R08-card.teaching_text: Repeat impairment arrests push administrative probable-cause revocations to a year and a half.

sec06-R09-card.question_text: How long is the administrative revocation for losing a chemical-refusal hearing on a first offense?
sec06-R09-card.teaching_text: Refusing the test quadruples first-offense administrative license loss from three probable-cause months to twelve.

sec06-R10-card.question_text: How long is the administrative revocation after an unfavorable chemical-refusal ruling on a second offense?
sec06-R10-card.teaching_text: Every chemical-refusal tier sits six to nine months harsher than the matching probable-cause hearing tier.

sec06-R11-card.question_text: What revocation length applies to an unfavorable chemical-refusal ruling on a third or later offense?
sec06-R11-card.teaching_text: A third-or-later chemical-refusal ruling hits the full two-year administrative revocation ceiling in Delaware.

sec06-R12-card.question_text: What four requirements must be met to reinstate after a probable-cause or chemical-refusal revocation?
sec06-R12-card.teaching_text: Finishing revocation months never restores privileges until rehabilitation, program fees, and the two-hundred-dollar DMV fee clear.

sec06-R13-card.question_text: Which three driver examinations may be required before reinstating after probable-cause or refusal action?
sec06-R13-card.teaching_text: Returning from an administrative DUI revocation can mean passing every licensing exam from scratch.

sec06-R14-card.question_text: How many months of license loss apply on a first DUI conviction involving drugs or BAC below zero point one five?
sec06-R14-card.teaching_text: Even the lowest first-offense DUI conviction bracket removes full driving privileges for twelve months.

sec06-R15-card.question_text: On a first DUI conviction, what license loss applies for a zero-point-one-five to zero-point-one-nine BAC?
sec06-R15-card.teaching_text: Crossing zero-point-one-five on a first DUI adds six extra months of license loss above the base year.

sec06-R16-card.question_text: How long is license loss on a first DUI conviction with BAC at least zero point two zero or test refusal?
sec06-R16-card.teaching_text: High-BAC readings of zero-point-two-zero or refusing testing double first-offense license loss to two full years.

sec06-R17-card.question_text: What fine range and maximum jail term appear in the court table for a first DUI offense?
sec06-R17-card.teaching_text: Judges can impose fines up to fifteen hundred dollars, up to a year of imprisonment, or both together.

sec06-R18-card.question_text: What restricted license option may someone entering First Offender Election instead of trial seek before revocation ends?
sec06-R18-card.teaching_text: Choosing First Offender Election lets qualifying first-timers drive approved interlock-equipped cars during revocation.

sec06-R19-card.question_text: When does IID application eligibility begin for FOE offenses dated February two, twenty fifteen or later?
sec06-R19-card.teaching_text: Post-2015 FOE participants avoid a multi-week waiting period once they satisfy every required application condition.

sec06-R20-card.question_text: What four items and record conditions are required on an FOE ignition-interlock license application?
sec06-R20-card.teaching_text: Out-of-state tags or separate active suspensions will block an FOE interlock application at the DMV counter.

sec06-R21-card.question_text: What happens once an FOE participant satisfies the IID application requirements?
sec06-R21-card.teaching_text: Never install an unapproved unit early without DMV authorization tying the device to your approved vehicles.

sec06-R22-card.question_text: How long must an FOE participant stay in the IID program, and what date starts that clock?
sec06-R22-card.teaching_text: Counting from arrest or court entry is a classic exam trap because the four months start on IID issuance.

sec06-R23-card.question_text: What must reach the DMV for FOE reinstatement and IID removal, and what exams might also apply?
sec06-R23-card.teaching_text: Never pull an interlock off early before the DMV receives treatment proof, two hundred dollars, and authorizes removal.

sec06-R24-card.question_text: What must an FOE participant without a vehicle in their name do if they choose not to get an IID license?
sec06-R24-card.teaching_text: Skipping the interlock track means zero driving for the entire revocation plus completing every reinstatement step.

sec06-R25-card.question_text: On a second DUI conviction, what license loss applies for drugs or BAC under zero-point-one-five?
sec06-R25-card.teaching_text: Every second-offense BAC bracket adds six more months of license loss than the matching first-offense bracket.

sec06-R26-card.question_text: On a second DUI conviction, what license loss applies for a zero-point-one-five to zero-point-one-nine BAC?
sec06-R26-card.teaching_text: A second DUI in the zero-point-one-five to zero-point-one-nine bracket removes your license for two full years.

sec06-R27-card.question_text: On a second DUI conviction, what license loss applies at zero-point-two-zero BAC or for refusal?
sec06-R27-card.teaching_text: Refusing testing or blowing zero-point-two-zero on a second DUI pushes license loss to two and a half years.

sec06-R28-card.question_text: What fine range and prison window apply in court for a second DUI offense?
sec06-R28-card.teaching_text: Unlike a first offense where jail is optional, a second DUI carries mandatory sixty-day-to-eighteen-month imprisonment.

sec06-R29-card.question_text: How can an eligible second-DUI offender have the minimum prison sentence suspended?
sec06-R29-card.teaching_text: Successfully finishing the Court of Common Pleas DUI Treatment Program gives judges authority to suspend minimum jail time.

sec06-R30-card.question_text: On a third DUI conviction, what license loss applies for drugs or BAC under zero-point-one-five?
sec06-R30-card.teaching_text: Notice the clean six-month step-up across first, second, and third offenses from twelve to eighteen to twenty-four months.

sec06-R31-card.question_text: On a third DUI conviction, what license loss applies for a zero-point-one-five to zero-point-one-nine BAC?
sec06-R31-card.teaching_text: Mid-range BAC on a third conviction carries thirty months of DMV license loss alongside felony court exposure.

sec06-R32-card.question_text: On a third DUI conviction, what license loss applies at zero-point-two-zero BAC or for refusal?
sec06-R32-card.teaching_text: High BAC or test refusal on a third offense locks in three full years of license loss.

sec06-R33-card.question_text: How is a third DUI committed at any time after two prior offenses classified in Delaware?
sec06-R33-card.teaching_text: There is no expiration lookback here because any third lifetime DUI elevates the charge to a felony.

sec06-R34-card.question_text: What maximum court fine is listed for a third DUI offense in Delaware?
sec06-R34-card.teaching_text: Crossing into felony DUI doubles the maximum court fine from twenty-five hundred to five thousand dollars.

sec06-R35-card.question_text: What imprisonment range is listed in the court table for a third DUI offense?
sec06-R35-card.teaching_text: A third DUI moves sentencing out of county-jail day counts into a one-to-two-year prison range.

sec06-R36-card.question_text: What felony classification applies to a fourth DUI committed at any time after three prior offenses?
sec06-R36-card.teaching_text: Regardless of how many years separate priors, a fourth DUI jumps from Class G to Class E felony.

sec06-R37-card.question_text: How many months of license loss carry across every BAC bracket on a fourth DUI conviction?
sec06-R37-card.teaching_text: Starting at the fourth offense, BAC brackets disappear and every conviction brings a flat five-year license loss.

sec06-R38-card.question_text: What maximum fine appears in the court table for a fourth DUI offense?
sec06-R38-card.teaching_text: Fourth-offense financial penalties climb to seven thousand dollars before counting mandatory treatment and interlock expenses.

sec06-R39-card.question_text: What prison range applies in the court table for a fourth DUI offense?
sec06-R39-card.teaching_text: A fourth DUI doubles the minimum prison term over a third offense and reaches up to five years.

sec06-R40-card.question_text: How is a fifth DUI offense classified under Delaware law?
sec06-R40-card.teaching_text: Fourth and fifth DUI convictions share the Class E felony label while court fines and minimum prison rise.

sec06-R41-card.question_text: How many months of license loss apply to every fifth-DUI conviction?
sec06-R41-card.teaching_text: Every felony DUI from the fourth offense onward carries the same sixty-month DMV license-loss period.

sec06-R42-card.question_text: What is the maximum court fine listed for a fifth DUI offense?
sec06-R42-card.teaching_text: At a fifth conviction, the maximum court fine hits five figures at ten thousand dollars.

sec06-R43-card.question_text: What imprisonment range is assigned to a fifth DUI offense in the court table?
sec06-R43-card.teaching_text: Compared with a fourth offense, a fifth DUI raises the floor to three mandatory years in prison.

sec06-R44-card.question_text: What felony classification applies to a sixth DUI offense in Delaware?
sec06-R44-card.teaching_text: Stepping from a fifth to a sixth DUI upgrades the crime from Class E to a Class D felony.

sec06-R45-card.question_text: How many months of license loss does the DMV table assign to every sixth-DUI conviction?
sec06-R45-card.teaching_text: Just like fourth and fifth convictions, a sixth DUI carries sixty months of DMV license loss.

sec06-R46-card.question_text: What maximum fine does the court table list for a sixth DUI offense?
sec06-R46-card.teaching_text: Fifth and sixth DUI offenses share the ten-thousand-dollar fine ceiling while sixth-offense prison exposure jumps.

sec06-R47-card.question_text: What imprisonment range appears in the court table for a sixth DUI offense?
sec06-R47-card.teaching_text: A sixth DUI pushes the prison floor to four years and raises the maximum term to eight.

sec06-R48-card.question_text: How is a seventh or subsequent DUI offense classified in Delaware?
sec06-R48-card.teaching_text: Seventh-or-later offenses reach the severest DUI felony grade in the table as a Class C felony.

sec06-R49-card.question_text: How many months of license loss apply to every seventh-or-later DUI conviction?
sec06-R49-card.teaching_text: Every conviction from the fourth through seventh-or-later offense carries sixty months of DMV license loss.

sec06-R50-card.question_text: What maximum court fine applies to a seventh or later DUI offense?
sec06-R50-card.teaching_text: Seventh-or-later DUI convictions carry the highest fine ceiling in the court chart at fifteen thousand dollars.

sec06-R51-card.question_text: What imprisonment window does the court table list for a seventh or later DUI offense?
sec06-R51-card.teaching_text: Repeat impaired driving at the seventh-offense mark carries five mandatory years and up to fifteen years incarcerated.

sec06-R52-card.question_text: When does an IID license permit driving an ignition-interlock-equipped vehicle?
sec06-R52-card.teaching_text: Simply bolting an interlock into a car gives zero authority to drive until every DMV qualification clears.

sec06-R53-card.question_text: How soon may First Offender Election participants apply for an IID license upon entering the program?
sec06-R53-card.teaching_text: Unlike convicted non-FOE offenders who sit out mandatory revocation days first, qualified FOE enrollees can apply right away.

sec06-R54-card.question_text: How many days of minimum revocation apply before IID application eligibility on a non-FOE first conviction?
sec06-R54-card.teaching_text: Going to conviction outside FOE requires serving thirty to forty-five revocation days depending on BAC before applying.

sec06-R55-card.question_text: What minimum revocation period must pass before IID application eligibility on a second DUI conviction?
sec06-R55-card.teaching_text: Second-time DUI offenders must sit out two full months off the road before seeking interlock privileges.

sec06-R56-card.question_text: What minimum revocation period precedes IID application eligibility on a third DUI conviction?
sec06-R56-card.teaching_text: Notice the thirty-day progression on repeat convictions, stepping from sixty days on second to ninety on third.

sec06-R57-card.question_text: How long is the minimum revocation before IID application eligibility on a fourth or later DUI conviction?
sec06-R57-card.teaching_text: At four or more convictions, the pre-application wait doubles from ninety days to half a year.

sec06-R58-card.question_text: Which license classes and crash outcomes are barred from using a Delaware IID license?
sec06-R58-card.teaching_text: Commercial vehicles, peripheral endorsements, and crashes involving death or serious injury never qualify for interlock driving.

sec06-R59-card.question_text: How do unrelated suspensions, revocations, disqualifications, or denials affect IID license issuance?
sec06-R59-card.teaching_text: An unpaid support suspension or point revocation will stop IID issuance even after your DUI wait ends.

sec06-R60-card.question_text: What license status at offense time, enrollment step, and surrender action are required for a general IID application?
sec06-R60-card.teaching_text: Unlicensed drivers at the time of their DUI cannot later convert that revocation into an IID license.

sec06-R61-card.question_text: What insurance documentation must an IID applicant provide?
sec06-R61-card.teaching_text: Every car scheduled for interlock installation needs verified active liability coverage before the DMV approves setup.

sec06-R62-card.question_text: Must an IID participant install devices and show Delaware registration on vehicles they drive even if owned by someone else?
sec06-R62-card.teaching_text: Borrowing a family member's or employer's car without an installed interlock violates your restricted license immediately.

sec06-R63-card.question_text: Which three driver exams might the DMV require prior to issuing an IID license?
sec06-R63-card.teaching_text: Be ready for the DMV to check eye, written-law, and behind-the-wheel competence before granting limited IID privileges.

sec06-R64-card.question_text: What two steps happen with the vendor before the DMV issues limited driving privileges?
sec06-R64-card.teaching_text: Limited driving privileges only activate after an approved vendor installs the unit and the DMV verifies completion.

sec06-R65-card.question_text: Who pays IID program costs, and from what date is required IID duration measured?
sec06-R65-card.teaching_text: Delaying your IID application never shortens interlock time because duration starts on IID issuance, not revocation end.

sec06-R66-card.question_text: How many months does the IID duration table require for an FOE participant?
sec06-R66-card.teaching_text: FOE offers the shortest interlock commitment in Delaware's table at four months from IID license issuance.

sec06-R67-card.question_text: How many months of IID use are required for a non-FOE first DUI conviction?
sec06-R67-card.teaching_text: Outside FOE, a first DUI conviction requires at least a full year and up to twenty-three interlock months.

sec06-R68-card.question_text: What IID duration range applies to a second DUI conviction depending on BAC?
sec06-R68-card.teaching_text: Higher BAC readings on a second conviction push required interlock time past two full years.

sec06-R69-card.question_text: What IID duration range applies to a third DUI conviction depending on BAC?
sec06-R69-card.teaching_text: After serving the ninety-day minimum wait, a third offender spends twenty-one to thirty-three months on interlock.

sec06-R70-card.question_text: At least how many months of IID use does the table require for a fourth or later conviction?
sec06-R70-card.teaching_text: Six months of initial revocation plus fifty-four interlock months covers the full sixty-month felony withdrawal span.

sec06-R71-card.question_text: What two actions can the DMV take if an IID participant fails to comply with program rules?
sec06-R71-card.teaching_text: Missed calibrations, failed breath tests, or tampering can tack on extra months or kick you out completely.

sec06-R72-card.question_text: What rules govern a DUI offender who skips applying for the ignition-interlock program?
sec06-R72-card.teaching_text: Without an IID license, zero legal driving is allowed until the entire revocation period expires.

sec14-F01-card.question_text: What two things should you communicate to surrounding road users so nobody gets caught off guard?
sec14-F01-card.teaching_text: Surprised drivers brake late or swerve abruptly whenever nearby vehicles move without clear notice.

sec14-F02-card.question_text: In which three weather conditions do headlights help other motorists spot your vehicle?
sec14-F02-card.teaching_text: Precipitation and mist swallow unlit cars long before your own daytime sight seems affected.

sec14-F03-card.question_text: What must you do with your headlights whenever your windshield wipers are running?
sec14-F03-card.teaching_text: Delaware links wipers and headlights so every car stays illuminated during active rain or snow.

sec14-F04-card.question_text: Why should you switch headlights on right as evening darkness begins?
sec14-F04-card.teaching_text: Twilight shadows hide dark-colored vehicles long before streetlights or stars fully brighten.

sec14-F05-card.question_text: Why shouldn't you drive using only parking lamps when conditions call for lights?
sec14-F05-card.teaching_text: Dim parking bulbs mark stationary cars and can trick oncoming traffic into misjudging your motion.

sec14-F06-card.question_text: Why should you turn headlights on when driving away from a low rising or setting sun?
sec14-F06-card.teaching_text: With bright sun behind your back, oncoming drivers stare straight into glare hiding your unlit silhouette.

sec14-F07-card.question_text: What is the safety purpose of sounding your vehicle's horn?
sec14-F07-card.teaching_text: A timely audible alert snaps distracted eyes back onto traffic before bumpers meet.

sec14-F08-card.question_text: When is a light tap on the horn appropriate?
sec14-F08-card.teaching_text: A brief polite beep warns a driver drifting toward your lane without startling surrounding cars.

sec14-F09-card.question_text: Which three immediate emergencies justify a sharp horn warning?
sec14-F09-card.teaching_text: Imminent danger to children, older walkers, or colliding vehicles calls for an unmistakable sharp blast.

sec14-F10-card.question_text: Which three everyday temptations are improper reasons to sound your horn?
sec14-F10-card.teaching_text: Honking out of impatience or waving hello distracts nearby traffic and dilutes genuine hazard alerts.

sec14-F11-card.question_text: How must you handle your horn around a blind pedestrian?
sec14-F11-card.teaching_text: A sudden horn blast disorients someone navigating by traffic sound and gives zero directional clarity.

sec14-F12-card.question_text: What is a key visibility priority if your vehicle breaks down along a highway?
sec14-F12-card.teaching_text: Fast highway drivers assume stopped cars are moving unless bright visual cues warn them early.

sec14-F13-card.question_text: How should you summon help when communication gear or posted numbers are available during a breakdown?
sec14-F13-card.teaching_text: Using posted highway assistance numbers dispatches patrols quickly so you spend less time exposed roadside.

sec14-F14-card.question_text: Where should you stop and what lights should you activate when mechanical trouble strikes?
sec14-F14-card.teaching_text: Clearing live travel lanes and switching on four-way flashers shields a crippled car from rear impacts.

sec14-F15-card.question_text: If you cannot get off the roadway during a breakdown, where should you avoid stopping?
sec14-F15-card.teaching_text: Halting just beyond a blind crest or bend hides your bumper until fast traffic rounds the corner.

sec14-F16-card.question_text: How do emergency warning devices placed behind a disabled vehicle help approaching traffic?
sec14-F16-card.teaching_text: Advance flares or reflective triangles alert highway drivers early enough to merge over smoothly.

sec14-F17-card.question_text: How can you warn approaching drivers if your vehicle lacks emergency warning devices?
sec14-F17-card.teaching_text: Standing well off the asphalt while waving a visible white cloth alerts oncoming drivers without entering lanes.

sec14-F18-card.question_text: When must you refuse to stand near your vehicle or change a flat tire?
sec14-F18-card.teaching_text: Kneeling beside a jack inside a live traffic lane exposes you directly to distracted passing drivers.

sec14-F19-card.question_text: Which simple visual cues on a parked vehicle signal a roadside emergency?
sec14-F19-card.teaching_text: Propping the hood open or tying white fabric onto a mirror or handle signals trouble universally.

sec14-F20-card.question_text: Why shouldn't you cruise beside and slightly behind another vehicle?
sec14-F20-card.teaching_text: Hovering off another car's rear fender places your nose right where side mirrors often miss.

sec14-F21-card.question_text: How should you move through another driver's blind spot while passing?
sec14-F21-card.teaching_text: Completing passes briskly minimizes the seconds you spend invisible beside another driver's quarter panel.

sec14-F22-card.question_text: Why must you avoid pacing alongside a bus or large truck?
sec14-F22-card.teaching_text: Long commercial sides hide entire sedans from cab mirrors if the operator needs to merge.

sec14-F23-card.question_text: Why must you warn drivers behind you before slowing down or changing direction?
sec14-F23-card.teaching_text: Early turn signals and brake taps prevent panic stops and chain-reaction rear impacts.

sec14-F24-card.question_text: Should you still signal turns, lane changes, merges, and parking when nobody looks nearby?
sec14-F24-card.teaching_text: The pedestrian, cyclist, or hidden car you missed is the exact road user who needs your blinker most.

sec14-F25-card.question_text: What minimum time cue and legal turn-distance requirement does Delaware pair for signaling?
sec14-F25-card.teaching_text: Remembering three seconds before general moves and three hundred feet before turns keeps every signal lawful.

sec14-F26-card.question_text: How can signaling before an intervening driveway or waiting vehicle create a hazard?
sec14-F26-card.teaching_text: A driver waiting at a side driveway may pull right out ahead of you assuming you plan to turn early.

sec14-F27-card.question_text: What should you verify right after completing a lane change or gentle turn?
sec14-F27-card.teaching_text: Slight steering angles often fail to trip the auto-cancel cam, leaving a false turn signal blinking.

sec14-F28-card.question_text: How should you use your brake pedal when slowing in an unexpected spot?
sec14-F28-card.teaching_text: Flashing your brake lamps three or four times catches trailing eyes far faster than one steady glow.

sec14-F29-card.question_text: Which three roadway situations call for extra warning before you slow down?
sec14-F29-card.teaching_text: Trailing traffic cannot guess you are turning without a turn pocket, parking near corners, or dodging hidden debris.
sec14-F29-card.must_match_memory_hook: No exit-lane, corner park, hidden block

sec14-F30-card.question_text: What signal methods and minimum continuous distance apply before making a turn in Delaware?
sec14-F30-card.teaching_text: Keeping a hand signal, electric blinker, or both active for three hundred continuous feet satisfies Delaware law.

sec14-F31-card.question_text: How should you adjust signaling distance at high speeds such as expressway lane changes?
sec14-F31-card.teaching_text: Freeway vehicles cover three hundred feet in roughly three seconds, demanding earlier blinkers before shifting lanes.

sec14-R01-card.question_text: Which factors govern safe speed selection, and why do higher speeds demand bigger margins?
sec14-R01-card.teaching_text: Faster travel multiplies stopping and steering room, so sightlines, traffic, and road grip set safe pace.

sec14-R02-card.question_text: At which three roadway features should you drop speed ahead of time?
sec14-R02-card.teaching_text: Carrying highway pace into tight bends, slick patches, or standing water breaks tire traction fast.

sec14-R03-card.question_text: Which two paired elements determine how well your tires grip the road?
sec14-R03-card.teaching_text: Even brand-new tread slides on glare ice, while bald rubber slips on mildly damp asphalt.

sec14-R04-card.question_text: Where should you look to find the right inflation pressure for maintaining your tires?
sec14-R04-card.teaching_text: Following vehicle manufacturer specs keeps the full tire footprint planted evenly for braking and cornering.

sec14-R05-card.question_text: Why must you drop speed when moving onto gravel or dirt roads?
sec14-R05-card.teaching_text: Rolling stones and loose dirt act like tiny ball bearings under tires during turns or stops.

sec14-R06-card.question_text: When should you finish slowing for a curve so you avoid skidding?
sec14-R06-card.teaching_text: Hitting the brakes mid-bend overloads front tires already working hard to hold your cornering line.

sec14-R07-card.question_text: When should you begin reducing speed as rain, sleet, or snow starts falling?
sec14-R07-card.teaching_text: Early raindrops lift road oil onto wet film while sleet and snow chill tire grip immediately.

sec14-R08-card.question_text: By about how much does the Delaware handbook advise reducing speed on wet pavement?
sec14-R08-card.teaching_text: Trimming roughly ten miles per hour on wet asphalt helps tire grooves channel water without floating.

sec14-R09-card.question_text: How much should you reduce your speed when driving on packed snow?
sec14-R09-card.teaching_text: Packed snow slashes friction so normal dry-road speeds easily double or triple your stopping run.

sec14-R10-card.question_text: What traction gear does the handbook recommend for snow-covered roads, and what pace for ice?
sec14-R10-card.teaching_text: Deep snow benefits from winter tread or chains, while glare ice demands barely-moving crawl speed.

sec14-R11-card.question_text: What precaution applies to icy trips and using studded snow tires?
sec14-R11-card.teaching_text: Staying off ice beats any tire, and metal studs face seasonal or local road restrictions.

sec14-R12-card.question_text: How do shaded roadway sections behave on cold, wet days?
sec14-R12-card.teaching_text: Trees and buildings block warming sunlight, leaving hidden ice bands across otherwise wet blacktop.

sec14-R13-card.question_text: Why do bridges and overpasses freeze while approaching roadways remain wet?
sec14-R13-card.teaching_text: Exposed spans lose heat from both top and bottom, icing up well before insulated earthbound pavement.

sec14-R14-card.question_text: Why is ice near thirty-two degrees more treacherous than deep-freeze ice?
sec14-R14-card.teaching_text: A thin skim of water atop freezing-point ice cuts tire grip to nearly half of subzero ice.

sec14-R15-card.question_text: What happens during hydroplaning, and what simple habit helps prevent it?
sec14-R15-card.teaching_text: Once water wedges beneath spinning tread, steering and braking vanish until speed drops.

sec14-R16-card.question_text: How do bald or badly worn tires change wet-road hydroplaning risk?
sec14-R16-card.teaching_text: Shallow grooves cannot pump standing rainwater clear, letting tires break loose even at modest speeds.

sec14-R17-card.question_text: What should your right foot do if your tires start losing grip on wet pavement?
sec14-R17-card.teaching_text: Gentle throttle lift lets spinning or planing tires slow down and sink back onto solid asphalt.

sec14-R18-card.question_text: How should you handle steering and braking while road grip is lost?
sec14-R18-card.teaching_text: Turning or braking without traction triggers spins, so steer straight or make only slow emergency turns.

sec14-R19-card.question_text: What safety drawback comes from repeatedly speeding past surrounding traffic?
sec14-R19-card.teaching_text: Every extra lane shift and close overtake adds another blind-spot conflict for minimal time saved.

sec14-R20-card.question_text: What should a driver moving much slower than normal traffic do when vehicles stack up behind?
sec14-R20-card.teaching_text: Clearing accumulated traffic at a safe turnout prevents frustrated drivers from attempting risky passes.

sec14-R21-card.question_text: How should you use a highway entrance ramp before merging into main lanes?
sec14-R21-card.teaching_text: Matching freeway pace on the ramp lets you slip into gaps smoothly without forcing hard braking.

sec14-R22-card.question_text: Why shouldn't you roll to the tip of an entrance ramp and stop, and what should you do instead?
sec14-R22-card.teaching_text: Stopping at the ramp nose leaves zero runway to build highway speed before entering fast lanes.

sec14-R23-card.question_text: When should you begin slowing down for a highway exit ramp?
sec14-R23-card.teaching_text: Braking early in fast through lanes invites high-speed rear-end crashes behind your bumper.

sec14-R24-card.question_text: How should you turn off a fast two-lane highway when cars follow behind without a turn lane?
sec14-R24-card.teaching_text: Early turn blinkers and brake-light flashes prepare trailing traffic before you shed highway speed.

sec14-R25-card.question_text: Why is spotting slow-moving vehicles far ahead important?
sec14-R25-card.teaching_text: Recognizing closing speed early avoids last-second swerves or panic braking behind tractors and trucks.
